intros.opening_hook: A strong opener shows its first visible change by frame 2-6 at 60 fps, or after one deliberate empty beat of 20-26 f that turns the first event into a hard cut; it never fades up from black or starts on a title card. The hook becomes readable information within about 40-70 f (a metric settled at 41 f, a seven-word line done at about 70 f), then passes its energy on by cutting at peak speed: E.in into the cut, with the next shot starting at that velocity. Brand is either held back (a number or a question first, the mark at most a corner tag until about 60% of the runtime) or shown as the mark alone, already moving; the full lockup is saved for the end. The sound for the first ~2 s stays sparse, about 14 dB under the body with no sub, and the drop lands on the first hard cut: kick on the cut frame, sub 8-12 f before it. Readable type moves at no more than 20 px/f (letters travel faded and resolve as the move slows), edges move at no more than 60-80 px/f with master motion blur above 12 px/f, and every hold stays alive with a 0.3-0.5 px/f drift or a 0.04-0.07 %/f breath.
intros.transition: A transition is a designed handoff, not a cut between unrelated pictures. Something always crosses the seam: a velocity, a shape held within ±20-30 px of the same screen point, a dot, a line or a stage colour. The default that carries most edits is the velocity handoff. The outgoing move speeds up about ×1.13-1.2 per frame over its last 16-24 f, the cut lands on its fastest frame at 25-40 px/f, and the incoming shot opens at that speed or faster and slows about ×0.92-0.94 per frame to rest in 45-90 f. A scale jump of 1.3-2.5x (8-9x for a frame-filling macro of a related mark) is invisible when the scale velocity matches in log space, about −8% per frame on both sides of the cut. One-take seams (morphs, irises, portals, carets) run 20-90 f and keep every element edge under about 80 px/f, and only flat mask edges may move faster. Polarity flips, where mean luma jumps by 150 or more of 255, are the loudest punctuation: put them on downbeats, once or twice per film. Blending appears only as 1-2 ghost frames at a motion peak, never as a crossfade seam.
intros.camera: The camera is one transform on one world container (src/lib/camera.ts). A shot frames a world point at a screen point at scale k, and lc() blends shots with k in log space, so a zoom keeps an even perceived speed and the subject travels a straight line. What makes camera work feel expensive is the speed profile more than the path. Moves arrive fast and brake (E.out, E.cam), cruise at 3 px/f or less under readable copy, and leave by accelerating over the last 18-24 f into a cut on the fastest frame, ending at 13-47 px/f, and the incoming shot is already moving when it opens. Hero moves are 2-3x pushes over 60-67 f on E.smooth, peaking around 4-5% scale per frame, with the caption starting in the last 25% of the move so the text and the settle land together. No hold is ever dead: a 0.04-0.07%/f creep or a 0.3-1.5 px/f drift runs under every read longer than about 30 f. Keep camera speed under 60-80 px/f at the frame edge, render anything above 12 px/f with the motion-blur pass (--blur), keep roll under 11 deg and give each act one rotation axis.
intros.typography_motion: Measured type arrives on expo-out moves that cover 30-45% of their travel on the first frame and settle in 12-24 f at 60 fps, staggered 4-10 f per word (20-24 f for a calm one-word-per-beat read). What matters most is the readable moment: a word is either legible from its first frame (40% strength, rising at most 0.6 em at about 14 px/f) or it flies faded and streaked and resolves only once it slows below 20 px/f, and it always lands sharp, with any blur gone by 60% of the move. Colour carries recency: the newest glyph or word arrives in the one accent and relaxes to ink over 12-24 f. Lines never freeze and never jump: layouts are pre-solved or re-centred on a critically damped spring, a landed line tightens 2-3% or drifts 0.3-0.5 px/f, and a hold swells about 6% on an ease-in into the cut. Typing is time-boxed (any length done in about 68 f, half of it visible within 6 f), and the film's one discrete trick (a step edit, a scramble, a letter morph) acts out the copy instead of decorating it.
intros.ui_choreography: UI choreography is layout logic in motion: every rect is a function of the frame and the product's state, siblings reflow from computed positions instead of crossfading, and a container is on screen before its contents, which start once their slot is about 60% open. Entrances decay with no overshoot (a 200 px window rise on E.out covers about half its travel in the first 6 f and settles in 50 f) and exits accelerate, handing over to the next panel or the cut on their fastest frame with at most a 4 f gap. Size every move from peak speed = distance x the token's peak slope / frames (E.out 6.2 on its first frame, E.inOut 7.7, E.contact 4.4 on its last, E.whip 3.8, E.rest 3.5, E.glide 3.0, E.smooth 2.9, E.ui 2.7, E.dolly 1.5), so UI text stays at or under 20 px/f and nothing passes about 70 px/f; scale spawns and collapses with lmix so a small surface does not explode on its first frame. Cadence carries meaning: 4-6 f per row reads as data streaming in, 5 f per dealt card as tactile, a 14 f metronome of inserts as abundance, and uneven gaps such as 4, 15 and 18 f as a person deciding. The strongest moves make one motion do two jobs, an incoming panel's edge pushing its neighbour or a hero holding its exact screen position while the world changes around it, so the edit happens inside the product instead of at a cut.
intros.data_and_numbers: Numbers are proof, so they must read at a glance and stay true on any paused frame: tabular figures, a fixed digit count, and every shown value computed from fd(frame) so no motion-blur sub-sample shows two values. Hero counts are short, 28-46 f, starting from a credible 85-90% of the target on a quad-out (E.type) so the last unit lands in the final ~6 f instead of stalling; ambient UI counters may run 36-104 f. Charts draw in 24-96 f, bars grow 12-20 f each at 1.6-5 f staggers with any group landing within 30 f, and every bar tip, scan edge or line head stays at or under about 60-70 px/f at 1080p. A figure starts changing on the frame its cause lands (a press, a landing, a tab; effects follow the interaction by 2 f) and then holds at least 36 f plus 6 f per word of its label under a 2-3% breath. The one accent marks the hero series or the chosen item while comparison data stays grey, and two numbers are never crossfaded in place: cut them, count them or roll them.
intros.product_demo: A product shot depends on cause and effect: every action has a visible cause, the state changes on the cause frame itself (a 1 f swap, never a crossfade), and the result holds at least 36 f before the camera leaves. Give small UI hero weight through scale contrast, not length: alternate a wide with a 2-5x macro of the exact control, or open on the value moment at 1.6-2.2x and pull back to context over about 56 f, landing the next UI event within 2 f of the settle. Product arrivals are real motion. A device or window enters already moving (about 20 px/f on its first frame, settled by 44 f on E.out), and scrolls, sheets and widening bars peak at 35-60 px/f under the motion-blur pass. Holds stay alive with a 2-4% breath push instead of a dead lock. A person types at 30 cps. A fast product types at 50-72 cps, or to a fixed 68 f time box, with the newest characters arriving in the accent. Wherever possible let the product's own behaviour do the editing (a headline that grows into the input bar, an element that stays put while the page rebuilds around it, a window that recedes to its corner), so every transition also shows a feature.
intros.logo_and_end_card: The end card is the film's poster. The lockup appears once, sized at 28-45% of frame width, resolves within about 36-80 f, then holds 90-120 f (1.5-2.0 s, never past ~150 f) while it keeps building: a 10-20% push on E.dolly and tracking that tightens 0.03-0.06 em over ~46 f. Anything static past 48 f reads as a stalled player. The strongest endings come out of the story instead of starting a new logo animation: the last object lands on the mark's exact position and size, or the product clears the stage to uncover it, or the opening's mechanic returns carrying the name. Scale moves run in log space (lmix). Collapses from 9-12x settle in 36-66 f, and the fastest frames are flat fill, low contrast or motion-blurred. The name follows the mark at 55-60% of its slide, with letters 2-3.5 f apart and readable type never faster than 20 px/f. Sound carries half the weight: cut the music dead on the end-card frame, leave ~36 f of near-silence, put one hit on the frame the name resolves, and let its tail decay to digital zero inside a tail of at least 60 f. The last frame must show the mark plus the name, with at most one CTA at 44-56 px that stays readable for at least 1.7 s, and it never fades to black.
intros.color_and_light: Colour carries meaning, so ration it. Keep one accent with one job. It should cover roughly 0.05-6% of frame pixels on average (peaking near 12%) on a stage that fills 85-90% of the frame, and it should change on cut or impact frames, never through slow fades. Brightness is the strongest lever here: give every shot a planned mean luma, spend polarity flips of 160-240 levels on downbeats and act changes, and use at most one inverted card (about 60 f) in a dark film. Light moves are short and asymmetric: accent floods rise in 10-12 f and release over 20-26 f, sheens cross in about 36 f, and washes rise over about 40 f and recede over about 90 f. Stages never freeze: breathe them ±15% luma on a period of about 160 f, or drift them under 1 px/f. Build every gradient from tonal steps of one hue mixed in OKLab with mixColor, on normal blend, and let a hard edge or a one-frame white flash do the work a glow would.
intros.texture_and_finish: Texture and finish decide whether a film built from code reads as photographed or as a slideshow, and almost all of it works at the edge of perception: grain at a sigma of 1-2 code levels (a 1.5-2% layer), dot fields about 4% off their ground, photo plates graded to 5-8% mean luma, gobo shadows drifting under 0.5 px/f. Speed is finished in the render, not faked per layer: anything over 12 px/f gets the 240-degree float-accumulated blur pass, holds sit under 2 px/f so they render pin-sharp, and no element passes about 70-80 px/f. Every soft ramp ships as a dithered PNG, because a CSS gradient spanning fewer than about 30 code values bands, and every texture that animates is keyed to fd(frame) so the motion-blur sub-samples agree. Each texture must name its job (context, material, concealment, a hit) and keep one strength for the whole film. One signature surface move (a 34 f scanline transmutation, a ring field, a locked mosaic) is plenty for a film.
intros.layout_and_composition: In motion, layout means two things: where the eye lands, and how space gets made when something new arrives. The default is one subject per frame. That is a UI card at 72-92% of frame width or one line of type no wider than 80%, with captured UI shown at about 2x so body text is at least 27 px at 1080p, and everything that is not the hero dimmed to 0.6-0.7 brightness or defocused. When something enters, the layout makes room physically rather than overlaying it: neighbours move 0.43x the newcomer's travel and start up to 28 f early, and centred lines re-centre on a critically damped spring (20-45 px over 16-38 f) and then keep a 0.4-1.5 px/f drift so type never freezes. Captions go in the space the subject leaves: a 25-30% band, at most 24% of the frame width, inset 8-10% from the edge, starting in the last 25% of the move. To show breadth, use flush cells with no gutters on one shared stage, looping on coprime periods so a change lands somewhere about every 20 f. Any mark inside a sentence sits on the baseline at cap height, in a reserved slot.
intros.pacing_structure: Pacing is the shape of speed over time, and the strongest films control it at three scales. Per shot the shape is a U: arrive on E.out over 20-50 f, keep living through the hold at 0.3-1 px/f (no near-dead run longer than about 22 f), then accelerate over the last 18-24 f so the cut lands on the fastest frame at 17-38 px/f and the next shot opens already moving. Stillness is spent like money. One near-still hold of 60-90 f on the key claim, or a 12-15 f freeze on true silence before the lockup, reads as intent only because everything else moves. Per sequence, repetition teaches the viewer: a fixed 180 f ask beat with answers of varying length, a second instance at 0.6x length, phrase chunks landing one per beat. Per film, acts sit on the bar grid (a 30-60 s launch splits roughly 19/14/58/9%), stage polarity flips 3-5 times, and the score's arrangement follows the acts, with 12-24 f music holes before key statements and every slam within ±1 f of a picture event.
intros.micro_interaction: A micro-interaction is the visible cause of a cut. The response starts on the press frame, never a beat later, and the result holds at least 36 f before the camera moves on. A press works as a light envelope, not a bounce: an accelerating attack of 8-12 f, a one-frame peak and a release about twice as long (tau about 8 f), with no scale overshoot, because spring overshoot is kept for true landings. Small elements get weight by deforming with speed. A tab pill whose leading edge arrives in 12 f and trailing edge in 20 f stretches to about 1.9x its width mid-travel, and a moving dot stretches to its rest length plus about 4-5 f of travel. A cursor arrives 6-12 f before it acts and the target shows its hover state about 4 f after arrival; the press goes down in 4 f and recoils in 8 f, with at most one click per 30 f at uneven gaps such as 4, 15 and 18 f. Keep sound sparse: about 6-8 dry ticks in 45 s, each on the frame its element reaches 50% opacity and 12-18 dB under the landing hit, stepping up about 3 dB per action only across a counted run.
intros.depth_and_3d: Depth looks expensive only when it is physical and used sparingly. Use one rotation axis per act and perspective of 1800-2600 px for UI planes (about 3-4x the object's width for a small icon or coin), and tilt live components that have their own shadow and ground, never tilted screenshots. Most moves here are short and offset, not simultaneous: flips run 10-12 f, a tilt resolves over 20 f starting 6 f before the position settles, an unfold takes 24 f, and the state change lands on the edge-on or peak-tilt frame. Long moves (de-skews of 81 f, dollies of 60-68 f) ride E.cam or E.rest so they start gently and settle slowly. Keep speed honest: E.out puts about 5.5x its mean speed into the first frame (E.in into the last), so cap travel to keep peaks near 70 px/f and let the master's sub-frame blur carry anything over 12 px/f. Chromium decides the finish: keep roll outside the tilt and at most 11 deg, sort layers by z yourself (overflow, opacity and filters flatten preserve-3d), lay text out at shot scale with CSS zoom, and rack depth of field with RackFocus copies, never an animated filter blur.

techniques.name: Four live cells from frame 2
techniques.summary: There is no title. The film opens on a flush 2x2 grid where every cell is already mid-action (a line assembling, a counter ticking, an object orbiting, a pin dropping), so from its first frames the frame reads as one living system.
techniques.recipe: Root AbsoluteFill with a CSS grid (grid-template 1fr 1fr / 1fr 1fr, gap 0); every cell is overflow:hidden on the same stage colour (C.ink), so the seams disappear, with its content on the cell's own optical centre at 50-90% of the cell's width. Render each cell's scene at full 1920x1080 inside a wrapper with scale(0.5) and transformOrigin '0 0', so type keeps its native sizing and a cell can later go full-frame sharp. Wrap each cell's composition in Remotion <Loop durationInFrames={P}> with mutually awkward periods so the four never repeat in sync, and start each cell's first arrival by frame 2-6 on its own E.out curve with no shared global ease: for example a line converging with SPR.word, a Roll counter driven by countSteps(..., E.out), and an orbit whose angular speed decays as w = 11.25*e^(-t/10) + 2 deg/f, with satellites spawning on f10, f18 and f28. Only the one story element in each cell (pin, payoff word, button) gets C.accent; everything else stays greyscale. Merge every cell's cut frames into one list and nudge apart any two that fall within 6 f, and use no per-event SFX: one continuous groove carries the sound.
techniques.timing: First arrivals on f2, f2, f2 and f6 (no cell later than f8). Typical entrances: a type lockup settles in 18 f on E.out, a counter finishes in 28 f. Loop periods 260 / 462 / 244 / 428 f. Something changes somewhere about every 20 f (longest gap about 62 f). Cells 960x540 at 1080p.
techniques.use_when: A hero or social loop that must show several features at once, or a launch whose first second has to prove breadth.
techniques.avoid_when: The story needs one idea at a time, a single-message sting, or a 9:16 frame where the cells would shrink below about 540 px wide.

techniques.name: Macro number scramble, one-frame snap-out
techniques.summary: Huge digits fill and overflow the frame, re-rolling every frame. On one frame the view cuts back to the whole figure, which rolls into the final metric and holds: the number is the hook before any brand appears.
techniques.recipe: Lay out the final figure once with typeStyle('display') (tabular figures, fixed group separator) at a size where the whole string spans about 0.9 W, and draw each digit column as a Roll-style strip whose mask stays 1.6 lines tall during the macro phase, so outgoing digits stack and overflow vertically. Macro phase: scale the wrapper to 1.22 about the frame centre and, on every whole frame (fd), give 1-2 columns a new digit from rand(`${seed}:${fd(frame)}`). Snap: on a single frame decided with fd (so the motion-blur sub-samples agree), cut the scale to 1.0 with no tween, clip the masks to one line and lock the columns left to right 3 f apart until the final string is forced; then hold on breath (scale +0.065%/f) with no glints or sparkles, and keep the brand out until the end lockup. Sound: five dry glitch ticks inside the first 0.6 s, then the bed drops at least 30 dB within one frame on the lock frame and stays silent through the hold; reuse the identical tick cluster under the closing sting as a bookend.
techniques.timing: Macro 29 f; snap 1 f at f29; settle 12 f; final string forced from f41 (0.68 s); hold 72 f with only the scale drift. Ticks at about 0.17, 0.23, 0.31, 0.36 and 0.40 s.
techniques.use_when: The strongest proof is one metric (users, hours saved, uptime) and the film earns attention with the outcome before the brand.
techniques.avoid_when: There is no credible or impressive number, or the tone is calm and premium.

techniques.name: Mark builds, then is thrown into a macro of itself
techniques.summary: On frame 1 a dot swells into the brand mark. The mark grows briefly, holds for a breath, then shrinks away faster and faster and hard-cuts at peak speed to a frame-filling macro of the same mark, which keeps pulling back.
techniques.recipe: Show the mark only; the wordmark lockup is kept for the end. A 12 px dot at frame centre scales into the 320 px mark over 18 f on E.out, while a wrapper grows 0.83 -> 1 on E.out over 32 f from f8; then hold 8 f. Exit: wrapper scale 1 -> 0.55 over 20 f on E.in, with the hard cut on the exit's last (fastest) frame. The next shot opens on the same mark at the same screen point, its k multiplied by zoomHandoff(t, v0, 24) with v0 = zoomSpeed(kOut, cut - 1) (about -0.168): it starts near 2.2x and slows to 1x with no speed step at the cut, revealing the stage and the first UI as it settles. No overshoot anywhere; the master's motion-blur pass handles the fast frames (incoming edges peak at about 59 px/f).
techniques.timing: Dot to mark 18 f on E.out (edge about 49 px/f on its first frame); grow 32 f from f8; hold 8 f (f40-48); exit 20 f on E.in (f48-68), cut at f68 (1.13 s); macro pull-back 24 f through zoomHandoff from about 2.2x.
techniques.use_when: A brand-first logo sting where recognition must land in under half a second and the energy must pour into the next shot.
techniques.avoid_when: The mark is unfamiliar and needs a longer hold to be learned, or the film already uses a scale-continuity cut elsewhere. Never use it to show the full lockup.

techniques.name: Sparse intro, drop on the first hard cut
techniques.summary: (Sound and picture.) The first ~2 s carry only light plucks or a filtered, wide pad under the opening type; the low end and the kick land exactly on the frame where the punchline card or first product shot cuts in.
techniques.recipe: Arrange or edit the track so bar 1 has no sub and no kick and sits about 14 dB under the body, sounding at intent from frame 0 with no fade-in across the first bar: a steady filtered bed of plucks or pad, which may step up a few dB at the half-bar. Keep it wide (side about 3 dB under mid) and narrow it on the drop (side 16-19 dB under mid). Put the first hard cut on a downbeat, for example b(2) in src/timeline.ts (frame 120 at 120 BPM). Schedule the kick on that exact frame in src/sync.ts and the first sub swell 8-12 f before it. Keep the intro picture to one line or two short cards (2 words each at most) so reading fits the space; per-word ticks ride on top at a constant level.
techniques.timing: Intro 117-156 f (1.95-2.6 s); about +14 dB from intro to body; sub 8-12 f before the cut; kick on the cut frame (within 1 f).
techniques.use_when: Almost any film that opens on type and then shows the product with a tension-and-release shape.
techniques.avoid_when: Stings under 4 s, openers designed to be loud from frame 0 (live grid, macro scramble), or a drop that cannot land on a whole-frame cut.

techniques.name: Cursor into a field, two-stage push, typed provocation
techniques.summary: A small search pill sits still on a dark stage; a text cursor drifts in, the camera pushes in twice to a macro framing, and a provocative query types into the field before any brand appears.
techniques.recipe: Lay out the pill as world content under the anchor camera (camera(lc(A, B, t)) from src/lib/camera.ts), anchored on the caret. An I-beam SVG, placed by transform only as Cursor is, is already travelling on frame 0: it arrives on cursorArc (bow 0.2) over 30 f on E.glide, with a soft offset shadow (a copy blurred 6 px at 35% black, offset about a quarter of its height). The camera holds for the first 24 f, then push 1 takes k from 1 to 2.16 over 42 f on E.cam and push 2 from 2.16 to 7.2 over 44 f on E.glide (lc mixes k in log space, so the zoom rate stays even). Start TypeOn (cps 30) at about 60% of push 2 and feed typeOn's followX into the camera anchor through a 6-10 f lag so the camera tracks the caret without stepping; size the pill so one character advances at most 40 px on screen at 7.2x, which keeps the caret-following scroll of the typed text under 20 px/f. Draw no halo around the pill. Sound: micro ticks only (2-6 ms bursts high-passed above 4 kHz, at most one per word, 18-24 dB under the bed, with 20% seeded jitter in timing and gain), muted once the drums enter.
techniques.timing: Camera still for 24 f while the cursor flies in from frame 0 (30 f on E.glide); push 1 42 f (f24-66, peak 0.077 ln k per frame); push 2 44 f (f66-110, peak 0.082 ln k per frame); 7.2x in total over 88 f; typing from about f92 at 30 characters/s, each character at most 40 px wide on screen.
techniques.use_when: AI, search or command products, or any opener whose hook is a question the product answers.
techniques.avoid_when: The product has no input field, the film's camera grammar is flat, or the query runs past about 40 characters (the macro framing cannot hold it).

techniques.name: Oversize line flies through, restarts small
techniques.summary: A huge fragment of the headline, about a quarter of frame height, brakes in from the right with its letters fading on as it slows, then dissolves; three frames later the same line restarts small and centred so it can be read.
techniques.recipe: Start the big line's clock 6 f before the film's first frame (t = f + 6), so frame 0 already shows its first letters fading on as it brakes. Layer 1: the line at about 270 px, weight 500, colour rgba(255,255,255,0.65) on C.ink (or over a single-hue wash), with x = startX + inertia(t, 0, -70, 0.89).x (601 px of travel from 70 px/f). Per-character opacity is 0.65 * prog(t, 6 + 1.5i, 12 + 1.5i, E.smooth), so letters only resolve once the speed drops below about 20 px/f, and the whole layer fades 1 -> 0 over its last 7 f on E.smooth while it is still sliding. Start layer 2 on the next frame, with no empty frames between: a dissolve to an empty frame and a fresh start reads as the film restarting. Layer 2: the same line at reading size with its final centred layout precomputed, per-character opacity prog(t, 1.3i, 1.3i + 5, E.smooth), and container x = inertia(t, 0, -10.8, 0.88).x: an 84 px drift that lands exactly centred and never passes 12 px/f. Keep the opening type translucent and make the end card solid white, so the film reads as a question becoming an answer.
techniques.timing: Big line visible from f0 (its clock t = f + 6) to f35: slide 39 f, about 35 px/f at t = 6 and 17 px/f at t = 12; letters 6 f each, 1.5 f stagger; fade over the last 7 f. No gap; small line from f36, 13 characters in 17 f, drift settled in about 40 f.
techniques.use_when: The headline has a thesis word worth previewing big, in a dark, energetic launch.
techniques.avoid_when: Light stages where 65% white loses contrast, or headlines longer than about 5 words whose big fragment will not read. Also avoid it when the big fragment would sit still and cropped at both edges at any point: viewers read an oversized, cropped line that vanishes and then restarts small as a false start, not a preview. It has to travel every frame it is on screen.

techniques.name: Problem pile-up, freeze, turn
techniques.summary: The film opens inside the problem: cards, alerts or rows pile in faster and faster while a counter climbs, the picture freezes for a breath of true silence, and the turn hits on the downbeat.
techniques.recipe: Frame 0 already holds 2-3 overlapping cards. Arrival k comes gap_k = max(4, 14 * 0.88^k) frames after the previous one, so the pile accelerates, and each card rises from +40 px on SPR.firm with opacity over 8 f on E.smooth and a slight rotation of rand(k) * 6 - 3 deg. A corner counter climbs with Roll and countSteps(..., E.in) while the camera's k is multiplied by breath(prog(f, 0, end, E.in), 0.04). At peak density comes a designed freeze of at most 15 f, with the picture held and the bed and every tail cut dead; then the turn lands on the next downbeat b(...): the pile implodes on E.in, or the frame cuts to the answer. Sound: one soft tick per card, each 1 dB louder than the last, ending in the silence.
techniques.timing: 14 arrivals in about 100 f (gaps 14, 12, 11, 9.5, 8.4 ... down to 4 f); freeze of 15 f at most; turn on the next downbeat.
techniques.use_when: Problem-first launches whose pain is volume: notifications, tickets, tabs, invoices.
techniques.avoid_when: The pain is not about quantity, the brand film is calm, or the film already uses its one freeze elsewhere.

techniques.name: Finished result first, then rewind
techniques.summary: The film opens on the finished end state at its most impressive, holds for a beat, then visibly rewinds every element back to the empty start, where the story begins playing forward.
techniques.recipe: Every element is a function of frame, so remap time once at the act root: local = f < r0 ? T_end : T_end - (T_end - T_0) * prog(f, r0, r0 + R, E.smooth), with R = 36-48 f. Pass local to every component and decide discrete state with fd(local); entrances then replay backwards, and E.out arrivals become accelerating exits. Open at T_end with breath (+2.5%) over a 40 f hold. The rewind's peak rate is 2.86 × (T_end − T_0) / R times real time, so rewind at most about 120 f of build (about 8x at the peak for R = 42); for a longer build, set T_0 to a later, partly built state. Any element whose reversed move would pass 60 px/f, and any readable text that would pass 20 px/f, fades out over the rewind instead of travelling. Put one short filtered reverse swish under the rewind and a click on its last frame, then play the walkthrough forward from T_0 on the next beat.
techniques.timing: Hold 40 f; rewind 36-48 f on E.smooth (peak about 8x real time, at most about 120 f of build); forward play from the next beat.
techniques.use_when: Walkthroughs and feature films whose output is visually rich and readable at a glance.
techniques.avoid_when: An end state that needs explaining, or more than about 30 state changes (the rewind turns to mush).

techniques.name: A click starts the film
techniques.summary: From frame 0 a cursor is already travelling toward the one button on an otherwise bare stage; it presses, and the button floods open into the first scene.
techniques.recipe: C.paper stage with a single button (the product's primary action) slightly below centre. Cursor follows cursorArc(a, b, prog(f, -6, 18, E.glide), 0.2), so frame 0 is already mid-path because the clock starts 6 f before the shot. pressAt(f, 22) drives the cursor's press, and the button dips by 1 - 0.03 * hitPulse(f - 22, 2, 5). Iris starts at the press frame minus 1 (24 f, E.out in log space) from the button's centre and reveals the first scene inside it. Put the click SFX 0-1 f before the press frame, with nothing before it.
techniques.timing: Cursor arrives f18; press f22 (4 f down, 8 f recoil); iris f21-45; first scene live from f45.
techniques.use_when: UI walkthroughs and feature films where a single action is the product ('one click to ...').
techniques.avoid_when: Products that act on their own, or films where the cursor never returns after the hook (it breaks continuity).

techniques.name: Cut in mid-sentence, pull back to the line
techniques.summary: The film opens inside one giant word, its first letter cropped by the frame edge as if cutting into a thought mid-sentence; after a beat the camera pulls back to reveal the whole sentence at reading size.
techniques.recipe: Lay out the whole sentence once at display size (TYPE.display, 120 px) as world content and frame shot A at k = 3.2 on the key word, offset so its first glyph is about 40% cropped by the left edge. Frame 0 is already settling: a vertical inertia(f, 0, 3, 0.8) of about 13 px, then a 0.3 px/f drift through a 36 f hold. Pull back with lc(A, B, prog(f, 36, 92, E.dolly)) to k = 1 with the sentence centred; the log-space zoom keeps the rate even, and glyphs 600 px from the anchor stay under about 20 px/f. The neighbouring words exist from the start with no fades and simply enter the frame as it widens.
techniques.timing: Settle 12 f; hold 36 f; pull-back 56 f from 3.2x to 1x on E.dolly (peak about 0.032 ln k per frame).
techniques.use_when: Copy-led launches built on one charged word, in calm-to-medium films.
techniques.avoid_when: The key word is short or ordinary (the crop will not intrigue), or the film already opens on another zoom-out (icon card, macro number).

techniques.name: Velocity handoff cut
techniques.summary: The outgoing shot speeds up in one direction and is cut on its fastest frame. The next shot opens already moving the same way and brakes to rest, so momentum runs straight through the edit.
techniques.recipe: Make the cut an act boundary in timeline.ts so motion-blur samples never straddle it, and place it on a beat with b(). In the outgoing act, drive the camera (src/lib/camera.ts) or the hero's translate on E.exit (E.contact, or E.in for a harder snap) over its last 16-24 f, so it ends at peak speed on the final frame; for a zoom, apply the same ramp to k through lmix. In the incoming act, start the key element moving on frame 0 in the same screen direction at 1.0-1.5x that speed and slow it on E.out over 45-90 f. Size the two sides with exitSpeed(D, T, ease) and entryDistance(v, T) from references/transitions.md; for a flicked list, use y = v0·(1 − k^f)/(1 − k) with k = 0.92-0.943 and no overshoot. Give each act one dominant screen vector (+x in one act, −x in the next) and start every incoming element on the side it would enter from.
techniques.timing: Exit: last 16-24 f on E.exit (speed grows about ×1.1-1.2 per frame), ending at 25-40 px/f (never above 60) or −6 to −8% scale per frame. Entry: 30-55 px/f on frame 0, slowing about ×0.92-0.94 per frame (E.out over 45-90 f; entryDistance(40, 60) is about 400 px). A 1-3 px/f drift may run under the hold before the ramp. Text inside a moving shot must be under 20 px/f by the time it has to be read.
techniques.use_when: Most cuts between moving shots: feature-to-feature edits, montages, chapter changes, and any film that must never stop. Velocity-matched cuts are exempt from the two-uses-per-type limit.
techniques.avoid_when: One side has to be still (a held statement or a designed freeze), or the two shots would move in opposite directions. Carry a shape or an anchor across instead.

techniques.name: Scale-through cut
techniques.summary: An object shrinks faster and faster toward a fixed point, the film cuts, and a matching object appears much larger on the same point and keeps shrinking as it brakes, so one pull-back runs through two different worlds. The mirror version swells into the cut and opens on an undersized object that grows.
techniques.recipe: Choose an anchor screen point and keep both objects centred on it within ±30 px (fixed sx, sy in an anchor-camera Shot, or transform-origin on the anchor). Outgoing: k = lmix(1, 0.75, prog(f, T − 20, T, E.in)), so the last frame shrinks about 7.8%; cut on an act boundary. Incoming: the same subject in a new medium (3D render to flat map, device to flat UI, brand card to product world) with k = lmix(1.8, 1, prog(f, 0, 40, E.out)). Its first frame shrinks about 8.4%, so scale velocity is continuous in log space. For a related mark shown as a frame-filling macro, use k = 1 + (S0 − 1)·0.84^f from S0 = 8-9 and snap to 1 once |1 − k| < 0.01. Push version: the hero swells 1 → 1.22 on E.in over the last 16-24 f while the rest of the frame dims (brightness 1 → 0.6 on a dark stage), and the next shot opens at 0.8 and grows to 1 over 30 f on E.out.
techniques.timing: Exit: 16-24 f on E.in to 0.70-0.80 (last frame −7 to −9% per frame). Cut on a downbeat. Entry: 1.7-2.0x → 1 over 30-40 f on E.out (first frame −8 to −9%), or an 8-9x macro shrinking toward rest ×0.84 per frame and settled by about 30 f. Anchor drift ≤ 30 px. Push variant: +20-25% over 16-24 f, then 0.8 → 1 over 30 f.
techniques.use_when: Changing medium or world while keeping the subject: 3D to flat, device to UI, brand card to product, a mark coming back as a macro. Also hero pull-backs at act changes.
techniques.avoid_when: The two objects cannot share a centre point, or both sides are calm; a scale jump without matched scale velocity reads as a jump cut. Use it at most twice per film.

techniques.name: Anchored overlay, background swap
techniques.summary: A foreground element (a pin, a status pill, a modal, a big word) keeps its exact screen position while the world behind it hard-cuts, so a total change of scene reads as a change of zoom or context.
techniques.recipe: Render the overlay from one absolute-frame function drawn by every act it crosses (deviceAt in references/transitions.md §4.1). Use the identical transform string on both sides of each cut, so its last frame in one act and its first in the next are consecutive samples of one curve. Each background change is an act boundary; a montage is 2-3 background acts in a row behind the same overlay. The overlay keeps its own clock through the cut (a running scale tween, a 0.5-1 px/f drift or a breath() push), so it is never static for more than 48 f. After the last swap the overlay acts on the new world: it travels into its slot on E.glide over 40 f (moves up to 350 px), or FLIPs into an input.
techniques.timing: Background holds of 10-22 f each in a montage (2-3 swaps), or a single swap. Overlay offset across the cut: 0 px ideally, 30 px at most. Overlay drift 0.5-1 px/f. Follow-up move 40 f on E.glide. Cuts on beats or 16ths.
techniques.use_when: Showing that one thing persists across contexts: a location going from 3D city to map, a request going from an empty void to the full app, a claim held over a run of photos.
techniques.avoid_when: The overlay is text that must be reread after each swap, or the backgrounds are busy and bright enough to swallow it. Keep backgrounds near 5% mean luma under light overlays.

techniques.name: Polarity flip cut
techniques.summary: A hard cut flips the stage between near-black and near-white on a downbeat, often with the same icon or pill held on the same spot in inverted colours, so the luminance jump itself is the accent.
techniques.recipe: Plan adjacent acts with opposite stage luminance (mean luma differing by at least 150 of 255) and cut on their act boundary on a downbeat, after a dropout or silence, with one impact in the sound. Carry the flip; never cut from a static frame. Either cut on the outgoing motion peak (a zoom-through or an accelerating exit), or end on a shape centred at P and open on the same shape at P ±20 px, at 1-2.5x the size, with fill and ground swapped. An ink icon on paper becomes a paper icon on ink; an accent pill on paper becomes a paper pill on an accent field. The incoming shape is already drifting, translateY −36 px over 30 f on E.out. For a softer edge, draw two ghost frames with the incoming shot at 0.12 and then 0.94 opacity over the fully opaque outgoing frame. Declare the cut for scripts/forensics.py, and use no flash frame and no dip through black.
techniques.timing: Cut in 0 f, or 2 ghost frames at 0.12 and 0.94. Anchor scale jump 1.0-2.5x. Post-cut drift 30 f on E.out. After a flip to dark, wait 12-20 f before any small type. At most one flip per bar and two flip cuts per film.
techniques.use_when: Act breaks: problem to answer, public to private, demo to claim. The strongest punctuation on a drop.
techniques.avoid_when: A third time in one film; a flip from a static frame with nothing carried; or when the accent field would be the film's second full-frame accent flood.

techniques.name: Shape match cut
techniques.summary: The hero shape leaves one shot at a known point and size, and the next shot opens on a matching shape (the mark, the flat UI, the real object) on the same point, so the object's identity carries across a change of world.
techniques.recipe: Record the outgoing shape's centre and size on its last frame (toScreen from src/lib/camera.ts, or inkBox from src/lib/measure.ts for type). Open the incoming act with the matching shape centred there within ±20 px, at 0.57-1.3x that size. Keep motion on both sides. The outgoing shape shrinks 2-4% over its last 4 f on E.in (or a coin turns face-on, rotateY 90 → 10 deg over 22 f on E.out). The incoming shape keeps going, for example k = lmix(0.57, 1, prog(f, 0, 18, E.out)), with no overshoot. Match colour, corner radius and stroke weight so only the medium changes (device screen to flat UI, coin emblem to logotype, circle to app icon), and hold the result 12-30 f before it moves on.
techniques.timing: Cut in 0 f. Centre offset ≤ 20 px. Scale ratio 0.57-1.3x. Incoming settle 18 f on E.out, with half the change done in about 2 f. Outgoing pre-cut shrink 4 f on E.in. Hold 12-30 f.
techniques.use_when: Turning a problem shape into the answer, a device mockup into the bare UI, or a physical object into the mark.
techniques.avoid_when: The silhouettes differ (round against tall), so the match cannot be seen. Use a dot relay or a container morph instead.

techniques.name: Giant word punch-out
techniques.summary: A hard cut lands on an extreme close-up of an oversized word sliding fast and braking, its letters resolving one by one. A second cut jumps out to the whole word at reading size, arriving with wide tracking that slams together.
techniques.recipe: Close-up act: set the word at 2-2.5x its final size, cropped by the frame, with x = x_end + (x_start − x_end)·0.92^f, starting at no more than 70 px/f. Each letter animates blur 12 → 0 px and colour C.mute → C.ink over 12 f on a 2 f stagger starting at frame 4, so the first letter lands sharp at frame 16, when the pan is down to about 18 px/f. Cut on the act boundary while the word still moves at 13-20 px/f. Wide act: show the whole word, with p = prog(f, 0, 30, E.out) driving scale lmix(1.38, 1, p) and letter-spacing from 0.8 em to its resting track. Add a horizontal-only blur (SVG feGaussianBlur stdDeviation '18 0') set by blurIn(p, 18), opacity 0.5 → 1 over the first 8 f, and colour mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, t) with t going 0.6 → 1 over 17 f. Hold 30-60 f, then exit on E.in over 6-12 f.
techniques.timing: Close-up 18-22 f: starts at ≤ 70 px/f and slows ×0.92 per frame (about 18 px/f by frame 16); letters resolve over 12 f with a 2 f stagger from frame 4. Cut at 13-20 px/f residual speed. Wide entry 30 f on E.out: scale 1.38 → 1, tracking 0.8 em → rest, horizontal blur of 18 px gone by 60% of the move, outer letters ≤ 60 px/f. Colour settles in 17 f. Hold 30-60 f. Exit 6-12 f on E.in.
techniques.use_when: A one-word claim or product name that deserves two beats: read it, then see it whole. Vertical cut-downs where one huge word fills the frame.
techniques.avoid_when: Lines of more than two words, or words over about 10 letters (the close-up loses the word); or when the next shot needs the word small within a second.

techniques.name: Collapse to a dot relay
techniques.summary: The hero collapses into one small dot, or the whole world shrinks into it. The dot, the only thing that survives, opens into the next object: a check ring, an avatar, the mark.
techniques.recipe: Collapse the hero (a card, a prompt box, or the detached dot of an i) to a 24-52 px dot: width and height go to the dot size and border-radius to 50%, over 4 f on E.in when it feeds a cut, or 16 f on E.out when it snaps and holds. To take the world with it, start 15 f later and scale the world group with k = lmix(1, 0.03, prog(f, s, s + 24, E.contact)) about the dot centre, over the next stage colour. Its corner radius grows to 50% and its mask edge is feathered 40 px; unmount it once it is smaller than the dot. The dot stays at full opacity through the seam (one absolute-frame function, or a hard cut that holds it on the same screen point). Then it opens into the next object: a check ring (stroke-dashoffset 1 → 0 and scale 0.6 → 1 over 8 f on E.out, its label 4 f later), an avatar disc (fill ramps paper → ink linearly over 12 f, icon fading in over the last 4 f), or the mark.
techniques.timing: Collapse: 4 f (E.in, into a cut) or 16 f (E.out, snap and hold). World shrink: 24 f on E.contact for a dot near centre (edges ≤ 66 px/f), or 40 f for a dot near a corner, starting 15 f after the collapse. Reopen over 8-12 f. Any device rotation that follows settles over 28 f on E.out.
techniques.use_when: Submit, send, process, receive: actions that mean 'this went in and came out as that'. Also the film's signature device when the mark contains a dot.
techniques.avoid_when: The dot would blink out or change size or colour at the seam, or the film already has an implosion seam.

techniques.name: Defocus cut
techniques.summary: The outgoing shot throws itself out of focus in a few frames, the film cuts to a shot that is still fully defocused with its content already moving, and the lens snaps sharp as that content settles.
techniques.recipe: In the outgoing act's last 6 f, wrap the scene in RackFocus with t = prog(f, T − 6, T, E.in) and blur 16 px, fading it toward the next stage colour (opacity 1 → 0.2). Hard cut on the act boundary. The incoming act opens in RackFocus at blur 24 px and t = 1, held for 6-12 f while its content already moves in (cards on a diagonal, E.out over 20 f). Then t goes 1 → 0.1 over 8 f on E.in (the snap) and 0.1 → 0 over 12-20 f on E.outSoft with mid = true. Text in the incoming shot uses Words.tsx or blurIn so it lands sharp, and readable text is never blurred for more than 6 f.
techniques.timing: Out: 6 f on E.in to 16 px. Cut. Defocused hold 6-12 f at 24 px. Snap 8 f (E.in) to t = 0.1. Settle 12-20 f (E.outSoft). Incoming card move 20 f on E.out. About 30-45 f in all.
techniques.use_when: Joining two shots with nothing in common (no shared shape, direction or colour), or a deliberate 'look again' beat.
techniques.avoid_when: As the default seam (it turns into a soft crossfade), on shots dominated by small text, or more than twice per film.

techniques.name: Path relay
techniques.summary: A line and its lead dot carry the eye from one place to the next. The connector bends around a rounded corner with the camera following, or continues across a cut and enters the next shot from the same edge at the same angle.
techniques.recipe: Draw the connector as an SVG path (stroke ≥ 1.5 px, C.white on ink or C.ink on paper) with pathLength 1, revealed by stroke-dashoffset; corners are arcs of r = 40 px. Place the lead dot with getPointAtLength (from @remotion/paths, or an analytic line-plus-arc), where the arc length grows with prog(f, a, b, E.linear) at 8-16 px/f. The camera follows with a lag: the anchor-camera Shot frames the dot's position at f − 10. Across a cut, start shot B's path at the frame edge where A's path left, at the same angle and speed, so the dot reaches its target 18 f after the cut. Off-frame variant: the dot or cursor speeds out of frame on E.contact over 24 f and stays hidden 12 f while the camera relocates. It then re-enters at ≤ 60 px/f, slowing ×0.92 per frame to rest in about 36 f.
techniques.timing: Dot at a constant 8-16 px/f. Corner radius 40 px. Camera lag 8-12 f. One run lasts 60-72 f. After a cut the dot lands 18 f later. Off-frame gap 12 f; re-entry at ≤ 60 px/f, slowing ×0.92 per frame.
techniques.use_when: Money, data or messages travelling (send, route, sync), flowcharts and timelines, and films whose UI already uses lines and nodes.
techniques.avoid_when: The film has no line language, or the path would cross readable text. A path that loops back reads as indecision.

techniques.name: Iris from a glyph
techniques.summary: A small dot appears on a word or icon in the current shot and balloons exponentially to swallow the frame, showing the next scene inside it, so the reveal starts from content rather than from nowhere.
techniques.recipe: Render the incoming scene above the outgoing one, clipped with clip-path: circle(r at cx cy). The 14 px seed dot (in the next scene's stage colour) appears on the glyph, scale 0 → 1 over 6 f on E.out, and holds 6-10 f. Then r = lmix(14, R, prog(f, 0, 20, E.linear)), where R is the distance to the farthest frame corner: a constant ratio of about ×1.25-1.29 per frame. Over the same 20 f, (cx, cy) moves from the glyph to the frame centre on E.smooth. Optional residue: when the disc reaches r ≈ 900 px, step its fill through three tones of one hue over 6 f, and leave a 90 px ring one tone darker at that radius as set dressing for the new shot. For an app icon, use a funnel instead of a circle: a clip polygon anchored at the icon's base whose top width and height grow ×1.18 per frame over 24 f.
techniques.timing: Seed in over 6 f, hold 6-10 f. Iris 20 f at a constant ratio (about ×1.25-1.29 per frame, radius in log space). Centre drift 20 f on E.smooth. Optional tonal ramp: 3 steps over 6 f. Funnel variant: 24 f at ×1.18 per frame. The disc fills the frame on the downbeat.
techniques.use_when: A word in the copy names what the next scene shows (a benchmark, a feature, a place); dark-to-light or light-to-dark act changes.
techniques.avoid_when: A linear radius (it crawls, then snaps); the same iris more than twice per film; a seed glyph the viewer has not had 6 f to find.

techniques.name: Portal zoom with aspect morph
techniques.summary: A window opens in the middle of a solid tile. Tile and window grow faster and faster while the square stretches to 16:9, until the window's interior is the next scene and the tile's border has flown off the edges.
techniques.recipe: Draw an outer rect in the accent and an inner rect inset by 30% of the outer width and height on each side. The next scene renders inside the inner rect's clip (insetClip) from frame 0, at its final transform. Outer width w = lmix(204, 4800, prog(f, 0, 39, E.linear)), a pure exponential of about ×1.084 per frame, with aspect = mix(1, 16/9, prog(f, 0, 30, E.smooth)) and height = w / aspect. The accent border's outer edges leave the frame near frame 30, and the inner window covers the frame at frame 39, when the clip is dropped. Optional lead-in: the words on either side speed inward under the tile (translateX by their distance over 22 f on E.in, with blurOut). Then the tile turns 90 deg like a cube to bring a plain accent face to the front (CSS 3D box, front = the mark, side = accent at brightness 0.85, over 12 f on E.inOut), and holds that blank face 6 f before the window opens. Keep text out until the window has filled; the next scene's labels rise in as the border clears.
techniques.timing: Lead-in: converge 22 f, cube turn 12 f, blank hold 6 f. Portal: 39 f at ×1.084 per frame (border gone by about frame 30, inner window edges ≤ 78 px/f). Aspect 1 → 1.78 over the first 30 f. Next-scene labels start from about frame 30 on a 4-6 f stagger.
techniques.use_when: The film's energy peak and act break, going inside the product, when the mark or app icon is a tile.
techniques.avoid_when: The accent has already flooded the frame once (the tile border is a brief accent flood), or another zoom-through sits in the same act.

techniques.name: Band wipe
techniques.summary: A band crosses a region (snapping up, lingering, then whipping off, or sweeping across a chart) and the content changes along its edge: the old state is erased under it and the new state draws in its wake.
techniques.recipe: Clip both states to the region and drive one band position b(f). The old state stays clipped to the side the band has not reached (clip-path: inset(0 0 0 b px)), and the new state draws in behind it (a line chart's stroke-dashoffset follows b). In the full look the band is a luminous light core falling off through a warm hue, screen-blended over the content. Sweep profile: a 368 px band crosses a chart at a constant 60-70 px/f (prog with E.linear, about 27 f for a 1400 px chart plus the band), starting 2 f after the control that caused it (a tab) lands, never easing out, until the chart edge cuts it off. Hang-time profile, for a full-frame band behind giant type: the bottom edge goes from 81% to 66% of frame height over 6 f on E.out, 66% to 53% over 20 f at constant speed, and 53% to 0 over 16 f on E.contact. In the hang-time profile the band's edges are flat mask edges, so they may pass 80 px/f; nothing textured rides on them.
techniques.timing: Sweep: 368 px band at a constant 60-70 px/f (about 27 f across a 1400 px chart), starting 2 f after the cause. Hang-time: 6 f (E.out) + 20 f (constant speed) + 16 f (E.contact) = 42 f. The new state draws in within 6-10 f after the band passes.
techniques.use_when: Swapping a data series, a filter result or a big-type card in place, when a control's tap should visibly cause the change.
techniques.avoid_when: Applied to whole scenes again and again (it becomes a preset wipe), or when the band would cross text the viewer has not finished reading.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Fill the band with the one accent (or ink on a paper stage) at full strength. Its trailing side falls off by opacity of that same colour over 30-40% of its width, with no light core, no screen blend and no second hue.

techniques.name: Horizon rise
techniques.summary: A huge disc rises from the bottom edge like a planet horizon, its rim washing over the frame, until its dark core swallows the screen and becomes the stage for the next line.
techniques.recipe: One full-frame layer holds a circle of radius R = 1.1 × frame width (2112 px at 1080p), centred horizontally: a dark core in the next act's stage colour out to 55% of R, then bands of rim colour out to 85%, softened by a 30 px blur. In the full look the rim is several hues with a bloom. Bake the disc as a dithered PNG with scripts/dither-gradient.py so the soft falloff does not band. Move its centre from y = H + R (the disc's top just touching the bottom edge) to y = 0.58 H over 56 f on E.dolly, with the previous scene disappearing behind it; at rest the core covers all four corners. Start the next text at about frame 46, inside the core. Lighter version: a rim band 40% of the frame height rises from the bottom edge over 16 f on E.in, and the cut lands mid-rise on the beat.
techniques.timing: Rise: 56 f on E.dolly, about 2570 px of centre travel at 1080p (the rim's leading edge peaks near 70 px/f mid-move). Next text from about frame 46. Band version: 16 f on E.in. The core fills the frame on a downbeat.
techniques.use_when: A single colour event that divides the film into acts (UI section to brand moment), or a calm lift from a statement into the next card.
techniques.avoid_when: More than once per film, or on a light film where the dark core would be the only dark frame.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Keep one hue: the dark core, then a rim of the accent at full strength falling off by opacity of that same accent (no second hue, no bloom), baked dithered. Or use a hard-edged ink disc with a 1.5 px accent edge rising over a paper stage.

techniques.name: Product surface cover wipe
techniques.summary: A product surface (a UI panel, a window, a device) moves in front of the old shot and either passes straight through it with the scene changed behind it, or lands and becomes the new shot.
techniques.recipe: Pass-through: a panel 1.15x the frame height, showing the product's real UI, moves at a constant 64-72 px/f (prog with E.linear) from fully above the frame to fully below. The scene beneath switches on the first frame the panel covers the frame completely, decided with fd(frame); the motion-blur pass streaks the panel. Land: the product window rises about 940 px from below the frame to its rest pose over 44 f on E.glide, above the title layer, while the title fades 1 → 0 over 36 f, starting 16 f before the window moves. Occluder variant: during a fast camera push, time one foreground object to cross the lens on the push's peak frame, covering at least 60% of the frame for 2-4 f, and change the world behind it then. In every version the surface sits above the old shot in z-order, and its own content does not need to be readable until it rests.
techniques.timing: Pass-through: about 2600 px at 64-72 px/f, or 36-40 f; the scene switches on the full-cover frame. Land: 940 px over 44 f on E.glide (peak about 64 px/f at 31% of the move); the title fades over 36 f, starting 16 f before. Occluder: covers for 2-4 f at the push's peak.
techniques.use_when: Promise to product: the UI pushes the headline off. Scene changes that should show the product itself rather than a graphic.
techniques.avoid_when: The surface is a plain coloured slab (then it is a preset wipe), or the pass-through would need more than 80 px/f; shorten the distance with a cut instead.

techniques.name: Reveal by subtraction
techniques.summary: The clutter in front of the hero flies off toward the frame edges or shrinks away, uncovering a hero that was already sitting at its final size behind it.
techniques.recipe: Layer order: the hero at the bottom, static, already at its final size and position; the clutter above it. Each clutter item moves along the vector from the hero's centre through its own centre, its distance scaled by (1 + index × 0.1), on E.contact over 30 f. Set its travel to twice its distance to clear the frame, which keeps it under about 75 px/f until it is gone; keep that clearing distance ≤ 750 px by starting big cards near the edges. Window variant: the current window shrinks into the corner where the cursor sits, with transform-origin on that corner and k = lmix(1, 0.05, prog(f, 0, 40, E.contact)). Its opacity goes to 0 over the last 6 f, and the next panel's entrance starts 4 f after it vanishes. Staccato variant: remove one item every 5-7 f on hard steps (fd), re-centring the survivors instantly, until one remains, held 17 f.
techniques.timing: Scatter: 30 f on E.contact; items clear the frame by about frame 24; stagger 0-2 f; the hero stays static throughout. Window minimize: 40 f on E.contact in log scale (far corner ≤ 75 px/f), fading over the last 6 f; next entrance 4 f later. Staccato: one removal every 5-7 f, final hold 17 f.
techniques.use_when: Ending a busy montage on the one stat, card or word. Walkthroughs that change app areas through the product's own window behaviour.
techniques.avoid_when: The hero is not ready behind the clutter (it must never pop in), or the clutter is readable content the viewer has not finished.

techniques.name: Conveyor line swap
techniques.summary: The current line floats up and fades, the stage is empty for an instant, and the next line rises from below into the same spot, so a run of statements reads as one upward feed.
techniques.recipe: Outgoing line: translateY 0 → −135 px through depart(q), with q = prog(f, 0, 30, E.in); opacity 1 → 0 over its last 8 f, plus blurOut(q, 8). Leave 2 empty frames. Incoming line: translateY +188 → 0 through arrive(p), with p = prog(f, 0, 30, E.out). Its opacity goes 0 → 1 over the first 10 f, so it flies faded while faster than 20 px/f, and its colour goes C.mute → C.ink over 16 f with mixColor. For a word-by-word version, use Words.tsx with stagger 3-4 and out/outDur 16, so each old word rises away as its replacement rises in. Keep one direction (up) for the whole run.
techniques.timing: Exit: 30 f on E.in (last frame about 26 px/f, while fading). Gap 2 f. Entry: 30 f on E.out (first frame about 37 px/f, while faded); colour over 16 f. Per-word stagger 3-4 f. One line per bar or half bar.
techniques.use_when: Sequences of short claims, lists of capabilities, a subject that changes while the predicate stays.
techniques.avoid_when: Lines of very different length or alignment (the eye loses the slot), or more than 4-5 lines in a row without another seam type.

techniques.name: Motion-masked swap
techniques.summary: Content changes on exactly the frame something else moves fastest (background rings whipping past, a card kicking into a tilt), so the change hides inside the motion and two states chain in one space with no visible cut.
techniques.recipe: Drive a large secondary motion with a curve whose peak falls on the swap frame s. Either run a background sweep on E.smooth over 20-24 f, from s − 11 to s + 11, so its peak speed lands on s. Or kick a card with rotateY = 12 deg × hitPulse(f − s + 2, 2, 3) and skewY 2 deg on the same envelope, in a perspective(900px) container. Decide the content with fd(frame) >= s, so every motion-blur sub-sample agrees, and give the new content its own arrival (a slam or a word reveal) from s. Give kicked cards a soft shadow (0 18px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.18)) so the tilt reads.
techniques.timing: Sweep: 20-24 f on E.smooth, centred on the swap. Kick: attack 2 f, decay tau 3 f, settled in about 8 f. Repeat no faster than every 48-54 f.
techniques.use_when: Changing copy inside a continuous environment; cycling examples (photos, prompts, results) in a loop.
techniques.avoid_when: The masking motion is weak (under about 20 px/f at its peak), so the swap shows; or the content is a counter (roll the digits instead).

techniques.name: Tip-back exit
techniques.summary: The outgoing scene tips away from camera like a sheet laid onto a table, or flips up into a line, speeding up and fading into the next stage colour, and the next element lands on the clean field.
techniques.recipe: Wrap the outgoing scene in a 3D container (transform-origin 50% 100%, perspective 1200 px) and tip it: rotateX 0 → 40 deg and translateY 0 → +10% over 30 f on E.smooth. Lay a floor of the stage colour over it, opaque across the bottom 25% and transparent from 55% up, so the scene sinks into the stage, and dim it toward the next act's stage colour (overlay 0 → 0.9) over the last 12 f. Fast version: rotateX 0 → 88 deg with translateY 0 → −400 px over 20 f on E.contact (last frame about 70 px/f), so the scene flattens into a line at the top edge and uncovers what sits beneath. Flat version: a clip-path inset from the bottom grows on E.contact over 24 f, and the cut lands on its fastest frame. The next element starts on the frame the exit clears, or 1 f before.
techniques.timing: Tip-back: 30 f on E.smooth (rotateX 40 deg). Flip to a line: 20 f on E.contact. Crop collapse: 24 f on E.contact. Dim overlay 0 → 0.9 over the last 12 f. The next element starts 0-1 f after the exit clears.
techniques.use_when: Ending a UI section to hand over to a statement or an alert, when the next beat needs an empty stage for big type.
techniques.avoid_when: The next act opens on the same pose (use a relay instead), or the dim would go to black and back up (a dip) instead of into the next stage colour.

techniques.name: Envelope-matched type cut
techniques.summary: A big line hard-cuts to a much smaller, longer line whose words start spread apart so it spans exactly the old line's width, then the gaps close while the sideways drift carries on, so the outer edges of the type survive the cut.
techniques.recipe: On the cut frame, measure line A's on-screen width W_A and its centre or left edge (measureTracked from src/lib/measure.ts times A's current scale). Lay line B out at rest (cap height 2-3x smaller, more words) and read its natural width W_B, which must be smaller than W_A, and its word positions from measureTracked prefixes. Spread B with an extra gap per word space, g(f) = g0 · (1 − prog(f, 0, 36, E.outSoft)) with g0 = (W_A − W_B)/(n − 1), applied as translateX g · (j − (n − 1)/2) on word j of a centred line (g · j with the left edge pinned for a left-aligned one). Each word keeps its own tracking, so it stays readable while the gaps close. Cut on the act boundary, optionally with one ghost frame of B at 0.65 opacity over A. Both lines carry the same horizontal drift through the cut (A's creep, for example −3.5 px/f), which decays in B over 60 f on E.outSoft, and B may ink in from C.mute to C.ink over 16 f with mixColor.
techniques.timing: Cut in 0 f, or 1 ghost frame at 0.6-0.7 incoming. The gaps close over 36 f on E.outSoft, half done by frame 5. The outermost words travel (W_A − W_B)/2: keep that at or under 160 px so their first frame stays under 20 px/f, or fly them at 0.6 opacity for the first 6 f. Shared drift 3-4 px/f, decaying in B over 60 f. Hold B at least 60 f.
techniques.use_when: A big two- or three-word claim hands over to its full sentence or call to action; any big-to-small type change where both lines share a centre or a left edge and the type already drifts sideways.
techniques.avoid_when: B is naturally wider than A (use a blur-swap rescale instead), either line is a single word (there are no gaps, so collapse one word's tracking instead), or the alignment changes across the cut.

techniques.name: Angle change on a shared drift
techniques.summary: A hard cut jumps to a new angle or the next state of the same object (front to top-down, open to closed) while the slow zoom or pan carries on at exactly the same rate, so a calm shot changes viewpoint with no jolt and no speed ramp.
techniques.recipe: Write the drift once as a function of the absolute frame and multiply it into both acts' anchor-camera k (src/lib/camera.ts): d(abs) = lmix(1.10, 1, prog(abs, a, a + 96, E.outSoft)) for a settling pull (lmix(1, 1.10, ...) for a push), plus any pan as sx += v · (abs − a). zoomSpeed(kA, cut − 1) then equals zoomSpeed(kB, cut) by construction. Shot A frames the subject from one angle. Shot B frames the same subject at least 30 deg away (yaw ±35-50 deg on a tilted UI plane, or a top-down pitch on an object built with depth) or in its next state (lid open to closed, card face to back). Its on-screen centre stays within ±40 px of A's and its apparent size within ±15%. Cut on an act boundary 8-16 f into the drift, on a beat, while the frame still changes about 0.3% per frame. When the subject itself acts (a lid closes, a device turns), drive that action from one absolute progress too and cut at 35-55% of it, so it finishes in the new angle. Keep the stage colour and light identical, and add no ghost frame.
techniques.timing: Drift 96 f on E.outSoft from 1.10x (or a 2-4 px/f pan). Cut 8-16 f in, at −0.26 to −0.36% scale per frame (about 3 px/f at the frame edge); the drift settles 40-80 f after the cut. Angle change at least 30 deg, centre offset at most 40 px, size change at most 15%. Optional subject action 36-60 f on E.smooth, cut at 35-55% of it. Cut in 0 f.
techniques.use_when: Calm films and product beauty shots where a velocity ramp would be too loud: showing an object's second side or its next state within one continuous gesture.
techniques.avoid_when: The two angles look alike (under about 30 deg it reads as a jump cut), the subject's size or position jumps, or one side is static. For a lift in energy, use a velocity handoff instead.

techniques.name: Select and retype swap
techniques.summary: A finished headline is selected like text in an editor, the highlight holds for a beat, and on one frame the selection is replaced by a caret that types the next line in the same place.
techniques.recipe: Set both lines left-aligned in the same font, size and baseline, with line A rendered as per-character spans. The selection is a highlight rect 1.15 em tall from the ascender line: C.ink on paper with the covered glyphs switched to C.paper, or C.white with C.ink glyphs on an ink stage. Its left edge jumps one word leftward every 2-3 f, from the last word to the first, decided with fd and placed from measureTracked prefix widths; for a select-all it covers the line in one frame. The caret sits solid at its left edge. Hold the selection 10-12 f. Then, on one fd frame, remove line A and the highlight together, leave the caret at the line start and put one tick on that frame. Type line B with TypeOn from the same frame (2 f per character on E.type, head fade 4 f, caret blinking once idle). For a centred line, offset it by (full width − typed width)/2, using typeOn().followX through a 6-10 f lag. If the new line's last word is the beat that lands, give it the accent and relax it to ink over 12 f through charStyle.
techniques.timing: Selection 2-3 f per word (or a 1 f select-all), hold 10-12 f, replace on 1 f. Line B types at 2 f per character on E.type (a 20-character line in 40 f), and the caret blinks 30 f on, 30 f off once idle. About 60-75 f in all for a five-word, 20-character pair.
techniques.use_when: Products where text is the medium (editors, prompts, writing and AI tools); correcting a claim, where the assumption is selected and overwritten by the answer; two or three headline swaps that should feel authored.
techniques.avoid_when: The product has nothing to do with text, lines run past about 40 characters (the typing outlasts the read), or the swap repeats more than three times in a row and turns into a typing demo.

techniques.name: Stepped column fill
techniques.summary: Columns rise from the bottom edge in a stepped pyramid centred under the hero, spreading outward until they close into one solid field that becomes the next stage behind it.
techniques.recipe: Split the frame into N equal columns with no gutters, layered below the hero: 12-16 at 1920 px, or the hero's own grid unit so they line up with the bars or pixels of a mark. Column i starts d_i = |i − c| · 2 f after the first, where c is the column under the hero's centre. It rises from the bottom edge with height = H · prog(f, s + d_i, s + d_i + 40, E.smooth), so the tops form a stepped pyramid that widens outward. Fill each column with the next act's stage colour; in its full look every column carries a multi-hue vertical ramp. The columns are flat mask edges on a flat fill with nothing textured on them, so their tops may peak near 76 px/f. The hero keeps a living-hold creep throughout. Where the field rises behind it, draw a second copy of the hero in the opposite tone clipped to the union of the column rects (built by the same geometry function), so the hero flips tone exactly where a column stands behind it, with no fade. On the frame the outermost column fills, swap the column layer for one plate of that colour and land that frame on a downbeat. The hero answers it with scale 1 + 0.02 · hitPulse(f − close, 2, 5), or with its next build step.
techniques.timing: Each column rises over 40 f on E.smooth (tops peak at about 76 px/f at 1080p). Stagger 2 f per column outward from the centre (7 steps for 14-15 columns), about 54 f in all. The field closes on a downbeat and swaps to one flat plate on the same frame. Hero pulse: attack 2 f, tau 5 f.
techniques.use_when: Marks built from bars, steps or pixels; data and analytics products, where the columns read as a chart; stings and loop intros that change the stage colour behind a held hero.
techniques.avoid_when: As a general scene change between unrelated shots (it reads as a preset blinds wipe), behind small readable type, or more than once per film.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Fill every column with one flat colour: the next stage colour, or the accent if this is the film's one accent flood. Or alternate two adjacent lightness steps of one hue from column to column and let them merge into a single tone as the field closes. Never put a ramp inside a column.

techniques.name: Living hold creep
techniques.summary: Under every hold the frame keeps a barely visible push, pull or sideways drift, so no shot sits dead while the viewer reads.
techniques.recipe: Set the anchor camera's ax, ay on the focal element so the creep pivots there. Multiply k by breath(prog(f, holdStart, holdEnd, E.linear) * (1 - nextMove), amount), where amount = 0.0005 x the hold length in frames and nextMove is the next move's 0..1 progress, so the next move releases the creep with no velocity step. Push on proof and result shots, pull (negative amount) on busy or chaotic boards, and use a tiny creep on the end card. For type or a single card, drift sideways instead: with g = f - holdStart, sx = sx0 - v * (g - 20 * (1 - Math.exp(-g / 20))), which leaves the seam at zero velocity and reaches v after about 60 f. Keep every layer the camera carries static inside the one transform, so nothing stair-steps on the pixel grid during the creep.
techniques.timing: Scale creep 0.04-0.07%/f (+2.4 to +4.2%/s), at most 0.1%/f in a 40-60 f tail after a big push. Pulls about -0.08%/f. End card 0.0125%/f. Lateral drift 0.3-0.5 px/f for UI and cards, 1.5-3 px/f for big display type. E.linear once at speed, with a 20 f exponential ease-in from a seam. Released over the next move's own ease.
techniques.use_when: Any hold longer than about 30 f: reading a caption, watching a counter, a UI state sitting after an action, the end card.
techniques.avoid_when: A designed freeze of at most 15 f on a silence, or a shot where a big camera move or a travelling cursor already supplies the life. Never stack a creep on top of a punch-in drift on the same axis.

techniques.name: Breathing zoom between interactions
techniques.summary: After a reveal the camera slowly pulls back, coasts through a stop and turns smoothly into a slow push that lands on the next interaction, so the frame breathes across a whole act.
techniques.recipe: Drive only k, from a keyframed zoom rate rather than from poses: rate(i) = interpolate(i, [s0, s0 + 72, s0 + 108, s0 + 168], [-0.0025, 0, 0.0014, 0.0011], {extrapolateLeft: 'clamp', extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}) with linear interpolation, and k = k0 * Math.exp(sum of rate(i) for i = s0..f), computed in a pure loop every frame with no state kept between renders. Put ax, ay on the element the next interaction touches, so the zoom pivots on it and it holds its screen position. Keyframe the rate so it crosses zero rather than resting there: |rate| may stay under 0.0002 for no more than 12 f. Close the act with a short exhale under the final hold: k x lmix(1, 0.94, prog(f, T, T + 60, E.out)).
techniques.timing: Pull after a reveal: -0.25%/f falling to 0 over 72 f (about -9% total). Push into the next interaction: 0 rising to +0.14%/f over 36 f, about +6% within 60 f of the zero crossing; table and list acts run +0.03 to +0.17%/f (about +6.6% total). Rate keyframes 36-90 f apart, linear. Exhale x0.94 over 60 f on E.out.
techniques.use_when: Dashboard, analytics or table acts of 4-10 s with several interactions in one framing, where cutting would cost orientation.
techniques.avoid_when: Shots shorter than about 90 f, acts that already move pose to pose with big pushes, or a scrolling feed (a zoom on a moving list reads as wobble).

techniques.name: Punch-in insert on the same render
techniques.summary: A hard cut jumps from the wide view to a 2-2.5x on-axis close-up, or to a 3-4.5x macro of the exact control being used, while every animation keeps running, then cuts back out.
techniques.recipe: Lay the product out once and define two Shots on it: WIDE, and INSERT with ax, ay on the control's centre (or the cursor tip), sx, sy at frame centre or on a third, and k = 2.0-2.5 for an on-axis punch or 3-4.5 for a macro insert. Switch on a whole frame, cam = fd(f) >= CUT ? INSERT : WIDE, and keep the cursor path, hover lift, typing and counters on their own clocks so they carry on mid-motion across the cut; place the cursor with toScreen() of the active shot. Never hold the insert still: give it a 1-2 px/f linear drift along the action's direction, or open it with a decaying offset (+8% of frame width, decayed on E.out over 96 f). Build the UI as live layout at its final size, never as an upscaled bitmap, so text stays sharp at k = 4.5, and cut back out on the next action or at the peak of an exit move.
techniques.timing: Wide holds 20-64 f before an on-axis punch (90-220 f when it establishes the scene). On-axis close-up about 60 f. Macro insert 46-74 f, up to 76-154 f when it carries an action. Scale 2.0-2.5 on-axis, 3-4.5 macro. Drift inside the insert 1-2 px/f linear (3-5 px/f for a 2.5x component slide). Cut on the click, keystroke or beat, with no transition frames. Chain 2-3 punches on consecutive beats for a staccato build.
techniques.use_when: Small UI actions that need hero weight (send, picking a date, a chip), long walkthroughs that need their visual scale reset, and a wide/close rhythm that keeps both context and legibility.
techniques.avoid_when: The UI doesn't hold up at 3-4.5x, or the close-up isn't obviously the same place (keep the cut on-axis or anchored to the cursor, or it reads as a jump).

techniques.name: Detail first, then pull back
techniques.summary: A shot opens tight on the one thing that matters (giant prompt words, a chart counting up, a status pill) with no chrome, then the camera pulls back to show it sitting in the full window.
techniques.recipe: Anchor on the hero element (ax, ay at its centre, or at the caret for typed words) and hold k = 1.6-1.7 while its value animates; for giant type, pan sx after the caret at 2-4 px/f. Then pull with cam = lc(TIGHT, CONTEXT, prog(f, a, a + 52, E.cam)), so the hero barely moves on screen while the frame widens around it, and fade out any partly cropped edge tiles over the 16 f before the pull so they don't pop at the frame edge. Bring the context in during the pull: window chrome and neighbouring panels fade 0 -> 1 over 30 f from 20% of the move, optionally behind <RackFocus t={1 - prog(f, a, a + 30, E.smooth)} blur={10}>. The hero card can tip pitch 0 -> 6 -> 0 deg and yaw 0 -> -4 -> 0 deg as it docks into its slot. For an end-of-film re-establish, open the tight frame soft (RackFocus t = 1, blur 6) and resolve it over the pull.
techniques.timing: Tight hold 24-52 f while the value animates. Pull k 1.6-1.7 -> 1.0 over 52 f on E.cam (peak about 4%/f at 27%), or a settle back over 56-80 f on E.out (half done by f10-12). Edge tiles out over 16 f before the pull, context in over 30 f, 3D tip peaking mid-move. Re-establish k 2.2 -> 1.0 with focus over 60 f on E.cam (peak about 5.6%/f).
techniques.use_when: Result reveals, analytics, prompts and input moments where the value should land before the load of the full UI; breaking up a repeated card formula; re-establishing the whole product after a run of close details.
techniques.avoid_when: The product hasn't been seen yet and the tight frame stays unrecognisable for long (keep the tight hold under 52 f), or the wider frame adds nothing new.

techniques.name: Hero push with a 3D turn
techniques.summary: From a wide view of the whole app, one continuous move pushes 2.5x into a single panel while yawing, so the panel turns toward the viewer and an empty side of the frame opens for the caption.
techniques.recipe: Build one scene on one world container with two Shots: WIDE (k = 1, flat) and HERO, with ax, ay on the panel centre, sx at 0.67 x width (0.33 for a panel on the left), k = 2.56, yaw 24-30 deg and pitch about 5 deg, rendered through camera(shot, 2400). Blend with lc(WIDE, HERO, prog(f, a, a + 60, E.smooth)); k already lerps in log space, so the push keeps an even perceived speed. Start the caption in the void at a + 45 (the last 25% of the move) so the word reveal and the camera settle read as one gesture, then keep the hold alive with breath(prog(f, a + 60, next, E.linear), 0.025) instead of a dead lock. Check that the panel's smallest meaningful text is at least 22 px on screen at k = 2.56, and render with --blur for the peak.
techniques.timing: 60 f on E.smooth, 10-90% of progress between 29% and 71% of the move, peak about 4.5%/f scale (around 47 px/f on screen) at 50%. Zoom 1 -> 2.56; yaw 0 -> 24-30 deg and pitch 0 -> 5 deg on the same curve. Caption starts at 75% of the move. Hold breath +2.5%.
techniques.use_when: The film's energy peak: the one feature that needs both spatial orientation and close-up legibility, or a scene change inside a single-take film.
techniques.avoid_when: More than once per film, or on a lone card with no surrounding app (the turn needs a world to orient against). Keep each act on its own rotation axis.

techniques.name: Dolly surge with a foreground pass
techniques.summary: The camera surges from a wide shot into a 3x medium close-up, with most of the travel in half a second, and at the fastest moment a near object rushes past the lens before a long, slow creep.
techniques.recipe: Animate k = lmix(1, 3.1, prog(f, a, a + 67, E.smooth)) around the subject (or translateZ of a preserve-3d stage under perspective 2400px), multiplied by lmix(1, 1.04, prog(f, a + 47, a + 107, E.linear)) so the +4% creep starts 20 f before the push ends and the motion never stalls. Put one foreground object on its own layer above the world, 300-400 px off the anchor, and project it with a stronger scale, kFg = k ** 1.6 (screen position = sx + (p - ax) * kFg), so it grows and slides out past the frame edge around the push's peak frame (about a + 33); keep its crossing at 60-80 px/f or less.
