The motion-blur pass (--blur) streaks it, so never fake the streak with a CSS blur. Optional mid and far layers at 1.0x and 0.3x of the camera's translation add parallax.
techniques.timing: Push 67 f on E.smooth, zoom 1 -> 3.1, 10-90% of the travel in about 28 f, peak about 4.8%/f near a + 33. Creep +4% over 60 f on E.linear from a + 47. Foreground exits on the peak at 60-80 px/f or less, smeared by the blur pass.
techniques.use_when: Opening a launch film into a 3D or layered world, or a sting that dives from an overview into the hero object.
techniques.avoid_when: Flat UI with no depth layers (nothing to pass the lens), or calm walkthroughs.

techniques.name: Push-in with a roll swing
techniques.summary: The camera dives into one corner of the UI, rolls a few degrees off level mid-dive like a hand-steered move, and rolls back to level as it lands.
techniques.recipe: Blend lc(WIDE, TARGET, t) with t = prog(f, a, a + 60, E.smooth), where TARGET has ax, ay on the corner element, sx, sy at that element's current screen point (so it stays put while the frame grows around it) and k = 2.09 x WIDE.k. Add the roll on its own curve: roll = t < 0.57 ? mix(0, -4, E.smooth(t / 0.57)) : mix(-4, -0.3, E.smooth((t - 0.57) / 0.43)), passed as the Shot's roll so camera() keeps it rigid outside any tilt. For a tilted landing, ease pitch 0 -> 8 deg over the last 24 f. Keep |roll| under 11 deg.
techniques.timing: 60 f; zoom 1 -> 2.09 on E.smooth in log space, peak about 3.5%/f mid-move. Roll 0 -> -4 deg by 57% of the move, back to -0.3 deg at the end, each segment E.smooth. Optional pitch 0 -> 8 deg over the last 24 f.
techniques.use_when: A push that would otherwise feel mechanical: diving into a settings corner, a sidebar or a detail panel.
techniques.avoid_when: Next to another rolled or tilted move in the same act (one rotation axis per act), or on moves shorter than 40 f, where the roll reads as a wobble.

techniques.name: Isolating push into one item
techniques.summary: The camera pushes into one row, card or column while everything around it fades, dims or slides off the edges, picking a single thread out of a busy layout.
techniques.recipe: Anchor the push on the chosen item and pick a preset. Dive: k x lmix(1, 4, prog(f, a, a + 80, E.smooth)) while sibling rows fade from 1 to 0 opacity over 20 f from a; as the push ends, the item's icon dims to 0.3 and the next state swaps in on a whole frame (fd), a zoom-through without a cut. Accelerate-through: k x lmix(1, 1.25, prog(f, a, a + 60, E.in)) while the surroundings fade to the background colour over 16 f, then cut or swap on the peak frame. Eject: k x lmix(1, 1.48, prog(f, a, a + 30, E.smooth)) and then +4% over 60 f on E.linear, the flanking words taking blurOut text blur up to 6 px once they pass 80% of the half-width on their way off frame. Gentle focus: wrap the side columns in RackFocus (t 0 -> 1, blur 8) and dim them to 0.6 opacity while the parent pushes x1.06 over 18 f on E.smooth.
techniques.timing: Dive 80 f, x4 on E.smooth (peak about 5%/f), sibling fades 20 f, swap on the last frame. Accelerate-through 60 f, x1.25 on E.in, surround fade 16 f. Eject 30 f, x1.48 on E.smooth, then +4% over 60 f. Focus pull 18 f, x1.06, blur 8 px, opacity 0.6, running straight into the next move.
techniques.use_when: Choosing one result from a list of parallel processes, moving from a typographic act into a UI close-up without a cut, or steering the eye to where the next action will happen.
techniques.avoid_when: The item is still too small to read at 4x, or the surrounding layout carries information the viewer still needs.

techniques.name: Reactive reframe
techniques.summary: When something new appears (a popover, a result, the hero icon), the camera glides a few hundred pixels and pushes in slightly until it sits where the eye wants it.
techniques.recipe: On the event cue c, blend from the current camera into a reframed Shot: cam = lc(CURRENT, REFRAMED, prog(f, c + 4, c + 4 + N, E.glide)). REFRAMED puts ax, ay on the new element's centre and sx, sy at frame centre (or offset to leave room for its caption), with k = CURRENT.k x 1.05-1.23. Starting 4 f after the element begins to appear lets the content lead and the camera follow. The element arrives on its own curve; a popover, for example, scales 0.05 -> 1 from the click point over 10 f on E.out, its opacity rising over the first 4 f. To centre a hero after a punch-in, use the same blend over 22 f with position and k on one curve, so the subject arrives on a long tail.
techniques.timing: Popover reframe: starts 4 f after the pop, settles in 20-40 f on E.glide, k x1.05. Hero centring: 22 f on E.glide, 150-350 px of travel, peak about 22 px/f at 31% of the move, k 1.0 -> 1.23.
techniques.use_when: After any UI event that changes what matters on screen, or after a punch-in that left the hero off-centre.
techniques.avoid_when: Every small UI change (keep it for the ones that matter), or an element that already appears near frame centre (a move under 40 px reads as a twitch).

techniques.name: Pull-back that lands an event
techniques.summary: A long, gentle pull-back runs from a close-up to the full view, and as it decelerates the next UI event (a modal, labels, a caption) starts, so it lands together with the camera's settle.
techniques.recipe: Pull with lc(CLOSE, WIDE, prog(f, a, a + 108, E.smooth)), where WIDE.k is about 0.56 x CLOSE.k. Start the event at a + round(0.72 x 108) = a + 78. A modal arrives on SPR.firm from 0.92 to 1 scale, opacity up over 8 f, landing within 4 f of a + 108. Captions start no earlier than a + 81 (the last 25% of the move) and no later than a + 114, while labels and values can type in through the whole pull. After the settle, hand over to a breath creep instead of a dead lock.
techniques.timing: 108 f on E.smooth, zoom x0.56, peak about 1.5%/f (about 24 px/f) mid-move. Event starts at 72% of the move; the SPR.firm modal settles within 4 f of the camera. Captions start in the last 25% of the move or up to 6 f after it.
techniques.use_when: Walkthroughs and single-take films that move pose to pose, and any long move whose ending would otherwise be a dead beat.
techniques.avoid_when: Short or fast moves under 50 f, where an event in the tail just competes with the motion, and the finale, where the lockup needs a clean frame.

techniques.name: Cursor-led whip orbit
techniques.summary: Following a cursor that leads the way to the next panel, the camera swings fast across the product, yawing to show the slab's thick edge and rolling slightly.
techniques.recipe: Keyframe A (the current pose) and B, with ax, ay on the destination panel, yaw about +24 deg, roll about -10 deg and k = 0.77 x A.k, and blend lc(A, B, prog(f, a, a + 74, E.whip)) through camera(shot, 2400). Move the cursor in screen space along cursorArc(start, dest, prog(f, a - 5, a + 69, E.whip), 0.2), so it leads the camera by about 5 f and seems to drag it, projecting its destination with the same transform maths. Give the world container a 24-40 px side face (a darker tone of the surface, hinged on the right edge with rotateY(90deg)) so the yaw reveals the product's thickness. Render with --blur, since the peak is near 47 px/f.
techniques.timing: 74 f on E.whip, peak about 47 px/f at around 40% of the move. Yaw 0 -> 24 deg, roll 0 -> -10 deg, zoom x0.77. The cursor leads by 4-6 f.
techniques.use_when: Moving between two distant panels of one product in a single-take or walkthrough film, where a cut would lose the spatial relationship.
techniques.avoid_when: There is no cursor or other lead to motivate it (an unmotivated whip reads as a flourish), or the act already uses yaw for something else.

techniques.name: Off-frame whip relay
techniques.summary: The cursor accelerates up and out of frame, the camera whips down the product while it's hidden, and the cursor re-enters from the top as a fast streak that brakes onto its target.
techniques.recipe: Three overlapping keyed parts. Cursor exit: y on E.in toward -10% of the frame height from a to a + 24, after which it stays off screen for 12 f. Camera: sy travels the product distance D (900-1400 px) on E.smooth over N = 2.86 x D / 75 frames (34-54 f), centred on a + 30 so its fastest stretch falls inside the hidden window and peaks at about 75 px/f. Cursor entry: from -10% to the target over 36 f from a + 36 on E.out, entering at about 63 px/f; while it moves faster than 12 px/f, draw a trailing rounded capsule behind the tip, 0.6 x speed long at 40% opacity, and let the blur pass handle the camera.
techniques.timing: Cursor exit 24 f on E.in (2.5 -> 15 px/f). Off screen 12 f. Camera 34-54 f on E.smooth centred on the hidden window, peak 60-75 px/f. Cursor re-enters at about 63 px/f and brakes over 36 f on E.out (speed ratio about 0.92 per frame).
techniques.use_when: A big spatial jump within one product (top bar to bottom bar, one page to another) that should feel like a match-on-action without a cut.
techniques.avoid_when: Films without a cursor, or destinations less than about one frame height away (a plain reframe is enough).

techniques.name: Follow the lead dot
techniques.summary: A small lead (a progress dot, a travelling packet, a drawing line's head) moves through the layout and the camera follows it with a soft lag, never quite stopping, so the viewer always knows where to look.
techniques.recipe: Make the follow a pure function of the frame: loop i from the shot's first frame to f, updating c += (lead(i) - target - c) * 0.08 (target is the lead's desired screen position, for example 40% of the frame height), plus a constant 2 px/f drift in the direction of travel; never keep state between renders. Feed c into the anchor camera (ax, ay on the lead's world point) and draw the lead as a flat dot in the one accent colour with no halo. Reveal each step row as the lead passes it: opacity prog(f, tPass, tPass + 12, E.smooth) with a 12 px rise through arrive(). At a corner, let the lead turn first and the camera's lag carry the turn; at the destination, punch in (cam-punch-in-insert) or ease to rest on E.rest.
techniques.timing: Lag coefficient 0.08 per frame (time constant about 12 f). Peak 12.5 px/f, residual drift 2-2.5 px/f, never 0. Step rows reveal over 12 f as the lead passes. Bumps between steps about 40 f.
techniques.use_when: Agent progress, pipelines, timelines and journeys across a map: any story told by one thing moving through a layout.
techniques.avoid_when: The lead moves faster than about 20 px/f for long stretches (the lag lets it escape the frame), or the whole layout fits in one framing.

techniques.name: Crane down with a delayed push
techniques.summary: The camera tilts down the page past the chart to the detail cards while a slow push-in builds behind it, as if the operator were leaning in to read.
techniques.recipe: Sum two vertical components on the anchor camera's sy: a main move of about 240 px on prog(f, a, a + 64, E.smooth), and a 300 px drift on prog(f, a + 40, a + 220, E.rest) that overlaps it, so the motion never stalls and fades out slowly. Multiply k by lmix(1, 1.22, prog(f, a + 40, a + 240, E.rest)) so the push starts 40 f late and peaks while the tilt is decelerating. Put ax on the column the viewer will read so the push doesn't drift sideways.
techniques.timing: Main tilt 64 f on E.smooth, about 240 px, peak about 10 px/f mid-move. Drift 300 px from a + 40 to a + 220 on E.rest (peaks near 5.8 px/f, under 0.5 px/f by the end). Push +22% from a + 40 to a + 240 on E.rest, peak about +0.35%/f near a + 98.
techniques.use_when: Moving down a long page or dashboard from the overview to the detail that matters.
techniques.avoid_when: Pages too short to travel 500 px or more, or vertical formats where the push crops the column.

techniques.name: Extrude then crash in
techniques.summary: An object grows toward camera (a disc extruding into a tall cylinder) and the camera slams into it, hard-cutting to its interior while still rushing forward.
techniques.recipe: Extrude first: the object's scaleY goes 1 -> 2.5 over 12 f on E.in, with transform-origin at its base, so it accelerates toward camera. Overlapping the last 8 f of the extrusion, push the anchor camera into its face with k = k0 * Math.exp(0.64 * ((f - s) / 24) ** 3) over 24 f, then hard-cut on the last frame to the interior shot. Open the interior already moving: k starts at 1.76x its rest value and lmix-decays over 40 f on E.outSoft, while the tube walls converge on a vanishing point. Draw the walls as two or three flat, crisp-edged steps of the object's own colour (darker at the rim, lighter toward the vanishing point), with no bloom, halo or bright blurred edges. Render with --blur so the frames either side of the cut streak; spreading the crash across the cut keeps the frame edge under about 80 px/f.
techniques.timing: Extrusion 12 f on E.in. Camera push 24 f on a cubic ease-in, x1.9, reaching about 8%/f (about 77 px/f at the frame edge) on the cut frame. Interior entry x1.76 -> rest over 40 f on E.outSoft.
techniques.use_when: A violent spatial jump into the product at the energy peak of a launch film or sting.
techniques.avoid_when: Calm films, any second use in the same film, and readable text on either side of the cut.

techniques.name: Directional impact kick
techniques.summary: On a true impact (a card landing, a lock-in, a slam) the whole frame jolts a few pixels in the direction of the hit and pushes a hair closer, then settles within a fifth of a second.
techniques.recipe: On the impact cue c, add a decaying jolt to the anchor camera: sx += dir.x * 8 * hitPulse(f - c, 1, 4) and sy += dir.y * 8 * hitPulse(f - c, 1, 4), where dir is the unit vector of the incoming object's travel, and multiply k by 1 + 0.015 * hitPulse(f - c, 2, 5). Take c from the contact frame in src/lib/sync.ts so sound and picture peak together, pair it with squash() on the landing object, and never add roll. Use it at most 2-3 times per film, and only where something truly lands.
techniques.timing: Jolt 6-10 px, attack 1 f, tau 4 f (gone in about 25 f). Push +1.5%, attack 2 f, tau 5 f. At most 2-3 per film.
techniques.use_when: True landings and lock-ins: a heavy object slamming into a slot, or a statement locking together on a hit.
techniques.avoid_when: Every beat or tick (that makes a shake, not a hit), soft UI arrivals, or mid camera move (it fights the move's ease).

techniques.name: Layered parallax truck
techniques.summary: The camera trucks sideways across a scene split into two or three depth planes: the background barely moves, the subject moves with the camera and a near element slides past faster, so a flat layout reads as space.
techniques.recipe: Split the world into at most three layers in one AbsoluteFill (background, subject and an optional foreground), each with its own transform, and drive a single camera translation x = D * prog(f, a, a + N, E.cam), or a constant 1-3 px/f drift for a hold. Apply it at 0.3x to the background, 1.0x to the subject and 1.6x to the foreground, and scale the background to 1.08 so its slower travel never reveals an edge. Keep the subject's readable text under 20 px/f and let the text-free foreground carry the fast motion, which the blur pass smears above 12 px/f.
techniques.timing: Truck 200-400 px over 90-120 f on E.cam (subject peak about 12 px/f for 300 px over 105 f), or a 1-3 px/f drift. Plane factors 0.3 / 1.0 / 1.6. Background overscan 5-8%.
techniques.use_when: Hero product shots and feature cards that need depth without 3D, and slow establishing moves.
techniques.avoid_when: Dense UI walkthroughs where the eye has to track one control, or any scene with more than three planes (it starts to look like a parallax demo).

techniques.name: Seamless loop drift
techniques.summary: In a looping clip the camera drifts along a slow, closed figure-eight (a little sideways, a little up, breathing in and out) and returns exactly to its first frame, so the loop has no seam.
techniques.recipe: With L the loop length in frames and u = 2 * Math.PI * f / L, set sx = sx0 + 32 * Math.sin(u), sy = sy0 + 12 * Math.sin(2 * u) and k = k0 * Math.exp(0.03 * Math.sin(u + 1.2)) on the anchor camera, plus yaw = 3 * Math.sin(u) deg for a 3D product. Every term completes a whole number of cycles in L, so frame L equals frame 0 exactly and the motion never stops (the speed peaks around 0.6 px/f at L = 360). Time the content's own loop to L or a divisor of it.
techniques.timing: Loop L = 240-480 f. Amplitudes 24-40 px sideways and 10-16 px vertically (at twice the frequency), zoom +-3%, yaw +-3 deg. Peak speed about 0.5-0.8 px/f.
techniques.use_when: Feature loops, background clips and vertical loops that replay endlessly.
techniques.avoid_when: Linear films with cuts (use a living hold instead), or loops shorter than about 4 s, where the drift turns into a visible wobble.

techniques.name: Pull out from inside the object
techniques.summary: The shot opens on what reads as a full-bleed colour field or a statement card, and one long pull reveals it was the face of a small object (an app icon, a card, a screen, the mark) sitting among its neighbours.
techniques.recipe: Lay the object out at true size inside its real context (a dock, a grid, a window, the lockup) in the anchor camera's world, with its face, corner radius and shadow as live layout in world units, never a bitmap. Shot FACE puts ax, ay on the object's centre at frame centre with k0 = 1.04 x max(W / objectW, H / objectH), so its edges sit just outside the frame (about 13.3 for a 144 px icon at 1920 wide), and Shot CONTEXT frames the object at k = 1 in its slot. Blend cam = lc(FACE, CONTEXT, prog(f, a, a + N, E.dolly)) with N = 25.7 x ln(k0); this caps the log zoom rate at about 6%/f mid-move, so anything entering at the frame corner moves under about 66 px/f, and the corners, the shadow and the neighbours arrive purely by coverage, with no fades of their own. Draw the opening copy on a screen-space overlay at toScreen(cam, centre), scaled by (cam.k / k0) ** 0.46 so it shrinks more slowly than the object, and fade it out on E.smooth while the object's on-screen width falls from 1.3x to 1.0x the copy's width, so it never spills past the edges. Read the face under a cam-living-hold creep before the pull, land with no overshoot, and start the next beat (an icon hop, a wordmark build) within 12 f of the settle.
techniques.timing: Face hold 24-48 f for the read, with a 0.04-0.07%/f creep. Pull from k0 = 8-14 to 1 over N = 25.7 x ln(k0) frames on E.dolly (about 53 f from 8x, 66 f from 13.3x), log rate peaking near 6%/f mid-move and landing at rest. Copy scale tracks k ** 0.46 and fades over the 8-14 f in which the object's width passes 1.3x -> 1.0x the copy width. Anchor travel to the slot under 10 px/f. --blur for frames above 12 px/f.
techniques.use_when: Cold opens and hooks where a calm statement or a colour field should turn out to be part of the product (the question was printed on the app icon, the colour was one card in the grid); landing the mark into the final lockup; any reveal whose point is scale.
techniques.avoid_when: The face is a photo or bitmap (it falls apart at 8-14x), the context it lands in is not recognisable at a glance, or a scale-through cut or detail-first pull-back has already used the same object. Once per film.

techniques.name: Fly-through of a depth field
techniques.summary: Dozens of flat screens or tokens float at different depths and the camera travels forward through them: near ones swell and slide off the frame edges, far ones barely drift, until the move lands square on one hero screen.
techniques.recipe: Seed 24-36 items with rand(i): x within +-2200 px, y within +-1300 px, z from 800 to 6000 px ahead of the start, keeping a 420 x 260 px corridor around the camera's path empty so nothing hits the lens head-on, and place the hero at (0, 0, Zh), sized in world px at the size it should read. Project each item yourself rather than through preserve-3d: with F = 1200 and d = z - camZ(f), draw it as a flat layer at translate(W/2 + (x - camX) x F/d, H/2 + (y - camY) x F/d) scale(F/d), z-ordered far to near, and unmount it once d < 300. Multiply each item's opacity by a far fade-in (0 -> 1 as d falls from 6000 to 4800) and by a speed gate, clamp((70 - v) / 20), where v is its screen travel since f - 1 (project it again with camZ(f - 1)), so whatever rushes past the lens dissolves instead of breaking the speed cap; sink distant items into the stage with an overlay of the stage colour at 0.5 x clamp((d - 1200) / 4000) instead of blurring 30 layers. For the dive, camZ = (Zh - F) x prog(f, a, a + N, E.cam) lands the hero at exactly scale 1, sharp and readable; for a breadth drift that ends in a cut, pull back 1200 px on E.out, cruise forward at 4 px/f with camY sinking 1.5 px/f, then ramp out over the last 18-24 f on E.contact and hard-cut on the fastest frame (tr-velocity-handoff-cut). Tokens may also turn slowly on rotateY (up to 10 deg/s each), and the whole move renders with --blur.
techniques.timing: Dive: 150-180 f on E.cam through 4,000 px of depth (Zh = 5200, F = 1200), landing the hero at scale 1 on the long settle. Drift: pull-back 40 f on E.out, cruise 90-120 f, exit ramp 18-24 f. Speed gate between 50 and 70 px/f; far fade over 1,200 px of depth; about 12-16 items on screen at once. The hero's copy starts once it moves under 20 px/f.
techniques.use_when: Proving breadth (a whole platform, hundreds of templates, every integration) in 3-4 s without explaining any single screen; opening into a layered world; arriving on the one screen the next act is about.
techniques.avoid_when: Items must be read in flight, there are fewer than about 15 of them (the field looks sparse), the film is flat with no depth language, or lc-swarm-cluster-burst already spends the film's breadth crescendo.

techniques.name: Fit-to-content follow
techniques.summary: As a route, graph or plan builds, the camera widens just enough to keep every piece that matters in frame, so the shot opens close on the first node and ends on the whole structure.
techniques.recipe: Each frame, collect the world boxes that must stay visible: the origin, every item revealed so far (with its half-size) and the travelling head if there is one, its box stretched ahead along its direction of travel by 18% of the frame converted to world px at the current k. Turn their bounding box plus a 12% frame margin into a target shot: ax, ay at the box centre, sx, sy at frame centre (or shifted off the caption band), and k = min((W - 2 x SAFE.x) / boxW, (H - 2 x SAFE.y) / boxH), clamped between the opening k and a floor that keeps the smallest label at TYPE.ui size (24 px) on screen; when the floor binds, let the oldest items leave the frame rather than shrinking type. Smooth it as a pure function of the frame: loop i from the shot's first frame to f, keep lnT = min(lnT, ln kTarget(i)) so the zoom never pumps back in while the set grows, and step c += (target - c) x 0.07 for ax, ay and ln k, clamping each step to 1.2% of zoom and 12 px of screen travel, then feed exp(c.lnk) to the anchor camera so the widening keeps an even pace in log space. When the structure is complete, either hold the full fit as the payoff under a cam-living-hold pull or punch in on the destination with lc(FOLLOW, DEST, prog(f, e, e + 54, E.cam)).
techniques.timing: Follow coefficient 0.06-0.08 per frame (time constant 12-16 f); zoom at most 1.2%/f, centre at most 12 px/f on screen (--blur if the corners ever pass 12 px/f). Margin 12% of the frame, 18% lead on the head's side. Nodes 20-40 f apart give a steady widening rather than steps. Closing punch-in 48-60 f on E.cam, or a hold with a -0.08%/f pull.
techniques.use_when: Pipelines, agent plans, org charts, dependency or network graphs and routes that build piece by piece, where the first node needs close-up legibility and the payoff is the whole shape.
techniques.avoid_when: The finished structure already fits one comfortable framing, a single moving lead is the whole story (cam-lead-follow), or the full structure cannot fit with 24 px labels (split it into chapters with cuts instead).

techniques.name: Zoom-out hop between areas
techniques.summary: To travel between two distant parts of one product, the camera eases back as it sets off, crosses at a wider framing that shows where it is going, and pushes back in as it arrives.
techniques.recipe: Keyframe Shots A and B at the same k on the two areas, blend cam = lc(A, B, prog(f, a, a + N, E.smooth)), then multiply cam.k by dip(prog(f, a, a + N, E.linear), depth) from src/lib/camera.ts. Driving the dip on linear time instead of on the pan's eased progress is the point: the pull-back starts before the pan gathers speed and the push-in finishes after it slows, so the widest framing coincides with the fastest travel and the frame edge peaks 28-40% lower than the same pan without the hop. Set depth = clamp(1 - 0.7 x W / (A.k x D), 0.15, 0.45), where D is the world distance between the anchors, so both areas share the frame at mid-move, and size N = A.k x D / 34 frames at depth 0.45 (A.k x D / 25 for a shallow 0.15-0.25 hop, interpolated between) to keep the edge under about 60 px/f. Start B's caption in the last 25% of the move and render with --blur.
techniques.timing: Pan on E.smooth over N = A.k x D / 34 f at depth 0.45, or A.k x D / 25 at 0.15-0.25: about 76 f for 2,600 px at k = 1, 106 f for 1,800 px at k = 2, 72 f for 1,800 px at k = 1. Dip on linear time, depth 0.15-0.45, its zoom rate peaking at 1-2.6%/f a quarter of the way in and out. Frame edge at most about 60 px/f. Beyond about 120 f, cut instead (cam-offframe-whip-relay or cam-punch-in-insert).
techniques.use_when: Single-take and walkthrough films moving between two areas of one surface more than about a frame width apart (sidebar to canvas, one dashboard panel to another), where the viewer should see how they relate.
techniques.avoid_when: Areas less than about a frame width apart (cam-reframe-to-subject), a cursor that should lead the move (cam-cursor-whip-orbit), or a wide view that is cluttered or unfinished, since the hop shows it.

techniques.name: Phrase clamp at a junction
techniques.summary: Two halves of a phrase arrive from opposite directions and lock on one baseline at a fixed junction, like a clamp closing.
techniques.recipe: Fix a junction (x about 48% of the frame, on the shared baseline): the first half is right-aligned to it and the second half left-aligned, both measured with measureTracked so the junction gap is exactly one word space. Vertical default: hold the first half alone for 1 f at +64 px (the pre-pose), then translateY +64 -> 0 on arrive(p), p = prog(f, s, s + 18, E.out), while each word of the second half drops -40 -> 0 the same way, word i starting at s + 2i; give every piece opacity 0 -> 1 over 3 f and blurIn(p, 8), because frame 1 moves about 20 px/f. Horizontal snap: the line cuts in at full strength with each half 35 px out from the junction, closes to 0.75 of the word space over 10 f on E.out, then eases back to the true gap over 18 f on E.outSoft (the one designed undershoot, never closing the space); calm variant: a 1.7x gap closes to 1x over 80 f on E.outSoft. Put the lock on a beat and give it one 1.5% scale punch with hitPulse(t, 1, 4).
techniques.timing: Vertical: 18 f E.out, 64 px and 40 px travel (peak 19.7 and 12.3 px/f on frame 1), 2 f word stagger, 1 f pre-pose, opacity 3 f. Snap: 35 px per side over 10 f E.out (about 20 px/f on frame 1) to 0.75 of the gap, back over 18 f E.outSoft. Calm close: 80 f E.outSoft. Hold the locked line at least 54 f with a 0.3 px/f drift.
techniques.use_when: A two-part claim whose halves mean more together (subject + promise, problem + fix); the payoff line; a junction that a slot roller will reuse.
techniques.avoid_when: Lines over 5 words or halves of very unequal length; more than once per film; the end lockup.

techniques.name: Slot roller beside a fixed phrase
techniques.summary: A fixed phrase holds still while the word in its slot rolls through alternatives one line at a time, speeding up until the last one lands.
techniques.recipe: The fixed phrase sits in its own layer and never moves; the slot is a column of alternatives aligned to the junction, line pitch 1.5x the font size, translated by -index x pitch and cut by a feathered mask-image (transparent beyond +-1.2 pitch, opaque within +-0.5 pitch) so neighbours show only as slivers. Each step rolls on E.whip over 20 f (peak about 0.18 x pitch per frame, 12 px/f at a 68 px pitch); above a 110 px pitch, stretch the step to 0.18 x pitch frames so the rolling word stays at or under 20 px/f; the row on the junction baseline is ink and every other row is C.mute at no more than 1.3:1 contrast, flipped binary when |rowY - baselineY| < pitch/2 (no colour tween). For a run of 5 or more items, accelerate: intervals 26, 14, 12, 8, 8, 4, 4 f, where intervals under 12 f are whole-frame swaps chosen by fd(f) with no tween, the final item rolls home on SPR.detent, and every step gets a tick. For a loop, make the last item equal the first and wrap the index modulo the list.
techniques.timing: Step 20 f E.whip (0.18 x pitch frames above a 110 px pitch) every 29-34 f (0.48-0.57 s), 3 steps, then a 28 f hold before the cut. Accelerating run: 26/14/12/8/8/4/4 f (7 items in 76 f), last item on SPR.detent (home in about 9 f), held at least 54 f under a 0.3 px/f line drift. Pitch 1.5x the font size; ticks at least 3 f apart.
techniques.use_when: One sentence frame that fits many subjects or capabilities; listing use-cases without spending screen time; a feature loop that cycles items.
techniques.avoid_when: Items of very different widths in a centred layout (the fixed phrase would have to move); more than about 7 items; any mask loose enough that the neighbours read as a list.

techniques.name: Masked baseline rise
techniques.summary: Each word rises out of an invisible line at its own baseline, tops of the glyphs first, as if cut out of the layout.
techniques.recipe: Wrap each word in an inline-block with overflow:hidden and padding-bottom 0.15 em (room for descenders); the inner span goes translateY 110% -> 0 on arrive(p), p = prog(f, s_i, s_i + 12, E.out), s_i = start + 6i, with opacity 0 -> 1 linear over the first 3 f, because frame 1 moves about 57 px/f and must be streaked by the blurred master (render.sh --blur). Optional ink resolve: color = mixColor(C.mute, C.ink, prog(f, s_i, s_i + 10, E.linear)). For one short hero word, run it per letter with a 3 f stagger, or drop the letters unmasked from -0.25 em over 8 f, 4 f apart, so a small word falls into place. Exit back into the same mask (translateY 0 -> -110% on depart(q), q on E.in over 10 f) or with ty-reading-order-exit.
techniques.timing: Per word 12 f E.out (10-14 f), travel 110% of the line box (about 132 px at 120 px type): 57, 34, 18 px/f on frames 1-3; opacity 3 f; stagger 6 f (4-10); per letter 3 f stagger; letter drop 0.25 em over 8 f, 4 f apart; mask exit 10 f E.in.
techniques.use_when: Editorial headlines and in-UI headings that must land fast (a 3-word line in under 0.5 s) without stealing focus; titles that build while the plane or camera is still moving.
techniques.avoid_when: Tight leading where the mask would clip the line above; a calm voice-paced read (use ty-blur-focus-word-rise); per-letter runs on anything but one short hero word.

techniques.name: Blur-to-focus word rise
techniques.summary: Words materialise one per beat out of a soft blur, rising a few pixels and darkening to full ink as they sharpen.
techniques.recipe: Use src/fx/Words.tsx with stagger 20, dur 28, rise 0.11 (em) and blur 8: each word fades in, rises through arrive(p) and sharpens through blurIn(p, 8), so the blur is gone by frame 4 while the word is still moving and half transparent. Pass wordStyle to resolve colour as well: color = mixColor(C.mist, C.ink, p) on paper (C.mute -> C.white on ink), so a word reads pale and soft first, crisp and dark on landing. Give the whole line a 0.5 px/f translateX drift on E.linear so it never freezes, and start the first word while the camera is still decelerating so reveal and settle read as one gesture. For a URL, start the path segment 8-12 f after the domain.
techniques.timing: Per word 28 f E.out; opacity 8 f; blur 8 -> 0 px, clear by frame 4; rise 13 px at 120 px type (peak about 3 px/f); stagger 20-22 f (one word per beat at 160-180 BPM); line drift 0.5 px/f.
techniques.use_when: Calm, premium statements that keep pace with a voice-over or a slow bed; the opening line of a quiet film; light grounds.
techniques.avoid_when: High-energy acts or dense beats (the stagger is too slow); pale type on a pale ground (under 4.5:1); any blur left on readable text for more than 6 f.

techniques.name: In-place word light-up on beats
techniques.summary: The finished line is laid out from the start and its words light up in place, chunk by chunk on the beat, with the last word held back.
techniques.recipe: Lay out the final centred line once; every word is a span at its final position with opacity 0, so nothing ever reflows. Group the words into 2-3 chunks that start on beat frames, 6 f apart within a chunk; each word's opacity is tw(f, s, s + 5, 0, 0.75, E.linear) then rises to 1 over the next 40 f on E.outSoft (fast attack, slow brightening tail). Hierarchy without a second colour: keywords at weight 600, connectors at 400 held at 0.55 until the last chunk lands and then raised to 1 over 12 f; the final word or qualifier arrives a full beat late, and a qualifier may sit tucked under the line's right edge at 0.35x size. Across a film, shorten the per-word stagger from 24 f on the title to about 6 f on later captions, because viewers learn the pattern; exit the whole line at once.
techniques.timing: Attack 5 f to 0.75, tail 40 f E.outSoft to 1; 6 f within a chunk, chunks on beats; last token +24-34 f; connectors 0.55 -> 1 over 12 f; title stagger 24 f shrinking to 5-6 f; exit all words together over 26 f E.smooth. If the camera is locked, add a 0.3 px/f line drift.
techniques.use_when: Titles and walkthrough captions over a moving camera; lines with an inline glyph or partner wordmark that must not shift; music-led films where each chunk can sit on a beat.
techniques.avoid_when: High-energy acts that need motion in the type itself; lines over 6 words (it turns into a slide).

techniques.name: Time-boxed eased type-on
techniques.summary: Text types in with most of the line appearing in the first few frames, and every line, short or long, finishes in the same musical length.
techniques.recipe: Visible count n = fd(N x prog(f, s, s + 68, E.out)) for prompts and headlines (45% of the string by frame 6, the last letters trickle in), or E.linear at 22-45 characters/s for small mono UI labels; pre-fill the first word so frame 1 already shows text, and pre-solve the layout (left-anchored in a fixed centred box, or a pill sized to the final string) so nothing reflows. The caret is a 0.08 em x 1 em bar that rides the text while typing and blinks at 1 Hz (30 f on, 30 f off, decided with fd) only after completion, and is gone before the hold ends. When the line outgrows 88% of the frame width, translate the container by min(0, 0.88W - caretX), eased over 8 f per character, and fade the head out through a mask-image over the left 25%. To replace a typed line, turn the whole string accent for 6 f, swap it on one frame and retype the new one in 26 f.
techniques.timing: Box 68 f per line whatever its length (26-32 f for a headline under 22 characters, 84 f for giant type); E.out count; mono labels E.linear 22-45 cps; caret blink 30/30 f after completion; caret-follow 8 f per character, head mask 25%; retype: 6 f accent, 1 f swap, 26 f retype. Hold at least 36 f + 6 f per word after the last glyph.
techniques.use_when: Prompts, search queries and names typed into the product; UI labels appearing while the camera trucks; keeping a run of typed beats on one musical length.
techniques.avoid_when: Statements nobody would type; keystroke clicks on every glyph (let the music carry it); letter-by-letter reveals of a name whose prefixes spell another word.

techniques.name: Re-centring line build
techniques.summary: Words or typed glyphs join a centred line one at a time while the whole line glides sideways so it is centred on every frame.
techniques.recipe: Measure the line at each state with measureTracked and set targets x_k = centreX - width_k / 2; drive the container as a sum of springs, x = x_0 + sum over k of (x_k - x_(k-1)) x spr(f, land_k, SPR.firm), which never overshoots and smooths away per-glyph steps when it follows typing. Each new word drops from -0.35 em (or rises from +0.2 em) into its slot on arrive(prog(f, land_k, land_k + 18, E.out)) with opacity 0 -> 1 over 6 f; after the last word keep a residual 0.3 px/f drift. Pre-solved alternative for short typed lines: lay out the final centred line, fade each character in over 5 f at 1.3 f apart, and glide the container +90 px -> 0 on prog(f, s, s + 24, E.out) so it lands centred with the last glyph. Optional: a single-hue pill behind the line whose width follows the measured width + 50 px on the same springs.
techniques.timing: A new word every 26-36 f (0.43-0.6 s); SPR.firm re-centre (peak about 7% of the shift per frame, 97% by 27 f), so shifts up to 280 px stay under 20 px/f; word drop 18 f E.out; pre-solved: 1.3 f per character, 5 f fade, 90 px glide over 24 f E.out; residual drift 0.3 px/f.
techniques.use_when: Speaking-pace builds, stat rows that widen as words arrive, centred typed headlines, any line whose final width is unknown while it builds.
techniques.avoid_when: Shifts over about 280 px per word (split the line instead); left-aligned layouts; a line that must keep an anchored element still (use ty-inplace-light-up-beats).

techniques.name: Staggered word roll
techniques.summary: The words of a phrase roll up and away one after another while their replacements rise in from below, so one sentence mutates instead of cutting.
techniques.recipe: For slot i, t_i = t0 + 10i. Out: q = prog(f, t_i, t_i + 12, E.in), translateY = -depart(q) x 0.2 em, opacity = 1 - prog(f, t_i, t_i + 12, E.smooth), blur = blurOut(q, 6). In, starting at t_i + 4 (a 4 f overlap): p = prog(f, t_i + 4, t_i + 28, E.out), translateY = (1 - arrive(p)) x 0.25 em, opacity 0 -> 1 over 10 f, blur = blurIn(p, 8). Keep any shared element (an icon pill, an unchanged word) perfectly still as the anchor, always roll in the same direction, and re-centre on SPR.firm when the new words change the width.
techniques.timing: Out 12 f E.in, 0.2 em up; in 24 f E.out from +0.25 em (peak about 7 px/f at 120 px type), 4 f overlap; stagger 6-11 f per word; a phrase swap takes about 50 f; a whole-line conveyor variant leaves exactly 1 empty frame between the lines.
techniques.use_when: Swapping one claim for the next in place; a URL replacing a tagline; a category word turning into the product name; a closing bookend that rolls the opening phrase into the brand line.
techniques.avoid_when: Swaps where nothing persists (a cut or ty-blur-swap-rescale reads cleaner); more than two rolls in a row without a different move between them.

techniques.name: Reading-order word exit
techniques.summary: Words leave one by one in reading order, each lifting a few pixels and vanishing, until only the hero element is left on screen.
techniques.recipe: For each word except the hero, o_i = out + 4i and q = prog(f, o_i, o_i + 10, E.in): translateY = -depart(q) x 0.12 em, opacity = 1 - prog(f, o_i, o_i + 10, E.smooth) (never fade on E.in, which pops), blur = blurOut(q, 4). The hero word, icon or pill stays put, and the next move (zoom, match cut) starts from it within 6 f of the last word clearing. Loosen variant for a calm handoff: words drift apart vertically by sign_i x (10 + 10 x rand(i)) px with a rotation of +-2 degrees, fade toward the ground colour first (mixColor(C.ink, C.mist)) and then to 0, over 20 f on E.smooth, 6 f apart.
techniques.timing: Per word 10 f, lift 0.12 em (about 14 px), stagger 4 f (2-6), a 5-word line clears in about 26 f; loosen variant 20 f per word, 6 f apart, about 32-44 f in all.
techniques.use_when: Isolating a hero word or object before a match cut or zoom; clearing a statement gently before a calmer UI moment; mirroring a word-by-word entry.
techniques.avoid_when: Walkthrough captions just before a camera move: fade the whole caption at once over 26 f on E.smooth and finish 0-56 f before the move starts; exits that would hurry a payoff line.

techniques.name: One-word slam sequence
techniques.summary: A line is read one huge word at a time: each word hits oversized and blurred, settles, then is sucked away as the next word cuts in.
techniques.recipe: Each word is its own card, fitted to about 77% of the frame width with fitSize. Entry: scale = lmix(1.35, 1, p), p = prog(f, cue - 1, cue + 21, E.outSoft), opacity 0 -> 1 over 3 f, blur = blurIn(p, 12), then a 6 f drift (scale x 1.01). Never start above 1.35x: a larger start leaves the outer letters of a frame-wide word moving faster than 20 px/f after the blur has cleared. Exit: scale x lmix(1, 0.6, q), q = prog(f, end - 14, end, E.in), opacity to 0 on E.smooth over the same window, then a hard cut to the next word on its slam's first frame, with every cut on an act boundary so the blurred master never smears two words together. Optional echo: two copies behind the word use the entry progress at f - 2 and f - 4, at 0.35 and 0.18 opacity, tinted 50% toward the ground, so they converge into the word by +12 f.
techniques.timing: Entry 22 f E.outSoft from 1.35x (the edges of a 1120 px word start at about 43 px/f, faded and blurred, and are near 22 px/f by frame 4 when the blur clears), blur 12 -> 0 by about frame 4, drift 6 f, exit 14 f E.in to 0.6x (last frame about 72 px/f, nearly transparent); 36-42 f per word (0.6-0.7 s), last word held at least 54 f under a 1-2% scale creep; every hit on a beat.
techniques.use_when: A punchy 3-5 word line on a strong beat; a problem statement or rhythmic claim; vertical formats where one word fills the screen.
techniques.avoid_when: More than one sequence per film; lines over 5 words; calm films; a card for a lone connector word (fold it into the next word).

techniques.name: Multi-direction slam assembly
techniques.summary: Each word of a short sentence flies in from a different side, oversized and streaked, and the sentence assembles on one baseline almost at once.
techniques.recipe: Lay out the final line and give each word a start offset from a different side (+-220 px in x, or +200 px in y) and a start scale of 1.4. Per word: p = prog(f, s + d_i, s + d_i + 20, E.out) with delays d = [0, 4, 10, 12, 16]; translate = offset x (1 - p) (vertical offsets through arrive), scale = lmix(1.4, 1, p), opacity 0 -> 1 over 5 f, so each word stays faint while it moves faster than 20 px/f and the blurred master streaks it along its own direction. One quiet piece may simply fade in over 8 f while the others fly; once the line is complete it drifts from scale 1 to 0.99 over 60 f.
techniques.timing: Per word 20 f E.out, 220 px travel (62, 47, 33, 23, 16 px/f on frames 1-5), scale 1.4 -> 1, opacity 5 f; delays 0/4/10/12/16 f; each word readable from about frame 5, the whole line resolved in about 36 f; then 1 -> 0.99 over 60 f.
techniques.use_when: Re-spiking energy after a calm, read-paced card; a payoff line that needs a burst; 3-5 short words.
techniques.avoid_when: Long words that would cross each other in flight; straight after another high-energy type move; calm films.

techniques.name: Oversize word slide-in
techniques.summary: A huge word arrives streaked from beside the frame and brakes on a long tail, and a trailing word follows from further out and closes the gap so the phrase locks together.
techniques.recipe: Type height 21-25% of the frame. Word 1: x = x_f + 0.4W x (1 - prog(f, s, s + 90, E.out)) - 0.5 x (f - s), a long braking tail on top of a slow drift that never stops, with opacity 0.2 -> 1 over the 16 f it takes to fall below 20 px/f, so it travels faded. Word 2 starts 16 f later with a larger offset (0.6W) on the same curve, so the gap between the words shrinks from about 1.7x to 1x over about 80 f, and its opacity rises 0.2 -> 1 over 68 f; letters may fade on left to right 2 f apart as each word slows. Frame 1 runs about 52 px/f (78 for word 2), so render the blurred master; blurIn(p, 10) stands in for the sharp preview.
techniques.timing: Brake 90 f E.out (feels like a 33 f time constant); word 1 offset 0.4W (768 px), word 2 0.6W from +16 f; drift 0.5 px/f; opacity from 0.2, readable below 20 px/f from frame 16 (word 2 from frame 21); gap 1.7x -> 1x over 80 f.
techniques.use_when: The energy peak of a type act; a two-word claim; a cold open whose first frame already moves.
techniques.avoid_when: Long phrases; when screen direction must run the other way across the cut; small type.

techniques.name: Blur-swap rescale
techniques.summary: A big word blurs out and instantly re-forms smaller as the start of the full line, so the type changes scale without a rubbery size tween.
techniques.recipe: Use two layers and never animate font-size. Old layer: q = prog(f, s, s + 6, E.in), blur = blurOut(q, 12), scale x lmix(1, 0.85, q), opacity to 0 on E.smooth over the same 6 f, still moving in its current direction. New layer from s + 2: p = prog(f, s + 2, s + 16, E.out), scale = lmix(1.25, 1, p), blur = blurIn(p, 12), opacity 0 -> 1 over 6 f; carry any ongoing drift so both layers travel at the same px/f. Optional tracking collapse on the new line: letter-spacing +0.25 em -> the token's tracking over 16 f on E.out, so the small word arrives spread wide and slams together.
techniques.timing: Old out 6 f (E.in, blurOut 12 px); new in 14 f from +2 f (E.out, blurIn 12 px, scale 1.25 -> 1, edges of a 1000 px line about 51 px/f on frame 1); 4 f overlap; typical cap-height change -35%; tracking collapse 16 f E.out.
techniques.use_when: Going from one or two giant words to the full readable sentence; right after tr-giant-word-punch-out; any big-to-small type handoff inside one continuous take.
techniques.avoid_when: As a default between unrelated lines (it is not a crossfade substitute); small-to-small swaps; overlaps longer than 10 f, which read as a dissolve.

techniques.name: Hard-step edits that act out the copy
techniques.summary: The headline does what it says with one-frame edits: broken words click straight one at a time, or words delete from the end faster and faster.
techniques.recipe: Give each word two states and pick one by fd(f) >= step_i, with no tween at all. Fix variant: broken states are per-letter rotation along an arc (letter j rotated (j - mid) x 6 degrees and raised (j - mid)^2 x 2 px), skewX(15deg) with translateY -0.17 em, or rotate(-20deg), drifting 0.5 px/f while broken; steps land at +6, +26 and +40 f after the cut, each with a 2% scale punch from hitPulse(t, 1, 4) on the fixed word. Delete variant: words.slice(0, n) with n dropping at accelerating intervals (10, 5, 5, 2 f), building pressure into the cut. Each step gets one click, each a little louder than the last.
techniques.timing: Snap 1 f, no tween; fix intervals 20 then 14 f; delete intervals 10/5/5/2 f; broken-state drift 0.5 px/f; click within 1 f of each step; hold the fixed line at least 42 f.
techniques.use_when: Copy about fixing, undoing, cleaning up or simplifying; a deadpan joke beat; a problem line that should visibly go away.
techniques.avoid_when: Copy the motion would contradict; calm films; more than one per film.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Keep only the rotation-based broken states (letters fanned along an arc, or the word rotated -20 deg) and drop the skewX(15deg) state, which fakes an italic; the one-frame steps, the 2% punches and the accelerating deletes stay as they are.

techniques.name: Shared-letter morph
techniques.summary: One word turns into another: the letters both words share stay and slide into place while the new letters tumble in and click upright.
techniques.recipe: Split both words into glyph spans at measured, kerned positions; map shared characters (same letter, nearest index) so they keep their element and slide to the new x on prog(f, s, s + 24, E.out), while unshared old glyphs fade out over 6 f and the word spaces collapse over 8 f. Each new glyph starts at an offset of +-150 px in x and +-120 px in y from rand(`g${i}`) with a rotation of 90-180 degrees and animates to rest on E.out over 24 f, opacity 0 -> 1 over the first 12 f so it stays faint while faster than 20 px/f, with start times spread over 56 f and the last glyph dropping from above. Check every frame on a contact sheet so no in-between state spells another word.
techniques.timing: Space collapse 8 f; old glyph fade 6 f; each new glyph 24 f E.out (about 45 px/f on frame 1), opacity 12 f; starts spread over 56 f; hold at least 36 f after the last glyph settles.
techniques.use_when: Two words that share letters and whose relationship is the point (before and after, problem and product); one memorable word turn per film.
techniques.avoid_when: Fewer than 2 shared letters; words longer than about 8 letters; fast films where 60 f of letter flight is too slow.

techniques.name: Scramble decode
techniques.summary: A string of random glyphs locks into the real text from left to right, or real letters roll through the alphabet into gibberish and back.
techniques.recipe: Character i shows target[i] once fd(f) >= lock_i = s + 5i, otherwise a glyph from a fixed pool chosen by rand(`${i}:${Math.floor(fd(f) / 2)}`), which changes on twos and repeats exactly on every render; use tabular or mono figures, or pin each slot to the target glyph's measured advance, so the width never jitters. Unlocked glyphs sit at 50% opacity (or C.mute) and locked glyphs at ink, optionally with a 12 f accent decay on lock. Code-roll variant: each letter steps one character code per frame from an offset toward its target, or away from it as an exit while a container takes its place.
techniques.timing: One lock every 5 f (about 48 f for a 10-character string); unlocked glyphs change every 2 f; accent decay 12 f E.out; code roll 1 step per frame, 4-8 steps per letter.
techniques.use_when: Keys, codes, private or encrypted values, numbers resolving, a short technical name in a feature beat.
techniques.avoid_when: Prose statements (it delays reading); the brand name in the end lockup; glints or sparkles on the glyphs.

techniques.name: Travelling front restyles a word
techniques.summary: A front sweeps left to right across a settled word and restyles each glyph as it passes, in colour or weight, sometimes with a cursor riding under it.
techniques.recipe: After the word has landed, move a front x_F = mix(xL - band, xR + band, prog(f, s, s + 32, E.dolly)) across it, with band about 0.6 em. For glyph i at measured x_i, u_i = clamp((x_F - x_i) / band): its colour runs C.mute -> C.accent at u = 0.5 -> C.ink at u = 1 through mixColor (one hue only), or its variable-font weight runs fontVariationSettings 'wght' 400 -> 700, with each glyph's advance interpolated between measureTracked at both weights so the line re-flows smoothly and stays centred. If the beat is the user switching something on, ride src/fx/Cursor.tsx at the base of the front. For two promise words in a tagline, step the glyphs 2 f apart instead of using a continuous band.
techniques.timing: Sweep 32 f E.dolly (front peaks about 29 px/f across a 600 px word; stretch to 40 f for wider words); band 0.6 em; per-glyph weight morph about 4 f; a second word starts about 20 f after the first; begin at least 10 f after the word lands.
techniques.use_when: Turning a static big word into a moment of discovery; emphasising one or two promise words without a highlight shape; a change of voice mid-sentence.
techniques.avoid_when: Text still moving; sweeps whose half-restyled frames read as another word; colour and weight sweeps in the same film.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: A one-hue front (mute -> accent -> ink per glyph through mixColor) instead of a multi-hue band, and a variable-weight wave (400 -> 700) in the film's one sans instead of switching glyphs to a serif italic.

techniques.name: Words spill out from behind a mark
techniques.summary: A glyph or icon slides aside and the words shoot out from behind it, clipped at its edge, as if the mark were delivering the message.
techniques.recipe: Put the words in a container clipped at the mark's current edge (for a leftward spill, clip-path: inset(0 calc(100% - (markX - boxLeft)) 0 0)) and draw the mark above them. Mark: translateX 0 -> +260 px on prog(f, s, s + 20, E.out); words: translateX +320 -> 0 on p = prog(f, s + 1, s + 25, E.out) with blurIn(p, 8) and opacity 0 -> 1 over 6 f, hidden behind the mark at first and readable once they drop below 20 px/f around frame 6. Inline variant: an icon shrinks (lmix 3 -> 1, optionally tilting in 3D) into the bullet slot at the start of a sentence and the words slide out to its right from behind it the same way.
techniques.timing: Mark 260 px over 20 f E.out (peak about 73 px/f, blurred master); words 320 px over 24 f E.out (76 px/f on frame 1, under 20 by frame 6), 1 f after the mark; opacity 6 f; hold at least 54 f with a drift.
techniques.use_when: An icon-led claim mid-film, or an opening line pushed out by the mark already in motion; a feature icon that introduces its own line; a mark or number that says the sentence.
techniques.avoid_when: The end lockup (it appears once and belongs to the end card); marks smaller than the cap height (nothing to hide behind); spills longer than about 360 px.

techniques.name: Vertical word stack
techniques.summary: In a tall frame each new word lands on its own line under the last while the stack rises one line, so the newest word always sits on the optical centre.
techniques.recipe: Line pitch 1.05x the font size (110-140 px statement type in 9:16), lines left- or centre-aligned inside safeBox() so the stack clears the feed zones. Word k lands at land_k: translateY +0.35 em -> 0 on arrive(prog(f, land_k, land_k + 18, E.out)), opacity 0 -> 1 over 6 f; the stack container moves up by the sum over k of pitch x spr(f, land_k, SPR.firm), peaking at about 11 px/f for a 150 px pitch. Lines more than two steps old fade out through a feathered top mask (mask-image transparent -> opaque over the top 0.8 pitch), so at most 3 words of one statement are on screen; the final word may arrive in the accent and relax to ink.
techniques.timing: A word every 24-30 f; word rise 18 f E.out; stack step SPR.firm (97% in 27 f); at most 3 lines visible; final hold at least 36 f + 6 f per word with a 0.3 px/f drift.
techniques.use_when: Vertical cut-downs where a horizontal line would be too small; speaking-pace statements on a phone-sized frame; one word per beat.
techniques.avoid_when: 16:9 masters (use ty-recentre-line-build); statements over 6 words; stacking two separate statements.

techniques.name: Slice-band glyph assembly
techniques.summary: Each letter builds up from thin horizontal slices that slide in from slightly different offsets at slightly different moments, faint and pale at first, until the word locks solid.
techniques.recipe: Measure the word with measureTracked. Give each glyph an inline-grid cell holding N = 5 stacked copies of itself (6 copies for type above 160 px), with all copies in grid-area 1/1. Clip copy b to its band with clip-path: inset(calc(b * 100% / N - 0.5px) -0.1em calc((N - 1 - b) * 100% / N - 0.5px) -0.1em), on a line box padded 0.12 em on top and 0.26 em below, so neighbouring bands overlap by 1 px and no descender or overhang gets shaved. Band (i, b) starts at s + d, with d = fd(12 x rand(`${i}:${b}`)) (add 1 f per glyph for a left-to-right bias), and runs on p = prog(f, s + d, s + d + 20, E.out): translateX (1 - p) x sx x 0.12 em, where sx = rand(`x${i}:${b}`) > 0.5 ? 1 : -1; translateY (1 - arrive(p)) x 0.04 em; opacity over its first 8 f on E.linear; and color mixColor(C.mute, C.ink, p) on paper (stage tint to C.white on ink). On the frame the last band lands, swap the band stacks for one intact text layer, decided with fd, so no seam survives antialiasing, then tighten the tracking 0.03 em -> the token over 44 f on E.out. Beside a mark that slides aside, start the build at the slide's peak-velocity frame, so the letters seem to be pulled out by its motion.
techniques.timing: Each band takes 20 f on E.out, with opacity over 8 f on E.linear and colour over the same 20 f. Band delays are 0-12 f from rand (plus 1 f per glyph if biased). The whole word is built in about 32 f (about 40 f with the bias). Offsets are 0.12 em sideways and 0.04 em vertical: about 4 px/f on frame 1 at 120 px type, so no blur. The swap to intact text takes 1 f, then the tracking tightens over 44 f on E.out. Hold at least 60 f with a drift of 0.3 px/f.
techniques.use_when: A product or feature name that should feel assembled or digital. A name set beside a modular or pixel mark, including the one end-lockup build when the film bookends with it. A short title after a quiet beat.
techniques.avoid_when: Lines over about 3 words, or type under 48 px (bands thinner than 3 px alias into noise). Prose. Delay spreads wide enough that the half-built word reads as broken for more than about 30 f. A film that already has a scramble decode.

techniques.name: Slice glitch into a speed streak
techniques.summary: A word jolts into sideways-displaced horizontal slices for two frames, then stretches into a solid capsule that races off as a streak, and the next word lands in its wake.
techniques.recipe: Slice: for 2 f decided with fd, render the word as 6-8 stacked copies, each clipped to one horizontal band with clip-path: inset(), and offset each band by sign x 0.08-0.25 em, both drawn from rand(`${b}:${fd(f)}`). Under 30% of the bands, lay a C.mute copy offset 0.03 em (one hue, no RGB fringes), and raise the variable 'wght' by 100 for those two frames; frame 3 renders clean. Smear: from s, scaleX = mix(1, 1.8, prog(f, s, s + 18, E.contact)) about the word's left edge, so the right edge accelerates to about 70 px/f on the last frame (render the blurred master). Over those last 10 f, fade the text out while a capsule (C.ink on paper or C.white on ink, radius 50%) fades in over the same box and its height shrinks from the cap height to 0.35 of it. Streak: the capsule keeps its handoff speed, with head x = x_e + v_e x (f - e) and a trailing tail of length clamp(v x 1.5, 0, 240) px, until it clears the frame edge. Next word: it enters in the wake, layered under the streak, with translateX -320 -> 0 on p = prog(f, e + 4, e + 28, E.outSoft), opacity 0 -> 1 over 8 f and blurIn(p, 16), so it is faint while fast and readable once it drops under 20 px/f. The 2 f slice alone, with no smear, works as a hit on privacy or obfuscation copy.
techniques.timing: Slice: 2 f via fd, clean on frame 3. Smear: 18 f on E.contact, scaleX 1 -> 1.8; for a word up to 450 px wide the right edge ends near 70 px/f. Text-to-capsule crossfade over the last 10 f. The streak cruises at that speed and clears a 1920 frame in about 15 f, with a tail of at most 240 px. Next word: 320 px over 24 f on E.outSoft from e + 4 (58 px/f on frame 1, under 20 px/f from frame 7), opacity over 8 f. Hold it at least 54 f.
techniques.use_when: A speed or performance claim, where the word itself turns into motion. Handing a name off to a thread, packet or line that carries into the next scene. The 2 f slice alone on 'private', 'encrypted' or 'blocked'.
techniques.avoid_when: Calm films. More than once per film. Words wider than about 450 px at the smear, where the edge would pass 80 px/f. Long lines. Coloured fringes or a tint shift along the trail.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Make the streak a flat solid capsule in C.ink or C.white with a speed-scaled tail and true motion blur. No bloom on the type or the streak, the trail keeps the capsule's one tone, and the glitch copies stay in C.mute.

techniques.name: Scaled-echo extrusion
techniques.summary: A hero title carries two or three faint copies scaled out behind it, a short depth extrusion that compresses as the title lands and then holds.
techniques.recipe: Stack k = 3, 2, 1 copies of the same text behind the title, with the title on top. Give copy k transform scale(1 + step x k) about a vanishing point, opacity 0.55, 0.35 and 0.2 for k = 1, 2, 3, and color mixColor(C.ink, stage colour, 0.5) (C.white mixed toward the stage on ink). Arrival: step = mix(0.03, 0.012, prog(f, land - 2, land + 20, E.out)), so the extrusion collapses inward as the title lands. Put the vanishing point on the text centre for a straight-on echo, or 0.3 W to one side or below it for a directional depth. Keep the hold alive by sliding the vanishing point about 40 px across the text over the hold, opposite to a 0.3 px/f line drift, so the echoes shift like real depth. Solid-block variant for a giant cropped word: 8-12 copies translated (k x 1 px, k x 1.5 px) behind the face, each a step darker (mixColor toward C.ink by k / 12), with no blur, bevel or shadow.
techniques.timing: Converge over 22 f on E.out (step 0.03 -> 0.012; outer copy edges stay under 7 px/f on a 500 px title). Copy opacity 0.55 / 0.35 / 0.2. Hold the whole card (36-60 f) with a vanishing-point slide of about 40 px on E.linear and a line drift of 0.3 px/f. The solid-block variant uses 8-12 one-pixel steps that do not animate relative to the face; the card still drifts at 0.3 px/f.
techniques.use_when: A product name or a hero title of one to three words that needs weight in a flat sans. A giant cropped word that needs physical depth. A title card between two energetic acts.
techniques.avoid_when: Body copy or lines over 3 words (the copies tangle inside the counters). Low-contrast stages, where the copies turn to haze. Blur, glow, bevels or drop shadows on the copies. A film that already uses the motion-trail echo of the word slams: pick one echo device.

techniques.name: Quiet type swells on the drop
techniques.summary: A word appears small and low-contrast and waits through the build, then swells to hero size, with 90% of the growth landing exactly on the beat drop.
techniques.recipe: Set the word at about 9% of the frame height, centred, in C.mute (or at 0.5 opacity on ink), and bring it in quietly: per-letter opacity pops 5-6 f apart decided with fd, or ty-typeon-timeboxed. Put the drop frame h on the music's downbeat, register it in src/sync.ts, and scale the group about its centre with k = lmix(1, 2.5, prog(f, h - 32, h + 22, E.glide)), so 90% of the log-scale growth lands on h and the rest settles over 22 f. Run color mixColor(C.mute, C.ink, prog(f, h - 32, h, E.smooth)) so size and contrast peak together. Drive the scale with transform, never font-size, and keep the starting width under about 420 px, so the outer edges peak near 17 px/f (21 px/f at 2.9x) and the word stays readable through the swell; render the blurred master for the frames above 12 px/f. After the settle, keep it alive with a 0.3 px/f drift or a cam-living-hold creep, or cut within 54 f.
techniques.timing: Letters 5-6 f apart at 9% of the frame height. Swell over 54 f on E.glide, starting at h - 32 so 90% lands on h: scale 1 -> 2.5 (2.9 at most) in log space, with the outer edges of a 420 px word peaking at about 16.5 px/f around frame 17. Contrast goes C.mute -> ink over the 32 f before h. Hold at most 54 f after h, or 90-120 f if this is the final lockup's one appearance.
techniques.use_when: A hero word or product name that should detonate on the drop after a quiet intro. The one appearance of the final wordmark when the music builds into the end. A single-word answer after a question beat.
techniques.avoid_when: There is no real musical hit to land on. Words wide enough to swell past the safe area. Using it more than once per film. Stacking a separate scale punch or camera kick on the same hit.

techniques.name: Centre-out line unmask
techniques.summary: A short line opens from its own centre outward behind a soft-edged mask while the letters stay perfectly still, so a result or status reads as unveiled rather than flown in.
techniques.recipe: Lay out the final centred line, get its width w from measureTracked, and keep every glyph static. Reveal it with a horizontal mask on the line box: o = w x prog(f, s, s + 18, E.out), and mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent (50% - o/2 - 20px), #000 (50% - o/2), #000 (50% + o/2), transparent (50% + o/2 + 20px)), computed in px each frame, so both edges travel outward with a 20 px feather (a hard clip-path: inset(0 calc(50% - o/2)) is fine inside a pill). Over the same window, run opacity 0.6 -> 1 and letter-spacing +0.04 em -> the token's tracking on E.out, so the line tightens as it opens. Set it under a centred icon or check that has just landed, starting 4-6 f after the icon's landing frame; for a second line, open it 6 f after the first. Keep the hold alive with a drift of at most 0.3 px/f, and exit with the whole line over 12 f on E.smooth or with ty-reading-order-exit.
techniques.timing: Unmask over 18 f on E.out (31% of each half-width opens on frame 1), with a 20 px feather. Opacity 0.6 -> 1 and tracking +0.04 em -> token over the same 18 f. Starts 4-6 f after the icon lands; a second line follows at +6 f. Hold at least 36 f + 6 f per word, drifting at most 0.3 px/f. Exit over 12 f on E.smooth.
techniques.use_when: A result, status or confirmation line under a centred icon ('Published', 'Connected'). A hero word inside a pill that has just formed. A calm sub-line under a headline that has already landed.
techniques.avoid_when: Lines over about 40 characters (the edges take too long to reach the ends). Left-aligned layouts (wipe from the left edge instead). Text that is also moving, where the mask fights the glyph motion. Headlines that need energy.

techniques.name: Animated line re-break
techniques.summary: A centred one-line statement re-breaks into a two-line stack, or back, with every word gliding from its old slot to its new one, so the layout changes without a cut or a jump.
techniques.recipe: Pre-solve both layouts with measureTracked and baselineOf. Layout A is one centred line; layout B is two centred lines at pitch = lead x size, the block centred on the same point, optionally at a smaller size s_B. Store each word's centre in both. Move each word i as one FLIP: p_i = prog(f, s + 2i, s + 2i + D_i, E.glide), with D_i = clamp(0.15 x travel_i, 30, 48) f; x = mix(xA_i, xB_i, p_i); scale = lmix(1, s_B / s_A, p_i). Give y its own curve, mix(yA_i, yB_i, arrive(prog(f, s + 2i - 4, s + 2i - 4 + D_i, E.outSoft))), so words that change rows drop first and slide second and never pass through a neighbour. Keep travel under 320 px per word: E.glide peaks at about 3x its mean speed, so D = 0.15 x travel holds readable words near 20 px/f (render the blurred master). If a word would travel further, split the line differently or cut. When an insert causes the re-break (an icon popping into a gap), start it 6 f after the insert lands; once settled, drift the block at 0.3 px/f.
techniques.timing: Per word, D = 0.15 x travel, clamped to 30-48 f, on E.glide (peak about 20 px/f, near 30% of the move). y leads x by 4 f on E.outSoft through arrive. Stagger 2 f in the reading order of the new layout. Travel at most 320 px. Starts 6 f after a causing insert. Settled drift 0.3 px/f.
techniques.use_when: An inserted icon or a longer word makes a centred line too wide. A headline must stack to free half the frame for a product shot. Returning a stacked headline to a single line for the payoff.
techniques.avoid_when: Lines over about 7 words. Re-breaks that carry the hero word far from where it was being read (keep it as the still anchor). More than one re-break per statement. Vertical formats, where a stack is already the default layout.

techniques.name: Orbit gather and merge
techniques.summary: Tokens swing into orbit around a node, slow to a lazy spin, then accelerate one by one into a single exit point from which a line shoots out.
techniques.recipe: Place 4 tokens on a 95 px radius around the source node (above the node, below the exit line) and drive each angle in closed form: theta_i(f) = theta0 + 90*i - (132.5*(1 - exp(-f/10)) + 2*f) deg, a 13 deg/f swing (about 22 px/f of arc) that decays to a 2 deg/f spin within 30 f. Token 0 is there at f0; tokens 1-3 spawn at f10, f18 and f28, each scaling 0 to 1 over 10 f on E.out. Pick theta0 so each token is 90-120 deg short of the exit angle (3 o'clock) when its merge starts; token i then covers that remaining angle forward over 16 f on E.contact, landing at f72, f82 and f86 at under 60 px/f, its scale cutting to 0 on arrival while the exit node takes scale 1 + 0.08*hitPulse(t) and a tick. At f92 a line draws out of the exit point (pathLength 1, strokeDashoffset 1 to 0 over 12 f on E.out) and carries the story to the next diagram.
techniques.timing: omega = 13.25*exp(-f/10) + 2 deg/f, radius 95 px at 1080p. Spawns f10/f18/f28, 10 f each (E.out). Merges 16 f each (E.contact), landing f72/f82/f86 at < 60 px/f; hitPulse(t, 2, 5) on the exit node. Exit line f92, 12 f (E.out). About 105 f in all.
techniques.use_when: Several inputs, funds or sources gather before one action (pooling, batching, syncing, sending) and the idea should be told by physics with no words.
techniques.avoid_when: The tokens are UI cards carrying text (unreadable while orbiting), or the story has no single output point.

techniques.name: Path fractures into a fan, then re-converges
techniques.summary: A solid line draws out, breaks into dashes, splits into a fan of curves that end on obstacle pills, and later the curves funnel back into one point that becomes the next diagram.
techniques.recipe: Draw the trunk from the source node as an SVG path with pathLength 1, strokeDashoffset 1 to 0 on E.linear over 12 f; at +12 f let it degrade by tweening strokeDasharray from 'L 0' to '24 12' over 8 f (dash = mix(L, 24, p), gap = mix(0, 12, p)). At +26 f split it into 6 cubic beziers from one shared point with their ends spread +-200 px in y, each revealed by its own dashoffset on E.glide over 24 f at a 2 f stagger so the drawing head stays under about 70 px/f, and pop a labelled obstacle pill at each end as its curve arrives (opacity step plus scale 0.9 to 1 over 8 f on E.out). Hard-cut to a 2.5x punch-in on the pills about 10 f after the fan completes. To resolve, give each pill a trailing bezier ending on one point, the next diagram's first node, draw them over 24 f on E.smooth while the camera travels the same way with no cut, and finish the camera's travel with an E.out landing of about 210 px over 60 f (22 px/f at its start) through lib/camera.ts.
techniques.timing: Trunk 12 f (E.linear); dashes at +12 f over 8 f to '24 12'; fan at +26 f: 6 curves x 24 f (E.glide), 2 f stagger, complete at +60 f; punch-in cut at ~+70 f (2.5x). Converge 24 f (E.smooth); camera landing 210 px over 60 f (E.out), 22 px/f at its start.
techniques.use_when: Explaining the friction of an old way (one simple path turning into many obstacles) before the turn to one clean path.
techniques.avoid_when: The viewer needs real product UI on screen; this is diagram language, and a diagram act longer than about 4 s loses the thread.

techniques.name: Stalled state by dimming
techniques.summary: A token stops on its rail, the destination greys out, short status words appear one after another, and the frame goes briefly still so the blockage is felt.
techniques.recipe: Split the rail at the stalled token: the travelled part solid, the part ahead dotted (strokeDasharray '2 4'), both drawn from the same path and clipped at the token's position. On the stall frame the destination node dims to 30% (opacity, or mixColor toward C.mute) over 8 f on E.smooth; status words then appear beside the token at +6, +28 and +40 f, each an opacity step with a 6 px rise through arrive() over 8 f on E.out, and at +51 f the first word dims to 40% so the decisive word (the reason, the day) stands alone. Bring the camera to zero velocity for a designed freeze of at most 15 f on a gap in the sound, then resume a 0.3 px/f drift so nothing sits static past 48 f.
techniques.timing: Node dim 8 f (E.smooth) to 30%. Status words at +6/+28/+40 f, 8 f each (E.out, 6 px rise); first word dims at +51 f. Freeze <= 15 f on a silence, then 0.3 px/f drift.
techniques.use_when: The problem beat: money, a message or a task stuck waiting (closed, pending, rejected) just before the product unblocks it.
techniques.avoid_when: The film has no problem act, or the block would sit longer than about 1.5 s; stillness only works as a short contrast to the motion around it.

techniques.name: Clutter pile-up, then strip to one
techniques.summary: Clicks spawn copies of a control until the frame is a messy pile, then elements vanish one per beat and the survivors snap to re-centre until a single tile remains.
techniques.recipe: Pile-up: on each click (pressAt from fx/Cursor.tsx) spawn a clone every 4 f for about 60 f at x = (rand(i) - 0.5)*500 and y = (rand(i + 99) - 0.5)*300 px, each travelling 40-80 px out from the previous clone over 8 f on E.out while scaling 0.9 to 1, so the motion-blur pass smears every spawn, and drift the whole pile up 1.5 px/f. Strip: hold the survivors in an array whose length drops at listed frames, one removal every 5-7 f, choose the state with fd(f), and compute the centred layout from the current array with no tween, so the remaining tiles jump to their new places on the removal frame. Hold the last survivor 17 f under a 0.5% scale drift (breath() from lib/camera.ts), then exit it or let it become the next shot. Put a soft tick on every spawn and removal, rising in level, so the acceleration is heard.
techniques.timing: Spawns every 4 f for ~60 f (12-15 clones), 8 f each (E.out, 40-80 px), pile drift 1.5 px/f. Removals every 5-7 f with an instant re-centre (fd); last survivor 17 f with a 0.5% drift.
techniques.use_when: Showing overload (too many tools, buttons, tabs, notifications) and then focus: the product reduces chaos to the one thing that matters.
techniques.avoid_when: Calm or premium films, or elements whose text must be read; the jumps are deliberately abrupt.

techniques.name: Cards dealt or dropped into a grid
techniques.summary: Cards land in a row or grid one after another, either dealt fast with a small tilt that squares up, or falling from just in front of the camera and shrinking into their slots.
techniques.recipe: Deal preset: card i appears at t0 + 5*i, its opacity stepping to 1 on the first frame while rotate goes 4 to 0 deg and scale 0.95 to 1 over 7 f on E.out, left to right, with no overshoot. Depth-drop preset: card i starts at delays [0, 4, 10, 14] (row-major, 6 extra frames between rows) and goes translateY 534 to 0 px and scale lmix(1.38, 1, p) on the same progress p over 54 f on E.out, half the distance in about 6 f at up to 62 px/f under the motion-blur pass. In the depth-drop keep each card's text and icons at opacity 0 until the card slows (prog(f, s + 8, s + 16, E.smooth)), so content resolves on landing below 20 px/f. Cards are opaque with a soft shadow (0 8px 30px at 6% black) and a radius of about 32 px at 1080p.
techniques.timing: Deal: 5 f stagger, 7 f settle (E.out), rotate 4 deg, scale 0.95. Drop: 54 f (E.out), stagger 0/4/10/14 f, 534 px, scale 1.38 to 1, peak ~62 px/f, content fades in from +8 to +16 f.
techniques.use_when: Revealing a set of options, results, features or integrations that should read as one set with a clear reading order.
techniques.avoid_when: There is one hero object, or more than about 8 cards (use a row cascade or a scroll).

techniques.name: Container resizes, content reflows
techniques.summary: A card or window changes size because its content or the user changes it, growing as typed text wraps or narrowing as an edge is dragged, while everything inside reflows to the new width.
techniques.recipe: Make layout a pure function of the container's current width: measure text with measureTracked or inkBox, derive line breaks and block positions from that width, and evaluate typed text on fd(f) so the substring and the line count change on whole frames only. Content-driven: as the prompt starts, the input card widens from 67% to 77% of frame width over 24 f on E.outSoft (about 18 px/f per edge, centred so both edges move), and each newly wrapped line adds one line height over 12 f on E.out. User-driven: the cursor grabs a window's right edge and drags it 300-400 px inward on E.contact over 40 f, stopping dead like a real release with no settle, while the left edge follows at 15% of the right edge's speed so the window re-centres and the cursor trails the edge by 1 f. When the width crosses a breakpoint, compute both layouts and FLIP every block to its new slot over 16-24 f on E.ui (fastest block under 70 px/f) instead of crossfading the two layouts.
techniques.timing: Widen 67% to 77% FW over 24 f (E.outSoft); +1 line per wrap over 12 f (E.out). Drag 300-400 px over 40 f (E.contact), ends near 40 px/f, hard stop; breakpoint FLIP 16-24 f (E.ui); then a 0.3 px/f push-out.
techniques.use_when: Typing into an input, responsive layouts, resizable panels: any moment where the point is that the UI adapts.
techniques.avoid_when: The size change is a change of role, such as a button becoming a panel (use a container morph), or text must be read during the resize.

techniques.name: Row cascade
techniques.summary: List rows or cards appear one after another from top to bottom, each rising a few pixels as it fades in, so the list reads as data streaming in.
techniques.recipe: For row i, start = t0 + 4*i (6*i for taller cards); translateY 8 to 0 px through arrive() and opacity 0 to 1, both over 12 f on E.out, placed by transform only. When two columns describe input and output, give both sides the same row index so the build is mirrored and 5 rows complete in about 30 f. Let each row's text land in C.mute and darken to C.ink over 12 f, 40 f after the row arrives (mixColor), so the eye reads the structure first and the words second. Start the cascade about 20 f before the previous move (a transition, a portal edge) finishes, so the start of the scene is hidden inside it.
techniques.timing: Stagger 4 f (rows) to 6 f (cards); each row 12 f (E.out), 6-12 px rise; ink-in 12 f at +40 f; overlap the previous move by ~20 f.
techniques.use_when: Populating any list, inbox, table, feed or a pair of mirrored input and output columns.
techniques.avoid_when: Rows are added one at a time over a longer beat (top insert), or the list arrives by scrolling (flick scroll).

techniques.name: Fanned stack resolves into slots
techniques.summary: A tilted, overlapping stack of cards spreads into an even row, or each card flips to show its face and flies small into a slot of a list grid where its label resolves.
techniques.recipe: Start with 4-6 cards stacked 20 px apart with seeded tilts (rand(i) mapped to +-6 deg), or a fan (rotateZ -20 deg, rotateY 25 deg, 40 px offset), z-order from the stack. Row preset: x = mix(stackX + 20*i, slotX_i, p) and rotate = mix(seed_i, 0, p) with p = prog(f, t0 + 2*i, t0 + 2*i + T, E.out) and T = max(24, 0.09 x travel) f, so the farthest card stays under 70 px/f and nothing overshoots.
