Flip preset: card i starts at t0 + 6*i, turns rotateY 0 to 180 deg on E.linear over 6 f, or 8 f for cards wider than 200 px so the edge stays near 50 px/f at edge-on (swapping from its muted back to its full face at 90 deg), drifts on E.out for 12 f (28 down to 7 px/f), then FLIPs to its grid slot rect (scale about 0.25, rotateZ to 0) over max(12, travel/20) f on E.rest; its label then rises 6 px and clears from blurIn(p, 6) over 8 f. Six cards should land within about 60 f.
techniques.timing: Row: 2 f stagger, T = max(24, 0.09 x travel) f (E.out), tilt +-6 deg. Flip: 6 f stagger, flip 6 f (8 f over 200 px wide, E.linear), drift 12 f (E.out), FLIP to slot max(12, travel/20) f (E.rest), label 8 f; six cards in ~60 f.
techniques.use_when: Many options, offers, integrations or tools becoming an orderly set: the 'all in one place' or 'compare them all' beat.
techniques.avoid_when: The cards must be read while they move, or there is only one card.

techniques.name: Lens list scroll
techniques.summary: A list scrolls with momentum past an invisible lens line, and each item's size, tint or tilt depends on its distance from that line, like a phone picker, a rolodex cylinder or a smile-shaped arc.
techniques.recipe: Drive one offset s(f) for the whole list: a flicked picker uses s = D*(1 - (1 - p)^4) with p = prog(f, a, a + 120, E.linear) and D about 900 px (30 px/f at the start, under 20 px/f after 15 f, cut while it still drifts near 2 px/f, or land on an option with spr(f, a, SPR.detent)); a rolodex uses E.inOut over 90 f for about 480 px (peak about 41 px/f). Per item compute d, its distance from the lens line along the path, and map it: flat picker, scale = 1.2 - 0.35*min(|d|/375, 1) with text colour mixColor(C.ink, C.mute, min(|d|/375, 1)); cylinder, theta = d/R with R = 1.4*H, rotateX(theta) and translateZ(-(1 - cos theta)*R) under perspective 1600 px; smile arc, x = cx + R*sin(theta), y = cy + R*cos(theta) and rotate(-theta) with R = 1750 px and the centre about 790 px above the frame. Give each card a soft shadow; the depth comes from the geometry, never from translucent panels.
techniques.timing: Picker: 120 f quartic momentum, D ~900 px, 30 px/f start, < 20 px/f from f15, ~2 px/f at the cut; focus scale 1.2 to 0.85 across 375 px; optional SPR.detent landing. Cylinder: 90 f (E.inOut), ~480 px, peak ~41 px/f, R = 1.4H, perspective 1600 px. Arc: R 1750 px.
techniques.use_when: Choosing among options, showing many screens as one continuous surface, or a playful list of choices that read one at a time.
techniques.avoid_when: Items must be read while moving fast, or a plain scroll says it more simply.

techniques.name: Toss into a bin with one rebound
techniques.summary: Icons or chips are thrown into a container that rises in to catch them, drop through its mouth and peek back out once before settling.
techniques.recipe: Layer order, back to front: bin body, thrown items, bin front lip, with the items clipped by a clipPath at the mouth so they vanish inside; the bin rises 160 px on E.out over 24 f. Toss: each item rises about 260 px on E.out over 24 f (about 68 px/f on its first frame), hangs 3 f, then falls about 340 px on E.contact over 22 f while rotateZ goes to +-15 deg (sign from rand(i)) and x eases to the mouth on E.smooth, entering at no more than 70 px/f under the motion-blur pass. Chain variant: chips follow an SVG path into the bin, chip i at path.getPointAtLength(L*E.contact(prog(f, t0 + 5*i, t0 + 5*i + 60, E.linear))) rotated to the tangent (atan2 of a 1 px look-ahead), the element they trail squashed to a 6 px tall tail. Six frames after the last entry the contents peek back up about 24 px on spr(f, hit, SPR.land) and settle within 16 f, the rim takes squash(t), and a low 60 to 30 Hz thud lands on that frame; this counts as one of the film's two spring landings.
techniques.timing: Bin rise 160 px, 24 f (E.out). Item rise ~260 px, 24 f (E.out); hang 3 f; fall ~340 px, 22 f (E.contact), <= 70 px/f; tilt +-15 deg. Chain: 60 f per chip (E.contact along the path), 5 f lag. Rebound at +6 f, ~24 px, SPR.land, settled in 16 f.
techniques.use_when: A comic or decisive 'throw the old way away' beat: replacing old tools, clearing clutter, deleting the problem.
techniques.avoid_when: Serious, calm or enterprise tone, or the film has already used its two spring landings.

techniques.name: Push-aside with bound layout
techniques.summary: An incoming panel or card enters from the edge and the neighbouring content moves aside because it is bound to the panel's edge, so one motion moves two elements and nothing overlaps.
techniques.recipe: Bind instead of tweening twice: each frame set neighbour.x = min(restX, panel.left - gap), so the neighbour reflows from the panel's own position. Shove: a dark card (C.ink2, radius 24 px, about 62% of frame width) enters from beyond the right edge over 72 f on E.whip (peak about 72 px/f at 40% under the motion-blur pass) and is placed so it reaches the headline word only after 58% of its move, where the card has slowed to 20 px/f or less, so the shoved word stays readable. Make room: a side panel 36% of frame width slides in on E.glide over 54 f (peak about 38 px/f) while the content card moves 0.43x the panel's travel on E.smooth, starting 28 f before the panel so it anticipates the arrival; the exit mirrors both over about 50 f. For copy, the product card glides 370 px aside and scales 1 to 0.83 on E.glide over 48 f (peak about 23 px/f) while the headline rises line by line into the freed side (Words, 6 f stagger), starting 4-6 f after the slide.
techniques.timing: Shove: 72 f (E.whip), contact after 58% of the move, word <= 20 px/f. Side panel: 36% FW over 54 f (E.glide); neighbour 0.43x travel with a 28 f lead (E.smooth); exit ~50 f. Copy: 370 px + scale 0.83 over 48 f (E.glide); lines 6 f apart from +4-6 f.
techniques.use_when: Introducing a detail panel, a new card or a caption beside existing UI, or a joke where the layout itself does the gag.
techniques.avoid_when: The incoming element should float above (modal, popover), or there is no room to move into.

techniques.name: Outline-led insert and spawn
techniques.summary: A thin accent line or a heavy outline appears first and opens into a new row or a modal, then the stroke decays to a hairline so the content takes over.
techniques.recipe: Row insert: a 2 px C.accent line appears across the list in one frame at the insert position, then the row opens from height 0 to row height over 10 f on E.ui, pushing the rows below through the computed list layout at 20 px/f or less; its 2 px border decays from the accent to 40% over 24 f on E.linear and then to nothing, and the row's content fades in over the last 4 f of the open. Repeat inserts every 41 f so three new rows read as a countable rhythm, each with a tick on its line frame. Modal spawn: the modal scales lmix(0.07, 1, prog(f, a, a + 26, E.out)) about the trigger point while an overlay stroke in the accent runs 6 to 10 to 1 px wide (interpolate(p, [0, 0.6, 1], [6, 10, 1]) on the same progress); after landing it thins to 1 px over 12 f and its opacity falls to 0.3, leaving a clean modal. At its peak the stroke can carry a faint outer glow, which the hard bans rule out; build it flat (see the variant).
techniques.timing: Line 1 f; open 10 f (E.ui); border decay 24 f (E.linear); content in the last 4 f; inserts every 41 f. Modal 26 f (lmix on E.out) from scale 0.07, far edge ~52 px/f; stroke 6/10/1 px; thin 12 f; opacity to 0.3.
techniques.use_when: A click that creates something (a new account, row, record or dialog) that must read from a wide shot, or repeated creation shown as a rhythm.
techniques.avoid_when: The accent already means something else in the film, or the shot is a calm monochrome close-up where a bright stroke would shout.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Use a flat 2 px stroke in the film's single accent with no box-shadow, bloom or blur; express the flash as stroke width (2 to 3 px for 4 f via hitPulse) and an opacity decay from 1 to 0.4 to 0 over 24 f, and frame the modal with a solid 6-10 px accent stroke that thins to 1 px.

techniques.name: Spawn from the anchor point
techniques.summary: Menus, popovers, drop targets and detail cards scale out of the exact point that caused them, such as the cursor tip or a map pin, and collapse back into it.
techniques.recipe: Set transform-origin to the trigger point in the element's own coordinates (cursor tip, pin base, the edge of the button) and scale with lmix from about 0.05, opacity reaching 1 within the first 4 f; the log-space scale keeps the far edge from jumping on frame 1. Small surfaces (menus, popovers, a card out of a pin): lmix(0.05, 1, prog(f, a, a + 12, E.out)), no overshoot, adding 2 f per extra 100 px of size, then a small camera reframe toward the surface starting 2 f later over 20-40 f on E.cam. Large surfaces (a drop target filling a panel): lmix(0.036, 1, prog(f, a, a + 48, E.smooth)), a flat C.accent fill with a 12 px radius, its icon and hint text fading in over the last 8 f; it collapses back into the point over 36 f on E.smooth. Keep the cursor (fx/Cursor.tsx) parked on the trigger during the spawn so cause and effect share one point.
techniques.timing: Small: 12 f (lmix, E.out) from 0.05, opacity 4 f, far edge ~63 px/f for a 300 px menu; camera reframe from +2 f over 20-40 f (E.cam). Large: 48 f (lmix, E.smooth) from 0.036, hint over the last 8 f, collapse 36 f (E.smooth).
techniques.use_when: Any UI that opens from a click, or a drag target appearing: menus, popovers, dialogs, drop zones, cards from a map pin.
techniques.avoid_when: The element enters from off-screen or is a full window (rise-in), or the trigger point is out of frame.

techniques.name: Shell first, then contents, then the action
techniques.summary: The empty container is on screen first, its contents arrive left to right, the card unfolds downward in stages, and the primary button fills last as the clear call to act.
techniques.recipe: Show the container (bar, card, window) at t0 with nothing inside; its children enter in DOM order at a 4 f stagger, each rising 6 px through arrive() with opacity 0 to 1 over 12 f on E.out, and media slots first appear as C.mist rounded rects that fill with their image over 8 f, 8 f apart. The primary action comes last: its background ramps from transparent to solid on E.linear over 16 f from +20 f, and its label colour inverts on a single frame at +28 f. To teach the hierarchy, unfold the card downward in stages with a clip-path inset on its bottom edge on E.smooth (header row first, then 36 f to reveal the stats row, then 24 f to the full card, the bottom edge travelling about 330 px), each stage's content starting only once its slot is 60% revealed. Headlines inside the UI are live text in the camera world, revealed per word with Words (6 f stagger), so they inherit the plane's perspective.
techniques.timing: Children 4 f stagger, 12 f each (E.out), 6 px rise. Media fill 8 f, 8 f apart. Button fill 16 f (E.linear) from +20 f; label inverts at +28 f. Unfold 36 f then 24 f (E.smooth), content at 60% open. In-UI headline 6 f per word.
techniques.use_when: The first appearance of any real product screen, especially dashboards, headers and forms whose reading order matters.
techniques.avoid_when: The screen should feel already alive on the cut (enter it moving with a rise-in), or the shot is shorter than about 40 f.

techniques.name: Top insert pushes the list down
techniques.summary: New items arrive at the top of a list one at a time and every earlier item slides down one slot, on a steady metronome that reads as abundance or on a slower cadence where each row resolves as it is generated.
techniques.recipe: Compute every item's y from the data each frame (listLayout from the product-ui reference, newest at index 0), so earlier items slide down one pitch on E.ui as each new one mounts; overlapping pushes simply add. Metronome: one insert every 14 f with a 155 px pitch pushed over 20 f (about 21 px/f); the new pill reveals left to right with clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) to inset(0) over 12 f on E.ui, its icon leading and its label fading in 4 f later, while any paired object (an item landing on a stack) drops 60-90 px with opacity over 10 f on E.out; wrap the group in a camera drift whose velocity decays as vStart*0.97^f from about 19 to 3 px/f over 90 f. Generation: one insert every 36-40 f, the row starting at scaleX 0.6 about its left edge with blurIn(p, 6) and an 8% C.accent tint, reaching full width, sharp and neutral over 12 f on E.out while the rows below move 66 px over 10 f on E.ui. Put a tick on each insert frame (LANDINGS) so the cadence is heard.
techniques.timing: Metronome: every 14 f, push 155 px over 20 f (E.ui), pill reveal 12 f (E.ui), label +4 f, camera drift 19 to 3 px/f (x0.97 per frame). Generation: every 36-40 f, resolve 12 f (E.out) from scaleX 0.6 and 6 px blur, push 66 px over 10 f (E.ui).
techniques.use_when: Results, messages, subtasks or saved items accumulating: generated rows, imports landing, a feed or a stack filling up.
techniques.avoid_when: The whole list should appear at once (row cascade), or there are so many inserts that the pushes blur into noise (scroll instead).

techniques.name: Container morph into its next role
techniques.summary: One element changes shape into what it becomes, a button unfolding into a panel, a card stretching into a detail view, a pill collapsing into an app tile, so there is no navigation cut to explain.
techniques.recipe: Keep one element mounted and animate its position (x and y inside one transform), width, height and border radius from the old rect to the new role's rect; never swap two elements. Use E.whip over 30-36 f (slow first 5 f, speed peak near 40%, long settle) and lengthen it so the fastest edge stays under about 70 px/f (frames >= 3.8 x edge travel / 70); a pill collapsing to a tile keeps its height locked while its radius goes from 999 px to 22% of its side, and a panel's radius eases from 44 to 36 px. The old content fades out in the first 12 f on E.smooth, a title that survives FLIPs to its header position and scale (1 to 0.6) on the same curve, flying at opacity 1 - 0.45*clamp((v - 20)/30) (v its speed in px/f) whenever it passes 20 px/f so it lands sharp, the new content enters 8 f after the speed peak with a 2-4 f stagger, and a backdrop behind a panel morph dims linearly over the same frames. Optional preface: the card's outline retracts first (SVG rect with pathLength 1, strokeDashoffset 0 to 1 over 15 f); for a content swap inside a card that stays, the old child leaves with depart() and blurOut(q, 8) over 18 f on E.in, the card resizes to the new aspect over 20 f on E.out, and the new child arrives with arrive() and blurIn(p, 8) over 18 f on E.out.
techniques.timing: Morph 30-36 f (E.whip), edges <= 70 px/f. Old content out 12 f (E.smooth); title FLIP to 0.6 scale; new content +8 f after the peak, 2-4 f stagger; backdrop dim linear over the morph. Outline retract 15 f. Content swap: out 18 f (E.in), resize 20 f (E.out), in 18 f (E.out).
techniques.use_when: A click that opens something (button to panel, card to detail), a status becoming an icon, an object docking into its slot.
techniques.avoid_when: The size change comes from content or a drag (live reflow), or the two states have no visual relation.

techniques.name: Drag to reorder, siblings make way
techniques.summary: An item lifts under the cursor, travels on a slight arc to a new position while its neighbours slide aside one slot at a time, and settles into place with a firm landing and no bounce.
techniques.recipe: On the press (pressAt(f, grab)) the item moves to its own top layer and lifts: scale 1 to 1.03 and its shadow from 0 6px 16px at 8% to 0 18px 40px at 14% over 8 f on E.ui. It then follows cursorArc(from, to, prog(f, a, a + T, E.glide), 0.15) with T = max(36, 0.15 x distance) f, so it never exceeds 20 px/f and its label stays readable, and rotateZ = -0.15 deg per px/f of horizontal speed, clamped to +-4 deg. Siblings take their y from the computed layout for the currently hovered index, evaluated on fd(f), so each time that index changes the displaced sibling moves one pitch over 12 f on E.ui. On release the item settles into its slot with spr(f, drop, SPR.firm), the lift reverses over 10 f, its marker flashes C.accent and relaxes to neutral over 24 f, and a tick lands on the drop frame.
techniques.timing: Lift 8 f (E.ui), scale 1.03. Drag T = max(36, 0.15 x distance) f (E.glide) on a 0.15 bow, <= 20 px/f, tilt <= 4 deg. Sibling shift 12 f (E.ui) per index change. Drop SPR.firm, shadow back over 10 f, accent relax 24 f.
techniques.use_when: Prioritising, scheduling, kanban boards, playlists: any product whose smart part is ordering things.
techniques.avoid_when: The reorder is automatic (animate the computed reorder on one curve, with no cursor), or more than 2-3 drags would fall in one shot.

techniques.name: Progress spine leads the steps
techniques.summary: A thin line grows down the side of a step list with a dot at its head. Each step appears as the head reaches it, works with a spinner and a typed detail line, then flips to done, and the list scrolls to keep the head in view until the line turns a rounded corner toward the result.
techniques.recipe: Build the spine as one SVG path: a vertical run down the list's left gutter, then optionally a 40 px-radius arc into a horizontal run toward the result card. Place the head, a flat 10 px dot in C.ink, at getPointAtLength(L(f)) (from @remotion/paths). L moves only between steps, over 40 f on E.rest per step pitch, and waits at each step for that step's work time from the data (machine-timed, 24-60 f). Draw the path twice: a 1.5 px C.line hairline for the whole route, and above it a 2 px C.ink stroke with pathLength 1 and strokeDashoffset = 1 - L / total, so the part already travelled is solid and the rest is a guide. Step row i appears on the frame the head reaches its y (pass_i): opacity prog(f, pass_i, pass_i + 12, E.smooth) with a 12 px rise through arrive(). While the head waits there, the row shows a dashed-ring spinner (one turn per 48 f) and TypeOn types its detail line at about 1.5 characters per frame. On the last frame of the wait (decided on fd), the spinner becomes a C.accent check that draws over 8 f on E.out, a 'Done' tag fades in over 8 f, and the head leaves on that same frame. Scroll the list container, not the camera, with a lagged follow written as a pure function: loop from the shot's first frame to f with c += (headY(i) - 0.4 x H - c) x 0.08, and add a 2 px/f drift, so the head sits near 40% of the frame height and the list never stops dead. At the corner the head turns first, and the horizontal follow inherits the lag as it carries the eye to the result at a constant 10-14 px/f.
techniques.timing: Head travel 40 f per step (E.rest), about 10 px/f for a 120 px pitch; wait 24-60 f per step, taken from the data. Row reveal 12 f (E.smooth) with a 12 px rise. Spinner one turn per 48 f; detail line ~1.5 chars/f; check 8 f (E.out); tag 8 f. Scroll lag 0.08 per frame plus a 2 px/f drift, peak about 12.5 px/f. Corner radius 40 px; horizontal run 10-14 px/f.
techniques.use_when: An agent, build, deploy, import or onboarding process working through steps, where the point is visible progress toward one result.
techniques.avoid_when: There are fewer than 3 steps (one status capsule says it), or the steps finish too fast to read (show the result with a count instead).
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Draw the head as a flat 10 px dot in C.ink (white on an ink stage) with no halo, bloom or blur. Mark its state with size instead (12 px while travelling, 10 px while waiting). The spine, the step states, the scroll follow and every timing stay the same.

techniques.name: Genie launch from an icon
techniques.summary: A dock or home-screen icon flares open at its top into a curved funnel that keeps widening until it fills the frame, and the app's first screen is already sitting inside it.
techniques.recipe: Render the app's first screen full-frame above the current scene and clip it with clip-path: path(), rebuilt every frame from a few numbers. The bottom edge sits on the icon's base with width wb; the top edge is h above it with width wt. Each side is a quadratic curve whose control point is the bottom corner raised by 0.45 h, so the outline pinches like a funnel. Grow it in log space so it leaves the icon slowly and speeds up: h = lmix(iconH, H + 120, p) and wt = lmix(iconW, W + 240, p), with p = prog(f, a, a + 44, E.linear). Over the same 44 f, the top edge's centre drifts from the icon to the frame centre on E.smooth, which peaks mid-way, before the growth gets fast. In the last 24 f, with s = prog(f, a + 20, a + 44, E.smooth), the waist widens toward the top (wb = mix(iconW, wt, s)) and the bottom edge drops from the icon base to 60 px below the frame. With these numbers the fastest edge stays near 70-75 px/f on the final frames, under the motion-blur pass. Start the funnel 4 f after pressAt on the icon (the icon's tile darkens 10% on the press frame). Either keep the revealed screen still at its final size, or let it settle from 1.04 to 1 over the same 44 f on E.outSoft. On the first frame the path covers the whole frame, unmount the clip and the old scene, and start the app's first UI event (a caret, a typed greeting) on that frame, so the launch hands straight over to the product.
techniques.timing: Press, then funnel from +4 f: 44 f in log space (about x1.06-1.08 per frame, E.linear progress). Centre drift over the same 44 f (E.smooth). Waist and bottom edge open over the last 24 f (E.smooth). Fastest edge ~70-75 px/f at the end. Optional content settle 1.04 to 1 over 44 f (E.outSoft). Clip removed on full cover; the next UI event starts on that frame.
techniques.use_when: Opening an app, a document or a tool from its icon in a dock, launcher or home screen, as a playful product-native scene change.
techniques.avoid_when: The product is never launched from an icon, or the film already has a genie (once is a gag, twice reads as a template).
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Fill the funnel with the app's real first screen on its flat stage colour, or with one flat colour taken from the icon, never the icon's colour ramp. The clip path, the log-space growth and the timing stay the same.

techniques.name: Ease-out count-up from a near-final value
techniques.summary: A proof figure counts up in place from a credible value just below its target and decelerates, so the last units tick in one at a time and it reads in about half a second.
techniques.recipe: Compute the shown value on whole frames: v = Math.round(mix(a, b, prog(fd(frame), at, at + 28, E.type))), with a at 85-90% of b (173 to 195, 734 to 799), so early frames jump 2-3 units and the last ones step by 1. Use E.out only for ranges over ~500 units, where its long tail still has digits to tick. Render the value as plain text through typeStyle (tabular-nums), with a fixed digit count and Intl.NumberFormat separators so the box never changes width, and let the digits replace in place each frame: no roll, no crossfade. Start the count on the frame its cause lands and put ticks on countSteps(a, b, at, 28, E.type) frames, thinned to at most one every 2 f. After it lands, keep the block alive with breath() on the camera (2-3%) until the next element covers it.
techniques.timing: Hero count 28 f on E.type (quad-out: 2x the mean rate at the start, so the last unit lands in the final ~6 f). Prices and recounts 36-46 f; ambient UI KPIs 36-104 f. Start at 85-90% of the target. Hold the landed figure at least 36 f (plus 6 f per word of any label) under a 2-3% breath before anything covers it.
techniques.use_when: A single proof figure (countries, users, a price) must register in under a second, or a number inside a UI shot should feel live.
techniques.avoid_when: The number is the film's hero reveal and deserves a reel or a snap-out; nothing on screen causes the count to start.

techniques.name: Companion glyph swaps mid-count
techniques.summary: A small icon riding a counting number (a flag, an avatar, a status glyph) swaps to its destination state when the count crosses a threshold, then drops from superscript to the baseline.
techniques.recipe: Set a 0.45 em glyph at the number's top-right as a superscript (translateY -0.35 em). Swap its source on the first whole frame where the shown value reaches the threshold (an fd-based v >= T compare, about 60% of the way through the count), cutting between the two images with no crossfade. On that frame start the drop: translateY from -0.35 em to 0 over 8 f with arrive(prog(frame, swap - 1, swap + 7, E.out)), so the new glyph seats on the baseline while the count is still finishing. Put a soft tick on the swap frame, separate from the count ticks.
techniques.timing: Swap at ~60% of the count (frame 17 of a 28 f count). Drop 8-12 px at 1080p over 8 f on E.out through arrive. The count lands 10-11 f after the swap.
techniques.use_when: The count carries a from-to story (origin to destination, free to paid, pending to done) that one icon can tell.
techniques.avoid_when: The glyph would only be decoration; counts shorter than 20 f, where the swap gets lost.

techniques.name: Process-status pill with ring progress
techniques.summary: A compact capsule shows where a process stands in one glance: a live dot, a mono step label, a ring filled to the current percentage, the step count and a grey date.
techniques.recipe: Draw a rounded rect (radius 25% of its height) in C.ink2 with a 1.5 px C.line hairline border. Left to right, place an 8 px accent dot, a mono uppercase label (FONT.mono, 24 px at 1080p, tracking 0.15 em), an SVG ring (r 14 px, 3 px stroke, pathLength 1, strokeDasharray `${p} 1` over a C.line track), primary text at weight 500 ('Step 5/6 · Motion') and a C.mute date line. Animate it rather than parking it: the capsule rises 24 px on SPR.firm with opacity over 10 f on E.smooth; from the landing, the ring fills from 4/6 to 5/6 over 30 f on E.out, and the step digit rolls 4 to 5 through Roll on the fill's 50% frame. On the roll frame the dot pulses once, scale 1 + 0.4 * hitPulse(t, 2, 8).
techniques.timing: Arrival on SPR.firm (~24 f to settle). Ring fill 30 f on E.out. Step roll 14 f. Dot pulse: attack 2 f, tau 8 f. Visible 46-90 f.
techniques.use_when: Proving that a real, structured process exists (pipeline, build, delivery) as an overlay on process footage.
techniques.avoid_when: The step and percentage aren't true to the story; frames that already carry a headline, which the pill would compete with.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: The same capsule on a solid C.ink2 fill with a 1.5 px hairline border, no backdrop blur or frosted translucency, depth only from a soft drop shadow at about 0.16 alpha. Keep the live dot, the ring and the one step line ('Step 5/6 · Motion'); drop the tracked mono uppercase label and the grey date, which only decorate.

techniques.name: Metric as the first statement
techniques.summary: The film opens on its proof number already moving, with no title and no logo, and the brand waits for the end lockup.
techniques.recipe: Frame 0 is the number mid-count or mid-roll (an ease-out count-up, a digit reel or the macro snap-out) at hero size, cap height about 11% of frame height, centred on the stage colour. The first visible change comes by frame 2, with no fade-up from black. The number settles by frame 40, stays readable for at least 72 f including its unit under a 2% breath push, then hands off on a cut at a motion peak into the problem. Run the story as metric, problem, solution, process, lockup, and keep the logo and product name off screen until the lockup, which stays the only brand moment. Mark the landing with an audio drop: thin or cut the music on the landing frame and allow a designed freeze of at most 15 f there.
techniques.timing: First change by frame 2. Settled by frame 40. Readable for 72 f (about frames 41-113). Hand-off cut near frame 113. Optional freeze of at most 15 f on the landing silence.
techniques.use_when: The product has one strong, true outcome number (users, views, savings) that should earn attention before the name does.
techniques.avoid_when: The number is weak, generic or can't be verified; films where the mark itself must lead.

techniques.name: Tucked unit under the last digits
techniques.summary: A small lowercase unit word fades in right-aligned under a big number's last digits, its top overlapping the numeral's baseline, so number and unit read as one mark.
techniques.recipe: Set the unit at 0.35x the numeral's font size in the film's one sans (weight 450, C.mute or the stage's secondary ink). Align its right edge with the numeral's right edge (measureTracked, minus the last glyph's trailing tracking) and its top with the numeral baseline minus 0.3x the label's line height, so it tucks under the last two digits. Fade it in over 19 f on E.smooth with a 4 px rise through arrive, starting at least 12 f after the number settles so the figure reads first. It then holds with the number under the shot's breath.
techniques.timing: Starts at least 12 f after the number settles (36 f is a good default). Opacity over 19 f on E.smooth with a 4 px rise via arrive. Label at 0.35x the numeral size, overlapping its baseline by 30% of the label height.
techniques.use_when: A hero figure needs its unit (views, users, ms) without a second line pushing the layout down.
techniques.avoid_when: The unit is longer than one short word; numbers ending in narrow digits (1, 7) that leave no room to tuck under.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Same placement and size in the film's one sans at weight 450, in C.mute or the stage's secondary ink: no second display typeface and no cream or gold tint.

techniques.name: Hero bar in close-up, then pull back
techniques.summary: The winning bar (or the hero chart) grows across a tight frame, then the camera eases back to show the whole chart, with the grey comparison bars and their values.
techniques.recipe: Lay the whole chart out in world space with the anchor camera (src/lib/camera.ts): the hero bar in C.accent, the comparison bars in C.mute, values at the bar ends. Shot A frames the hero bar at k of about 1.33-1.5. Grow its width over 50 f on E.smooth while the camera pushes 4% and tracks the tip at about 60% of frame width; keep the tip at or under 70 px/f on screen (on-screen length x 2.86 / frames). On the landing frame, pull back with lc(A, B, prog(frame, land, land + 80, E.cam)) to the full chart at k = 1. The grey bars are already at value, the labels type in with TypeOn, and the percentages count on E.type over 28 f, 4 f apart top to bottom, starting 12 f into the pull-back.
techniques.timing: Bar fill 50 f on E.smooth (no overshoot) with a 4% push. Pull-back 52-80 f on E.cam to 0.65-0.75 of the close scale. Values count over 28 f on E.type at a 4 f stagger. Hold the full chart at least 36 f under a breath.
techniques.use_when: Benchmarks and comparisons the product wins; any chart whose hero value should be felt before it is compared.
techniques.avoid_when: Narrow wins, which the close-up would oversell; more than ~6 bars, whose labels go unreadable after the pull-back.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: A flat accent bar with no outer glow or bloom. It stands apart from the grey bars by colour and 4-6 px of extra thickness only.

techniques.name: Mini bar-chart answer card
techniques.summary: Inside a chat or a panel, an answer arrives as a small card of labelled horizontal bars that grow in sequence, followed by a one-line insight that states the key figures.
techniques.recipe: The card rises 24 px on SPR.firm (opacity over 10 f on E.smooth). Each row holds a label, a bar track (C.mist on paper, C.ink2 on ink) and a value. Bar i's width is value% x track x prog(frame, at + 5i, at + 5i + 20, E.outSoft), and its value counts on the same progress. Keep tracks at or under 300 px, or stretch the grow to track/15 frames, so the bar tip stays at or under 70 px/f. Only the row the insight is about takes C.accent; the rest stay neutral. Six frames after the last bar lands, type the insight with TypeOn with its two figures at weight 600. Keep the card under a 2% camera breath while it is read, and optionally hard-cut on the next 8th to a 2.4x punch-in on the highlighted row (cam-punch-in-insert) that pans sideways with inertia(f, cut, 20, 0.89), starting at the 20 px/f text limit and settling in about 30 f.
techniques.timing: Rows 20 f each on E.outSoft at a 5 f stagger (the group lands within 30 f). The insight types over ~40 f, starting 6 f after the last bar. Card visible ~180 f under a 2% breath. Optional 2.4x punch-in cut, then a pan from 20 px/f decaying 0.89 per frame (settled in about 30 f).
techniques.use_when: An AI or analytics product answers a question with data; a walkthrough needs one piece of quantitative proof.
techniques.avoid_when: More than 6 rows, where the group outruns 30 f and the labels shrink; bars that carry no real meaning.

techniques.name: Line chart draws with a tracking head
techniques.summary: A line or stepped series draws left to right behind a solid dot at its head that the eye can follow, accelerating through the middle and creeping into its last point.
techniques.recipe: Draw the series as an SVG path with pathLength={1}, strokeDasharray 1 and strokeDashoffset 1 - p. Put a solid head dot (r 6 px at 1080p, with a 2 px ring in the stage colour) at the point at fraction p along the polyline, sampled from the data in JS rather than measured from the DOM. Beneath the line, add an area fill in the line's hue fading from 18% to 0% opacity, clipped by a rect whose right edge follows the head. Drive p from 0 to 1 over 96 f on E.rest in a single link: it starts from rest, peaks near 29% of the draw and spends its last third creeping into the last point, so the head never stops and restarts. The head peaks around 40-60 px/f, so the blur pass streaks it while the drawn line stays crisp; when the head lands, roll in the endpoint value with Roll.
techniques.timing: Full draw 96 f on E.rest (peak near 29%, 3.5x the mean speed; the last 30 f creep at about 2-3 px/f on a 1,400 px path). Short form: 24 f on E.out, with the area fill fading in from 8 f later over 16 f. Head peaks at 40-60 px/f at 1080p. Endpoint value rolls over 14 f.
techniques.use_when: Growth, price or usage over time; any chart where the trend is the message.
techniques.avoid_when: Invented up-and-to-the-right data; charts under ~400 px wide, where the head reads as noise.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: A solid head dot with a 2 px stage-colour ring and no blur, drop-shadow halo or bloom. The area fill stays a single-hue opacity ramp.

techniques.name: Constant-speed bar sweep with lit caps
techniques.summary: A row of bars grows in a wave that travels at constant speed; each bar eases up on its own and flashes a bright cap that relaxes to the resting tone.
techniques.recipe: Bar i starts at at + 1.6i, a linear wave travelling at bar pitch / 1.6 px per frame (about 25 px/f at 1080p). It grows with height = h_i * prog(frame, start_i, start_i + 12, E.out) from a bottom anchor; make the grow last at least 0.09 x the bar height in px so the top edge never passes 70 px/f. A 3 px cap on each bar arrives in C.accent and relaxes to the bar's resting tone over 20 f after the bar lands (mixColor, cap opacity 1 to 0.6), because the accent means 'just landed'. For a centre-out symmetric wall, use tr-stepped-column-fill instead.
techniques.timing: 1.6 f per bar (~25 px/f wave). Each bar 12 f on E.out (at least 0.09 x its height in px). Cap relaxes over 20 f.
techniques.use_when: Volume, activity or histogram data streaming in; an opening equaliser or skyline that hints at growth.
techniques.avoid_when: Bars that must be compared precisely, since the wave delays reading; fewer than 6 bars.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Solid single-tone bars (or a single-hue tonal ramp) whose cap uses the film's one accent and relaxes to the bar tone: never a multi-hue gradient and never a warm amber cap.

techniques.name: One control drives several live numbers
techniques.summary: Dragging a slider visibly drives every dependent figure in lockstep, and the fill changes tint once it passes a marked threshold.
techniques.recipe: Drive everything from one progress, p = prog(frame, at, at + 90, E.smooth). The slider fill is mix(0.35, 0.84, p) x track, the thumb (with a 2 px ring) rides the same value, and each dependent figure (percentage, amount, headroom) is computed from that value on fd(frame), rounded and set in fixed-width tabular figures. Past the threshold marker, draw the fill from the marker to the thumb in a brighter tint of the fill hue, and switch the affected figure's colour on the crossing frame. The cursor (Cursor.tsx) grabs the thumb 8 f before the drag starts and rides it. Figures that fall (headroom 44K to 13K) count down on the same p, and the formula is asserted in data.ts so every frame stays consistent.
techniques.timing: Drag 90 f on E.smooth (fastest change mid-drag). Cursor grabs 8 f before. Figures update every whole frame. Hold the end state at least 36 f under a breath.
techniques.use_when: Calculators, pricing, risk limits, utilisation: any feature whose logic is 'move this and those follow'.
techniques.avoid_when: The dependent figures aren't computed consistently from one formula; more than 3 dependents.

techniques.name: Flag cascade, then one chosen
techniques.summary: Status marks appear on a set of cards one after another, then a single card switches to the accent state: many flagged, one picked.
techniques.recipe: Card i gets its flag at at + 6i: its border mixes from the card fill to a mid grey over 6 f on E.ui, and a 10 px hollow dot scales from 0 to 1 on SPR.micro. Flags stay neutral so the one accent can mean 'chosen'. About 28 f after the first flag, the chosen card switches over 8 f on E.ui: border to C.accent, a 6% accent inner tint, the dot filled, and scale 1 + 0.02 * hitPulse(t, 2, 6). Hold for at most 48 f with a slow 2% push toward it, then the chosen card leaves first on E.in into the cut.
techniques.timing: Flags 6 f apart, 6 f each. Selection ~28 f after the first flag, an 8 f change. Hold at most 48 f with a 2% push. The chosen card exits on E.in.
techniques.use_when: Triage, review, matching, anomaly detection: anything that narrows many down to one.
techniques.avoid_when: The pick isn't what the product actually outputs; grids of more than ~12 cards, where the cascade reads as a queue.

techniques.name: Top-to-bottom row refresh
techniques.summary: When a filter changes, a thin scan line crosses each table row in turn from top to bottom, and the row's icon, label and values change behind it.
techniques.recipe: Two frames after the filter chip lands, row i gets its own scan, x_i = rowW * prog(frame, at + 3i, at + 3i + 20, E.linear). Clip the old row content with inset(0 0 0 x_i px) and the new with inset(0 (rowW - x_i) px 0 0), so each cell changes as the line crosses it and nothing is crossfaded. A 1.5 px hairline in C.line rides x_i and fades over its last 6 f; only the row the story is about gets the accent. Figures that change by a small amount roll with Roll (12 f) from the frame the line reaches their cell, instead of wiping.
techniques.timing: Starts 2 f after the chip lands. 3 f row stagger. 20 f per row, linear (at most 60 px/f across a 1,250 px row). Six rows finish within ~35 f. Hairline fades over 6 f.
techniques.use_when: Tables, activity feeds or leaderboards that refresh on a filter or a new period.
techniques.avoid_when: Only one cell changes, so a Roll on it is enough; more than 8 rows, where the cascade reads as a queue.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: One neutral hairline per row (the accent only on the row the story cares about), with no rainbow-tinted streak and no glow.

techniques.name: Mechanical digit reel
techniques.summary: Each digit sits in its own masked column and rolls vertically like an odometer: the low columns spin while the high ones step once, landing column by column.
techniques.recipe: Use Roll from src/fx/Roll.tsx in count mode (from, to, start, dur 60, ease E.out, roll 14, group ','). countSteps places a step on every whole frame where the integer changes, so the low columns spin a slot per frame while each high column rolls once on its own E.out, and the fixed column count keeps the width still. For an event counter, pass steps at the landing frames of their causes, with roll 6-8 f. For a single column that matters (a badge going 9 to 10, the leading digit of a total), build that strip by hand and drive its slot with spr(frame, step, SPR.detent), so it clicks home with the one small overshoot a detent is allowed. Ticks go on step frames, thinned to one per 2-3 f while they are dense, with each of the last three steps ticked.
techniques.timing: Count 60 f on E.out. Column roll 14 f (6-8 f for event counters). Detent landing ~16 f. Ticks at least 2 f apart.
techniques.use_when: Counters with a tactile, product-like feel: totals, balances, counters that step on visible events.
techniques.avoid_when: The film already counts with plain in-place digits (keep one counting style per film); fewer than 3 changes, where one roll is enough.

techniques.name: Ring gauge filling with its centre number
techniques.summary: A circular gauge sweeps to its value while the number at its centre counts on the same progress, and the ring's end cap leads the eye around.
techniques.recipe: Draw an SVG circle rotated -90deg over a C.line track ring, with pathLength={1}, strokeLinecap round and strokeDasharray `${v} 1`, where v = target * prog(frame, at, at + N, E.outSoft) and N = max(48, 0.48 x radius x target) frames, which keeps the end cap at or under 60 px/f (48 f covers a 160 px ring up to 63%; a full 160 px ring needs 77 f). The centre figure is Math.round(100 * v) on fd(frame), in tabular figures with a tucked % at 0.4x size. The arc arrives in C.accent and relaxes to the ink tone over 20 f after landing; for nested rings, stagger them 6 f apart with stagger() so the group lands within 30 f.
techniques.timing: Fill over N = max(48, 0.48 x radius x target) f on E.outSoft (48 f for most gauges, 77 f for a full 160 px ring). Centre count on the same progress. Accent relaxes over 20 f after landing. Nested rings 6 f apart.
techniques.use_when: Percentages, scores, completion and utilisation; status pills and KPI tiles.
techniques.avoid_when: Values that aren't parts of a whole; more than 3 concentric rings.

techniques.name: Before-to-after with a delta chip
techniques.summary: The old figure steps back to a small grey 'before', the new figure counts in at hero size, and a delta chip ('-38%') pops in the accent on the landing frame.
techniques.recipe: At the cue the old hero figure lifts out (0.3 em up, 12 f on E.in through depart, opacity on E.smooth), while a smaller 'before' copy rises into a secondary slot above-left through MaskRise, so the two values never sit crossfaded in one place. The new figure counts at hero size from the old value to the new on E.type over 36 f, and a 2 px C.mute strike draws across the 'before' value over 10 f on E.out. On the count's landing frame, the delta chip (C.accent fill) scales from 0.6 to 1 from its left edge on SPR.micro (no overshoot) with a tick, then its fill relaxes to C.ink2 with accent text over 20 f.
techniques.timing: Old figure exits over 12 f on E.in. 'Before' MaskRise 30 f. New count 36 f on E.type. Strike 10 f on E.out. Chip on the landing frame (SPR.micro, no overshoot), fill relaxes over 20 f. Hold at least 36 f under a breath.
techniques.use_when: Improvements such as cost down, speed up or errors falling from 412 to 3; before-and-after claims.
techniques.avoid_when: The change is small or noisy; the story has no real 'before' state to show.

techniques.name: Unit grid that fills to the count
techniques.summary: A grid of small squares, each standing for a fixed number of units, fills in a diagonal wave while a counter beside it reaches the total, and one cell lands in the accent.
techniques.recipe: Lay out an n x m grid of 14-20 px rounded squares as a C.line track, each square standing for a fixed number of units. Fill cell (r, c) from at + stagger(r + c, n + m - 1, 30, E.out), with opacity over 8 f on E.smooth and scale from 0.6 to 1 on SPR.micro, and fill the last cell by its fraction through a width clip. The counter beside the grid shows filled cells x unit on fd(frame) in tabular figures, so the number and the grid can never disagree. The cell that carries the point (the last one, or 'you') lands in C.accent with scale 1 + 0.15 * hitPulse(t, 2, 8).
techniques.timing: Diagonal wave over 30 f on stagger with E.out. Each cell fades over 8 f, with an SPR.micro scale. Accent cell pulse: attack 2 f, tau 8 f. Hold at least 36 f with a 2% push.
techniques.use_when: Shares and proportions ('3 in 10 teams'), quotas, capacity; making a large count tangible without a chart.
techniques.avoid_when: Exact values with many significant digits, which the grid can't show honestly; cells under 12 px on vertical phone formats.

techniques.name: Area-true ratio comparison
techniques.summary: A multiplier claim ('10x smaller') plays as a block that shrinks in log space to the area the ratio implies, leaving an outline of its old size behind.
techniques.recipe: Draw block A at side s in C.mute, anchored bottom-left on a baseline. At the cue, scale it from that corner with lmix(1, 1/sqrt(ratio), prog(frame, at, at + 48, E.smooth)), so its area ends at 1/ratio and the shrink keeps an even ratio per frame. Its fill mixes to C.accent over the last 12 f, and a 1.5 px C.line outline stays at the original size as the reference. The ratio figure counts beside it on E.type over 36 f and lands on the same frame as the block. For speed or time claims, compare bar lengths (a linear ratio) instead of areas.
techniques.timing: Shrink 48 f on E.smooth via lmix. Fill mixes to the accent over the last 12 f. Ratio count 36 f on E.type, landing with the block. Hold at least 36 f under a 2% breath.
techniques.use_when: Multiplier and reduction claims about size, cost, time or footprint.
techniques.avoid_when: Ratios above ~25x, where the block shrinks to a dot (show the number alone); claims that aren't really proportional.

techniques.name: Device rises already moving
techniques.summary: A phone or app window enters from below already travelling on the cut frame and decelerates into place near centre while the whole shot slowly scales down.
techniques.recipe: Drive the device group's translateY = tw(f, cut − 1, cut + 43, rise, 0, E.out) with rise 140-160 px, so it already moves about 20 px/f on the cut frame (prog is 0 on its first frame, hence cut − 1); no fade-in, since the cut hides the start, and the shadow travels with the device. Under it, scale the whole shot 1 → 0.9 over 48 f on E.outSoft; a desaturated photo backdrop (grayscale(1) contrast(1.1) brightness(0.7)) keeps the device the only colour. When the device must push a title off screen without a cut, rise it from a full frame height below over 48 f on E.glide (peak ≈ 59 px/f at 31%, motion blur on), fade the title on E.smooth starting 16 f before the device moves, and keep the device above the title in z. For anticipation, peek first: 170 px in 14 f on E.out, hover 4 f, then launch the rest on E.whip over 40 f (peak under 70 px/f) and drift the scale 1 → 0.93 over 60 f.
techniques.timing: On a cut: 140-160 px over 44 f on E.out, first frame ≈ 6.2 × rise / 44 (about 20-23 px/f), 75% of the travel by f9, settled by f44; shot scale 1 → 0.9 over 48 f on E.outSoft. Over a title: ≈ 1,000 px in 48 f on E.glide, title fade 36 f starting 16 f early. Peek variant: 14 f peek, 4 f hover, 40 f launch on E.whip, 60 f scale drift.
techniques.use_when: The first product shot after a type card or a photo, when the previous shot's energy should carry straight into the product.
techniques.avoid_when: The device is already on screen; a calm film where a 20 px/f arrival feels pushy; it would be the third rise in a row (vary with a tilt or a pull-back).

techniques.name: Tilted product plane flattens
techniques.summary: A real product page lies tipped back in perspective, rises toward the camera and rotates flat to face the viewer, landing the product as a frontal screen.
techniques.recipe: Give the page's parent perspective 1800-2000 px; on the page set transform-origin 50% 100% and tween translateY 270 → −60 px, rotateX 25° → 8° and scale 1 → 1.3 over 68 f on E.out, then drift linearly at about 3.5 px/f and leave on E.in. Resolve the last 8° → 0 as follow-through on its own E.out over 20 f, starting 6 f before the translate lands, so position and tilt settle at different moments. Hero version: hold the plane tilted for up to 34 f with progressive depth of field (4-6 horizontal bands, each a RackFocus at 0/2/4/6/8 px by distance from the focal row), then rotate rotateX and rotateZ to 0 over 80 f on E.glide while every band racks to sharp as the rotation reaches zero. Edge the page with a 1.5 px solid C.line hairline rather than a lit rim; an in-page headline may build with src/fx/Words.tsx while the plane still moves, but nothing is meant to be read until it lands.
techniques.timing: Rise 68 f on E.out: top edge ≈ 35 px/f on the first frame, ≈ 12 px/f by f4, ≈ 5.5 px/f by f8, then ≈ 3.5 px/f drift and an exit at ≈ 5.5 px/f on E.in; tilt follow-through 20 f, starting 6 f before the position lands; hero de-skew: hold ≤ 34 f, then 80 f on E.glide (peak edge speed ≈ 60-70 px/f at about 31%).
techniques.use_when: Introducing a real web page or app screen as the real thing while keeping the camera alive; the first frontal look at the product.
techniques.avoid_when: The UI must be read during the move; the plane would need more than about 30° of tilt (text shears and aliases); the same flatten ran within the last 10 s.

techniques.name: Hard swap on the cause frame
techniques.summary: On a click or selection the product image, view or value changes in one frame with no crossfade, any price or count rolls up from just below its new value, and a physical card can hide the swap in a small 3D kick.
techniques.recipe: Export the cause frame once (the press of pressAt from src/fx/Cursor.tsx after a hover state shown 6 f earlier, or a selection marker's landing) and switch state on fd(f) >= CAUSE so every motion-blur sub-sample agrees; never crossfade the two states. Re-count numbers with Roll fed countSteps(next − delta, next, CAUSE, 40, E.out), delta about 5-10% of the value, so the digits roll instead of cutting. Punch the swapped object with scale 1 + 0.02 · hitPulse(f − CAUSE, 2, 5). For a print or card beside a list, kick it: perspective 900 px, transform-origin on its left edge, rotateY = 12° · hitPulse(f − CAUSE + 1, 1, 2.5) with skewY 2° on the same envelope and a soft shadow (0 18px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.18)), while the list's selection marker moves 6 f before the swap.
techniques.timing: Swap 1 f on the cause frame; hover 6 f before the press; recount 36-46 f on E.out with 14 f digit rolls; punch attack 2 f, tau 5; kick peaks on the swap frame and settles in 6-8 f; at most one swap per 30 f, 54 f apart in a repeating sequence.
techniques.use_when: A choice changes the product instantly: a variant picker, filter, plan selector, theme switch, a canvas that appears whole on launch.
techniques.avoid_when: The change is a process the viewer should watch; two numbers would sit half-and-half in place; swaps faster than one per 30 f (the clicks read as a macro).

techniques.name: Generated view resolves from soft
techniques.summary: A freshly generated window or row appears as a soft, out-of-focus shape over a flat placeholder plate and snaps into crisp UI in about a third of a second.
techniques.recipe: Mount the finished UI over a flat placeholder plate (C.mist, or C.accent at 12% opacity: one hue only). Render the UI through RackFocus (src/fx/RackFocus.tsx) with blur 20 px and t = 1 − p, p = prog(f, s, s + 20, E.out); fade its opacity 0.6 → 1 and scale it 1.03 → 1 on the same p so the focus pull rides a move, and fade the plate out over the same 20 f on E.smooth. For a list, insert rows one at a time: width 60% → 100% with RackFocus 6 → 0 px over 12 f, siblings pushed down one row over 10 f on E.ui, rows 34-40 f apart; inside an unfolding card, start a row's rack only once 60% of its height is revealed. t must reach 0 by the end, so text lands fully sharp.
techniques.timing: Window: 20 f on E.out (blur 20 → 0 px, opacity 0.6 → 1, scale 1.03 → 1), plate fade 20 f on E.smooth. Rows: 12 f each, push-down 10 f on E.ui, cadence 34-40 f. Card stats row: 12 f, starting once 60% of it is revealed.
techniques.use_when: An AI or build step produces a result and it should read as just arrived, without a spinner.
techniques.avoid_when: The UI was already on screen (use a state change); more than two resolves in one sequence (it becomes a fog filter); type so small that 12 f of softness hurts legibility.

techniques.name: Agent status beat, then streamed answer
techniques.summary: The product's tiny working status is shown at hero size, as a black capsule with a spinner and a typed label or as bare headline type, holds for a beat with a looping ellipsis or shimmer, then dissolves as the answer streams in.
techniques.recipe: Build the status as a capsule (height ≈ 8.4% of frame, border-radius 999 px, C.ink fill, an 8-dot spinner stepping 45° every 6 f, label typed with TypeOn) or as bare type at 72-100 px with a clock or spinner glyph at cap height, its trailing word arriving in C.accent and relaxing to ink with mixColor over 24 f. Keep the hold alive with a looping ellipsis '.'.repeat(1 + (Math.floor(fd(f) / 16) % 3)) and a one-hue shimmer (background-clip: text over three lightness stops of the label grey, band ≈ 120 px, position linear in f), while the camera settles 1.62 → 1 with lmix over 56 f on E.outSoft. Dissolve the status over 12 f on E.smooth, then stream the answer with TypeOn at about 60 cps, the newest three characters at 0.3/0.6/0.85 opacity and each new character in the accent relaxing to ink over 12 f. When the status itself is the payoff, type it, hold 30 f and dim it to C.mute over 12 f instead of streaming.
techniques.timing: Label types in about 30 f (40 f at headline size); hold 60-74 f with the ellipsis stepping every 16 f and one shimmer sweep per 60 f (≈ 20 px/f); camera 1.62 → 1 over 56 f on E.outSoft; dissolve 12 f; stream ≈ 1 character per frame (41 characters in about 42 f); payoff variant: hold 30 f, dim 12 f.
techniques.use_when: An AI or agent product needs its invisible work made visible, and a moment of anticipation before the payoff.
techniques.avoid_when: The product is not autonomous; the hold would run past about 74 f; a second status beat in the same film.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Keep the same beat but build every decoration from one hue: a flat C.ink capsule with a plain soft neutral drop shadow instead of coloured light blobs behind it, a dot spinner or clock glyph instead of a sparkle icon, a shimmer made of three lightness stops of one grey instead of a multi-hue sweep, and an accent-to-ink trail on the newest characters instead of a multi-colour wake.

techniques.name: Headline becomes the product input
techniques.summary: Without a cut the headline turns into the product: a caret appears in the gap between two words, swells into a capsule and widens into the input bar that shoves the words aside, or the sentence inside a card dissolves while the card reshapes into the input.
techniques.recipe: Lay out [wordL][slot][wordR] from data, centred, and bind each word's x to the slot's edges (wordL's right edge = cx − slotW/2 − gap) so the line reflows with no separate tween. Grow the slot as a 3 px C.accent caret (height 0 → line height over 6 f on E.out), hold 8 f, thicken to a 36 px capsule over 14 f, then widen to ≈ 92% of frame on E.rest over 60 f (edge peak ≈ 50 px/f, motion blur on) while its fill goes straight to the opaque input colour; the flanking words ride the edges and, once they pass 20 px/f, fade on E.smooth with blurOut as they leave frame. Populate container-first: icons, a C.mute placeholder and the send button fade in left to right 4 f apart over 12 f each with a 6 px arrive() rise, and the primary button fills last on a 16 f linear ramp. If the sentence already sits in a card, exit its words 6 f apart (the out props of src/fx/Words.tsx), tween the card's height to the input's over 30 f on E.out and fade the placeholder in over 16 f.
techniques.timing: Caret 6 f, hold 8 f, capsule 14 f, widen 60 f on E.rest (a short bar: 23 f in all on E.out); contents 12 f each at a 4 f stagger, button fill 16 f linear. Card variant: word exits 6 f apart, resize 30 f on E.out, placeholder 16 f.
techniques.use_when: Bridging from message to demo in a type-led film; the product's core surface is an input, search or command bar.
techniques.avoid_when: The product is not input-led; the headline has no natural gap; the bar would have to stay translucent over a busy backdrop (go straight to opaque).

techniques.name: Fast prompt at true scale
techniques.summary: The real prompt bar fills with a long, honest instruction in about a second at full legible size, the card growing as lines wrap, then the text is sent up into a chat bubble.
techniques.recipe: Type with TypeOn (src/fx/TypeOn.tsx), either time-boxed (dur 68, ease E.linear, so prompts of any length finish in 68 f and every ask beat keeps its length) or at a fixed 50-72 cps; pre-fill the first word so frame 1 already shows text, and draw the newest three characters at 0.3/0.6/0.85 opacity, each arriving in C.accent and relaxing to ink over 12 f. Grow the card from the measured text box: width ≈ 67% → 77% of frame over the first 24 f, then one line height over 12 f on E.out at each wrap, decided on fd(f). Keep the frame alive with breath(t, 0.025) from src/lib/camera.ts on the camera; the caret is solid while typing and blinks 16 f on / 16 f off only once done. On the send press the composer text fades out over 12 f while the bubble rises 12-20 px through arrive() and fades in over 16-18 f, starting 4 f later.
techniques.timing: Time box 68 f, or 50-72 cps (0.8-1.2 characters per frame); card width 24 f, +1 line per wrap in 12 f on E.out; read hold after typing at least 36 f + 6 f per word, kept alive by the breath; send: 12 f out, bubble 16-18 f in with a 4 f offset.
techniques.use_when: An AI, search or command product whose real input is the story; showing a real task without a dull typing wait.
techniques.avoid_when: The prompt runs past about 100 characters (cut it); a human-paced beat is the point (use 30 cps with human rhythm); the product is not input-driven.

techniques.name: Mark docks into the app
techniques.summary: An integration mark or icon travels to an app tile or page and settles overlapping its face, rising in front of it at the moment of contact, so it reads as plugging in.
techniques.recipe: Move the mark toward the tile centre minus a small offset (15-20% of the tile) over 25 f on E.outSoft so it decelerates into contact; at overlap (frame 17 of the approach) raise its z-index and translateZ above the tile, and let it come to rest on frame 25. On contact the tile answers with scale 1 + 0.02 · hitPulse(f − contact, 2, 3); the tile is a matte solid with a 1.5 px C.line edge and a soft neutral shadow. Shared-element variant: lift a small icon out of its row (scale 0.53 → 1 over 27 f on E.out while its tile inverts light/dark over 18 f), float it 45 f with a linear rotateZ 1.5° and rotateY 4° drift, then shrink it over 12 f on E.inOut into the logo slot of a page that swings in from the bottom right (perspective 1000 px, rotateX 55° → 40°, rotateZ −30° → −22° over 50 f on E.out). Position the icon through the page's own transform and, on the frame it reaches the slot, replace it with the page's own logo in one frame (decided with fd, identical transform) instead of crossfading the two copies.
techniques.timing: Approach 25 f on E.outSoft, overlap at f17, rest at f25; tile bump 2% (attack 2 f, tau 3, about 8 f). Variant: lift 27 f, colour invert 18 f, float 45 f, shrink 12 f on E.inOut, page swing 50 f on E.out, one-frame swap to the page logo on arrival.
techniques.use_when: An integration, plug-in or works-inside claim; handing off from a settings screen into the platform it acts on.
techniques.avoid_when: The mark would pass over text being read; the mark is also the end lockup (it would appear early, so dock an integration icon instead).

techniques.name: Edit with the product's own UI
techniques.summary: Instead of cuts, the film moves between product areas the way the app does: a window recedes to a corner, a sheet slides up, a popover pops from its anchor, a button or card unfolds into a full panel.
techniques.recipe: Model the app as stacked layers in one scene, park the cursor on the control that would trigger each change 6 f before the press, and use the matching native behaviour instead of a cut. Minimize: transform-origin at the trigger corner, scale 1 → 0.7 on E.in over 22 f while opacity falls 1 → 0 over its last 12 f on E.smooth (the far corner is mostly gone before it passes 60 px/f), with the next layer 4 f later. Sheet: translateY 100% → 0 of the window over 52 f on E.glide, clipped to the window. Popover: scale 0.5 → 1 from the trigger point over 12 f on E.outSoft with opacity over its first 4 f, then a 20-40 f camera reframe starting 2 f later. Launch: the sidebar glides left 31% of frame width over 96 f on E.smooth while the main canvas mounts whole on the trigger frame and its greeting starts typing on that frame. Unfold: one element interpolates rect and border-radius from the button or card to the full panel over 28 f on E.rest (longer for a big panel: at least edge travel / 20 f, so no edge passes about 70 px/f) and its title FLIPs to the header slot (scale 1 → 0.6), flying faded whenever it moves faster than 20 px/f; the old content fades out over the first 12 f, the panel content fades in 8 f after the morph peaks, and the stage behind dims over 24 f (a RackFocus at 40 px for a blurred desktop).
techniques.timing: Generic chain: exit on E.in 22 f, gap 4 f, entrance on E.out 52 f. Minimize 22 f; sheet 52 f (peak ≈ 50 px/f); popover 12 f plus a 20-40 f reframe; launch slide 96 f (peak ≈ 18 px/f); unfold 28 f on E.rest (at least edge travel / 20 f), content in 8 f after the peak, stage dim 24 f.
techniques.use_when: Walkthroughs across several product areas; any film where each transition can also demonstrate how the product navigates.
techniques.avoid_when: A purely conceptual or type-led film; desktop chrome that is not part of the brand world; more than one native transition every 3 s (it starts to feel like a screen recording).

techniques.name: Shared element survives the page change
techniques.summary: The cursor clicks a row; the page drains away except the row's icon (or the clicked card), which stays exactly in place while the next page assembles around it with a short zoom-out.
techniques.recipe: Duplicate the anchor (a row's icon, a card or a modal) into a top overlay at its exact screen rect. On the press frame fade page A to its background colour over 6 f on E.smooth and hold the lone anchor 2-4 f. Then mount page B at scale 1.2 about the anchor and settle it with lmix over 24 f on E.out, while the overlay interpolates from A's rect to B's (both computed from layout data, so FLIP by construction) and B's blocks fade in 2 f apart over 10 f. Cross-app variant: keep one card container mounted, take child A out through RackFocus to 8 px with opacity over 36 f, resize the card to the new aspect over 20 f on E.out, and bring child B in from 8 px over 24 f. Cut variant: keep the anchor fixed on a top layer while only the background layer switches on the cut frame, then drag the anchor into its new slot over 40 f on E.whip.
techniques.timing: Hover 12 f, press (pressAt), page A out 6 f, anchor alone 2-4 f, page B 1.2 → 1 over 24 f on E.out (≤ 50 px/f at 960 px from the anchor), block stagger 2 f over 10 f: about 48 f from click to settled. Cross-app: 36 f out, 20 f resize, 24 f in. Cut variant: anchor drag 40 f on E.whip.
techniques.use_when: Navigating into a detail view, or carrying a piece of content between apps, where spatial continuity should make the product feel instant.
techniques.avoid_when: Nothing exists in both states; the anchor is under about 40 px and cannot carry attention; it would need to travel more than a third of the frame (use a native transition).

techniques.name: Flick scroll lands the target
techniques.summary: A list or page scrolls like a trackpad flick, entering already fast or ramping up briefly, then glides on an exponential tail until the target row rests at its reading position.
techniques.recipe: On a cut, start at peak speed with inertia(f, cut, v0, 0.943) from src/lib/anim.ts (v0 ≈ 54 px/f: travel ≈ 920 px, readable after ≈ 49 f, within 0.5 px after its settle). Inside a shot, ramp first: position = vmax·t³/(3·tp²) for t < tp, then vmax·tp/3 + inertia(f, s + tp, vmax, d).x after tp, with decay d 0.93-0.98. Solve vmax = D / (tp/3 + tau), tau = −1/ln d, so the target lands about 15% from the top (a section heading) or at centre, and cap vmax at 60 px/f. Drive text through total · arrive(x / total, 0.98) so the slow tail does not tick, keep the camera itself crisp, and let the motion-blur pass streak the rows above 12 px/f; rows are not meant to be read until they drop below 3 px/f.
techniques.timing: Cut entry: v0 54 px/f, decay 0.943 (tau 17 f), ≈ 76 f to rest. In-shot: ramp tp 28-40 f, vmax 35-60 px/f, tail decay 0.93 for a form section, up to 0.98 for a long volume reel (≈ 277 f for ≈ 2,600 px); readable below 3 px/f.
techniques.use_when: Showing volume (many results, a long page, a feed), or moving down a form to its next section with a human feel.
techniques.avoid_when: The viewer must read during the move; the list is shorter than two screens; it would be the third scroll in a row.

techniques.name: One native control as the demo
techniques.summary: Instead of a screenshot, the feature is shown as the single control that embodies it (a picker wheel, a toggle, a segmented switch) at large scale, centred, with no chrome, doing only its native interaction.
techniques.recipe: Build only that control at 3-5x its native size, centred on an empty stage with no app chrome. For a picker, scroll the column with inertia(f, s, 20, 0.975) from src/lib/anim.ts (≈ 790 px, tau ≈ 40 f, starting at the 20 px/f readable-text limit) and style each item from its distance d to the centre line: scale 1.2 − 0.35 · min(d / 375, 1), colour mixColor(C.ink, C.mute, min(d / 375, 1)), opacity 1 → 0.35 on the same ratio. Either cut while it still drifts, or click the chosen item home with SPR.detent. Toggles and segmented controls keep their real geometry (knob 8 f on E.ui, the selected pill gliding between labels on E.glide).
techniques.timing: Shot ≈ 120 f; picker v0 20 px/f, decay 0.975 per frame, an item crossing focus about every 30 f early on and slowing after; detent settle ≈ 12 f; toggle knob 8 f; segment glide 18-24 f.
techniques.use_when: A settings, targeting or compatibility claim in a type-led film, where one interaction says it is a real product faster than a full UI.
techniques.avoid_when: The feature needs context to make sense; the control is generic (every app has a toggle) and says nothing about the claim.

techniques.name: Drag assets in, skeletons fill
techniques.summary: The cursor drags a fanned stack of images into the input; after the drop they appear as grey skeleton thumbnails that fill with the real images one by one.
techniques.recipe: Build the stack as four image cards rotated −12°, −4°, 4° and 12° that travel with the cursor along cursorArc (src/fx/Cursor.tsx, bow 0.2) on E.smooth, each card evaluated 1 f behind the one above so the fan trails slightly; pressAt marks the pickup and the release. On the drop frame (or just after a cut), mount the thumbnails as C.mist rounded rects in the input's attachment row and fade each image up over 8 f on E.smooth with a 1.04 → 1 scale, i × 8 f apart. The input's other contents shift by FLIP as the row opens over 18 f on E.ui, and the drag path stays clear of any text being read.
techniques.timing: Drag ≈ 72 f on E.smooth; thumbnails 8 f each at a 6-10 f stagger (≈ 36 f for four); attachment row opens over 18 f on E.ui.
techniques.use_when: The product takes real material as input (files, photos, documents) and the viewer should see that context going in.
techniques.avoid_when: The input is text only; the drag path would cross text being read; more than six assets (show a count chip instead).

techniques.name: Pin field pull-back
techniques.summary: A map pulls back from a close view to reveal a field of location pins that drop in as accent marks and relax to ink, then a card grows out of the pin the cursor picks.
techniques.recipe: Scale the map group with k = lmix(2.2, 1, prog(f, s, s + 50, E.outSoft)) about the focus point. Pop the pins during the pull with SPR.micro (no visible overshoot: a field of pins is not a landing) on scale 0 → 1 and translateY −12 → 0 px, transform-origin at the bottom centre, with offsets from stagger(i, n, 30) so the whole group lands within 30 f; each pin arrives in C.accent and relaxes to C.ink over 24 f (mixColor). The cursor clicks one pin and its card grows from the pin tip (transform-origin at the pin, scale 0.6 → 1 over 12 f on E.out), with a leader line drawing over 8 f and its label sliding 25 px over 12 f on E.out.
techniques.timing: Pull 50 f on E.outSoft (first frame ≈ −7% scale per frame); pins ≈ 11 f each on SPR.micro, the group within 30 f (2-6 f apart); colour relax 24 f; card 12 f, leader 8 f, label 12 f.
techniques.use_when: Location, coverage, store-finder or delivery features; any everywhere claim backed by real places.
techniques.avoid_when: Fewer than about five locations; a map style busy enough to hide the pins; a route arc has already run on the same map.

techniques.name: Before/after drag divider
techniques.summary: The cursor grabs a vertical divider on the product and drags it across, wiping away the old state to reveal the new one in the same layout.
techniques.recipe: Stack two renders of the same layout: before below, after above, clipped with clip-path inset(0 0 0 X px) where X is the divider's position; draw the divider as a 2 px C.white line (C.ink on paper) with a 40 px round handle holding two small chevrons. The cursor arrives on cursorArc over 36-48 f on E.out, presses the handle (pressAt) and drags it across the product panel on E.smooth over 60 f (≈ 1,100 px, peak ≈ 52 px/f). Optionally it pauses once at the midpoint for up to 24 f under a breath push so both states read side by side. Values that differ between the states change exactly where the divider passes them, because they sit on separate layers, so the halves are never crossfaded.
techniques.timing: Cursor approach 36-48 f on E.out; press 4 f down, 8 f recoil; drag 60 f on E.smooth, or 36 f to the midpoint on E.glide (peak ≈ 46 px/f), a hold of ≤ 24 f, then 36 f on to the edge.
techniques.use_when: Redesigns, image or audio cleanup, performance gains, any this-got-better claim with a visible difference.
techniques.avoid_when: The two states differ in layout (the wipe then reads as a glitch); the difference is invisible at frame size; the film has no human gesture anywhere else.

techniques.name: Long page flown like a runway
techniques.summary: A whole long page lies on a steeply tilted plane that recedes to a horizon, and the view travels along it faster and faster, so the page reads as one landscape and is cut at full speed.
techniques.recipe: Lay the whole page out as live components at desktop width inside a runway plane about 75% of frame width and 2x frame height long (overflow hidden), in a full-frame parent with perspective 1200 px and its perspective-origin at frame centre; give the plane transform-origin 50% 100%, rotateX(55deg) and put its bottom edge on the frame's bottom edge, so its far edge recedes to a horizon about 25% down the frame and its sides converge like a runway. Move the page inside the plane, never the camera: translateY = Y0 + 6n + 0.225n² for n = f − s up to 54 (plane speed 6 → 30 px/f), then +36 px per frame to the cut, so content streams toward the viewer and the page's upper sections emerge from the horizon (start with its lower sections on the plane so the hero arrives last); at the near edge the screen speed is about 0.95x the plane speed and the far half moves much slower. Fade the far end with an alpha mask on the plane, mask-image linear-gradient(to top, #000 45%, transparent 95%), so the stage colour swallows the horizon in one hue, and keep the empty stage above the horizon as the caption band, where one short line lands with src/fx/Words.tsx in screen space while the page streams below it. Nothing on the plane is meant to be read: keep the motion-blur pass on for the whole flight and cut on its last, fastest frame into a shot that opens moving the same way.
techniques.timing: Flight 80 f: plane speed 6 → 30 px/f over 54 f (closed form 6n + 0.225n², linear acceleration with no ease-out), then 36 px/f for 26 f into the cut, about 1,900 px of travel (page at least plane length + 2,000 px); near-edge screen speed ≈ 6 → 34 px/f, under the blur pass throughout; rotateX 55°, perspective 1200 px, plane 2x frame height; caption words 6 f apart, landed by f40 of the flight; cut on the final frame.
techniques.use_when: Showing the length or completeness of a page, document, feed or site in about a second without asking anyone to read it; a fast connective beat between two readable product shots, or the carrier for a change made mid-move, such as a theme switch.
techniques.avoid_when: The content must be read, the page is short (it reads as a tilted card instead), or the frame is vertical and leaves too little runway; use it once per film.

techniques.name: Ghost suggestion accepted with a key
techniques.summary: As someone types, the product proposes the rest of the line as pale ghost text after the caret; a small key chip appears, the key is pressed, and the ghost text inks in left to right as the caret jumps to its end.
techniques.recipe: Type the user's prefix with TypeOn at a human 30 cps; 12 f after the last key, draw the suggestion as one span starting at the prefix's caretX from typeOn(), in the same font and baseline and in C.mute, appearing whole on one frame (or streaming at 2 characters per frame for a longer block), so nothing already typed reflows. Twelve px past its last glyph (or under the line end if that would cross the field edge), mount a key chip (a FONT.mono label at 0.6 em in a 6 px-radius box with a 1.5 px C.line border and a 3 px bottom edge) on spr(f, s, SPR.micro) from scale 0.8 with opacity over 6 f, and keep the 30-40 f wait alive with breath(t, 0.02) on the camera. On ACCEPT the chip presses with pressAt (translateY 2 px and its bottom edge 3 → 1 px, both times the press value), and on that frame a recolour front runs through the ghost text, k = fd(prog(f, ACCEPT − 1, ACCEPT + 10, E.linear) × n): each character behind the front switches from C.mute to C.accent on its frame and relaxes to C.ink over 12 f by its own age (mixColor), while the prefix caret is removed (caretOut = ACCEPT) and a caret appears at the suggestion's end on the same frame. The chip fades out over 8 f on E.smooth from ACCEPT + 4; in a multi-line block each line's front starts 3 f after the line above, and a rejection uses the same chip labelled Esc with the ghost text fading out over 8 f on E.smooth.
techniques.timing: Prefix at 30 cps; ghost text 12 f after the last key, whole in 1 f (or 2 characters per frame); chip on SPR.micro with a 6 f fade; wait 30-40 f under a 2% breath; press 4 f down, 8 f recoil; recolour front 10 f per line (lines 3 f apart), accent relax 12 f; chip out over 8 f from ACCEPT + 4; read hold after acceptance 36-48 f.
techniques.use_when: An assistant that completes text, code, email or form fields inline: the moment the product does the work is one key away, and the cause (the key) and the effect (the ink) share a frame.
techniques.avoid_when: The product generates whole answers rather than inline completions (stream the answer instead), or the suggestion runs past about two lines at readable size; never show more than two accepts in a row.

techniques.name: List narrows with each keystroke
techniques.summary: A shortcut opens a command palette or search field, and as the query types the list answers every key: non-matching rows fold away, survivors slide up, matched letters ink in, and the highlight rides the top result until Enter.
techniques.recipe: Open with the shortcut if the product has one: two key chips (FONT.mono labels, 1.5 px C.line border, 3 px bottom edge) appear 4 f apart and press together with pressAt, and on the press frame the palette scales 0.96 → 1 about its top centre with opacity over 10 f on E.outSoft while the app behind racks to 8 px through RackFocus under a 20% C.ink veil over 12 f. Type the query with TypeOn at 30-40 cps and recompute the matches from the data on each key frame (typeFrames(), decided on fd(f)), so the list is a pure function of the characters typed: rows that stop matching fold from row height to 0 over 10 f on E.ui with their opacity gone in the first 6 f, and survivors FLIP to their new slots from the computed list layout over max(12, 0.14 × distance) f on E.ui, so no label passes 20 px/f. In every surviving label the matched characters switch to C.ink on the key frame while the rest drops to C.mute (colour only, never weight, so nothing reflows), and one shared highlight (C.mist, 8 px radius) always sits behind the top result and FLIPs to its new rect over 8 f on E.ui. On Enter (a single chip press) the chosen row takes a C.accent 12% tint for 6 f and the palette closes, scale 1 → 0.98 with opacity out over 8 f on E.smooth, while the result mounts underneath on the press frame.
techniques.timing: Chips 4 f apart, press 4 f down + 8 f recoil; palette 10 f on E.outSoft, backdrop rack and veil 12 f; query 30-40 cps; row fold 10 f on E.ui (opacity 6 f); survivor FLIP max(12, 0.14 × px) f on E.ui; highlight 8 f on E.ui; 4-7 keys narrow 8-10 rows to 1-3; final list held 24-36 f under a 2% breath before Enter; close 8 f.
techniques.use_when: Search, command menus, filters and pickers: any product whose speed claim is 'type a few letters and it is there', proving instant results without a spinner.
techniques.avoid_when: The rows are illegible at frame size (punch in first), or the query is long (past about 12 characters it becomes a typing beat); do not FLIP more than about ten rows at once.

techniques.name: Scrub a chart with a live readout
techniques.summary: The cursor glides across a chart; a hairline and a dot ride the series beneath it and a small readout shows the date and value at that point, stepping from data point to data point until it lands on the one that makes the claim.
techniques.recipe: Build the chart from data in one SVG and make the scrub a pure function of the cursor's x: move src/fx/Cursor.tsx along a shallow cursorArc (bow 0.05) on E.smooth at 6-10 px/f, and take the active point i as the data point nearest that x, decided on fd(f).
