Layer back to front: series, a 1.5 px C.line hairline at point i's x, a 6 px solid dot on the series at point i with a 2 px ring in the stage colour, the readout, then the cursor; the hairline and dot snap from point to point as i changes (use 40 or more points so each snap is small; with sparse data let the hairline follow the cursor x and snap only the dot and value). The readout is a small card (8 px radius, C.ink on paper or C.white on ink) with a FONT.mono date in C.mute above the value in tabular figures; it rides along the plot's top edge at the cursor's x, clamped inside the plot so it never flips sides, and its value changes through Roll fed one step per index change (roll 8) so digits roll instead of cutting. The hairline and readout fade in over 6 f as the cursor crosses into the plot, and the scrub ends on the point that carries the claim, where the dot pulses at scale 1 + 0.25 · hitPulse(f − LAND, 2, 6) and the value arrives in C.accent and relaxes to C.ink over 24 f.
techniques.timing: Scrub 90-150 f on E.smooth at 6-10 px/f (the readout never moves faster than the cursor); hairline and readout in over 6 f; value roll 8 f per index change; landing pulse attack 2 f, tau 6; accent relax 24 f; hold on the landing point 36-48 f under a 2% breath.
techniques.use_when: Analytics, finance, health or monitoring products whose value is reading any point in history; a calm interaction beat after a fast one.
techniques.avoid_when: The chart has no point worth landing on, or the readout is illegible at the framing (punch in to 1.6-2x first); never scrub faster than the readout can be read.

techniques.name: Command runs, output prints in bursts
techniques.summary: A command is typed at human speed and entered; the terminal answers machine-fast, printing whole lines in uneven bursts with a stepping spinner and a progress bar, and ends on a single success line.
techniques.recipe: Set the terminal in FONT.mono at no less than TYPE.ui size, in a C.ink2 window with a 1.5 px edge, with every line laid out from data on a fixed line height, and keep breath(t, 0.02) on the camera for the whole run. Type the command with TypeOn at a human 30 cps with fade 0 (keys appear whole), hold the caret 10 f, then enter on a quiet tick. Output never types: each line appears whole on its own frame from a hand-written schedule of uneven bursts (for example 3 lines on consecutive frames, a 14 f gap, 5 lines 2 f apart, a 22 f gap), decided on fd(f), with the newest line in C.white and older ones relaxing to C.mute over 24 f; once text reaches the bottom row, each burst scrolls the content up by its total height as one move over max(6, 0.14 × distance) f on E.ui, so text never passes 20 px/f. A working line steps the four-glyph ASCII spinner (bar, slash, dash, backslash) every 4 f beside a text progress bar whose filled cells advance on fd(prog(f, a, a + 60, E.smooth) × cells), and the run ends on one success line whose check mark and key word arrive in C.accent and stay, followed by a fresh prompt with the caret blinking 30 f on, 30 f off.
techniques.timing: Command at 30 cps, caret hold 10 f; bursts of 2-6 lines 1-2 f apart with 10-24 f gaps (40-80 lines in 120-180 f reads machine-fast); line relax 24 f; burst scroll max(6, 0.14 × px) f on E.ui; spinner step 4 f; progress bar 60 f on E.smooth; success line held 48-60 f under the breath with the caret blinking 30/30.
techniques.use_when: Developer tools, CLIs, infrastructure and build products, where the contrast between a human-typed command and machine-fast output is the speed claim.
techniques.avoid_when: The audience is not technical, or the output itself must be read line by line (show the result screen instead); never type the output.

techniques.name: Change applied as a visible diff
techniques.summary: A proposed edit lands in a code or document view as a diff: outgoing lines strike through and fold away, incoming lines open in place with a marker in the gutter, and the view steps hunk by hunk before the change is accepted.
techniques.recipe: Render the file as live lines from data (FONT.mono for code, the text face for prose) beside a gutter of line numbers, and drive each hunk from its own start frame. An outgoing line first gets a 1.5 px C.mute strike that draws left to right over 8 f on E.ui (scaleX 0 → 1 from the left) while its text dims to C.mute; 6 f later it folds from line height to 0 over 12 f on E.ui, its opacity gone in the first 8 f. On that same frame an incoming slot opens from 0 to line height over 12 f on E.ui (the lines below are pushed through the computed layout), a 3 px C.accent bar appears in the gutter on its first frame, the new text appears whole once the slot is 70% open, and a C.accent 10% row tint relaxes to clear over 36 f while the bar stays; line numbers below recompute on fd(f) and are never tweened. Step to the next hunk 60-90 f later with the anchor camera (lc to a Shot centred on it) over 48 f on E.glide, keeping each hop under about 300 px (peak ≈ 19 px/f) and hard-cutting on the same axis to anything farther; on Accept (a Cursor press with pressAt on the button) every gutter bar fades over 12 f on E.smooth and the clean file holds under breath(t, 0.02).
techniques.timing: Strike 8 f on E.ui; fold 12 f on E.ui starting 6 f later; slot open 12 f on E.ui with the text in at 70%; tint relax 36 f; hunks 60-90 f apart, camera hop 48 f on E.glide (≤ 300 px); accept fade 12 f; final hold 36-48 f under a 2% breath; at most three hunks.
techniques.use_when: AI coding or writing assistants and review, versioning or migration tools, when the claim is 'it changes exactly the right lines and shows you which'.
techniques.avoid_when: The code is unreadable at frame size (macro in first), or the change needs more than three hunks (show a summary instead); never give removals a second colour.

techniques.name: Several people at work at once
techniques.summary: Two or three named cursors move and act on the same canvas at the same time, each in its own rhythm, while presence avatars stack in the corner, so collaboration reads without a word.
techniques.recipe: Draw each collaborator as src/fx/Cursor.tsx plus a name flag pinned 14 px right and 18 px below the tip (a 6 px-radius label with an initial and first name in C.white on C.ink, C.ink2 or C.mute), so identity comes from the label rather than from colour and the one accent stays free for the newest edit. Script each person as a list of {to, at, action} beats: travel on cursorArc (bow 0.15-0.25, its sign from rand(name)) on E.smooth at 6-14 px/f, with every start shifted by rand(name + i) × 10 f so no two cursors arrive or press on the same frame. Between beats each cursor wanders: every 24 f it eases on E.smooth to a new point within 6 px of its rest, picked with rand(name + floor(f / 24)), so no hand ever freezes. Each action lands on that person's press frame (pressAt): a note dropped onto the canvas on SPR.firm, a shape dragged with the item evaluated 2 f behind the cursor, or a label typed with TypeOn at 30 cps beside the flag; the newest edit takes a 2 px C.accent outline for 24 f, then relaxes to C.line. In the top bar, overlapping 28 px avatar circles with initials scale in on spr(f, join, SPR.micro) as each cursor first enters the frame.
techniques.timing: Shot 180-240 f; travel 6-14 px/f on E.smooth, arrivals and presses at least 6 f apart; wander ≤ 6 px per 24 f; one action every 30-50 f across all cursors; note settle on SPR.firm ≈ 16 f; accent outline 24 f; avatars on SPR.micro 6-10 f each; at most three cursors.
techniques.use_when: Collaborative documents, whiteboards, design and planning tools: anything whose claim is 'together, live'.
techniques.avoid_when: A single-user product, or a frame where the name flags would be too small to read; never more than three cursors, which turns into noise.

techniques.name: Mark slides aside, name follows
techniques.summary: The centred mark glides sideways, shrinking if it was hero-sized, to open its slot, and the name resolves beside it just before the mark stops, so the lockup forms in one gesture.
techniques.recipe: Lay the finished lockup out first: LOCKUP token with mark height = the name's cap height, gap = 0.25-0.4x the mark height, and the name's width from measureTracked. Then slide the mark from frame centre to its lockup slot with x = tw(f, a, a+D, 0, -(nameW + gap)/2, E.smooth). If it was larger as a hero, scale it lmix(heroK, 1, same progress) with heroK about 1.6. Start the name when the slide passes 55-60% of its progress. As one block: opacity on E.smooth, blurIn(p, 10), translateX +30 -> 0 on E.out. Per letter: the same over 16 f at a 3 f stagger, with colour mixColor(C.mute, C.ink, p) so letters arrive grey and settle to ink. From the name's resolve, tighten its letter-spacing from +0.04 em to the TYPE.display track over 46 f on E.out; this hands into the hold's push. For a round mark, add roll: rotate = -(dx / r) * 180/pi degrees, so it rolls without slipping and stops exactly when x does. In 9:16, stack instead: the mark rises by (nameH + gap)/2 and the name rises in under it with MaskRise.
techniques.timing: Slide: 36 f for up to ~250 px (E.smooth peaks ~20 px/f), 60 f for ~350 px (~17 px/f). Motion-blur pass on the mark whenever it moves faster than 12 px/f. Name starts at 0.55-0.6 x D: a block takes 14 f; letters take 16 f each at a 3 f stagger (10 letters inside ~43 f). Tracking: 46 f on E.out. Lockup resolved by about D + 20 f, then hold 90-120 f.
techniques.use_when: Any end card whose mark is already on screen (it was the story device or the hero) and the name still has to arrive. The default lockup build.
techniques.avoid_when: The mark has not been seen yet (give it its own beat first). The film already used a slide-to-make-room for the product. Long names that would push the slide past ~400 px (stack vertically instead).

techniques.name: Name types backwards, group stays centred
techniques.summary: The name appears from its last letter to its first while the mark is pushed outward, so the lockup grows out of the mark's edge and stays centred on every frame.
techniques.recipe: Lay out [mark][gap][name], with every character laid out from the start and untyped characters at opacity 0. Measure each character's advance with measureTracked. Character i of n shows from frame t0 + 3.5 * (n-1-i), decided on fd, with a 4 f opacity ramp on E.ui, so the name grows leftward from its last letter. Keep the group centred without stepping: markLeft = cx - (markW + gap + ws(f))/2, where ws(f) = sum of adv_k * spr(f, t_k, SPR.firm) over the characters revealed so far. That is one critically damped spring per character, which glides the mark outward as each letter lands. If the story device is a dot, let it become the mark in place first: fill mixColor(C.mist, C.ink, p) over 12 f on E.smooth, with the glyph inside fading in over the last 4 f.
techniques.timing: 3.5 f per character (10 characters in 36 f), each fading in over 4 f on E.ui. Each width step eases on SPR.firm (no overshoot, ~20 f to settle). The mark travels ~270 px at 7-8 px/f on average. Dot-to-mark darkening takes 12 f. The lockup settles ~20 f after the last character, then holds 90-120 f under a 10-15% push (le-living-hold).
techniques.use_when: Agent, assistant or persona products whose mark is an avatar or a disc. Names of 4-12 characters. A centred lockup that must never jump.
techniques.avoid_when: Two-word names whose second word makes no sense on its own first. Right-to-left scripts (it becomes an ordinary type-on). The headline already used a typewriter.

techniques.name: Pull out of the mark, undershoot, breathe
techniques.summary: The mark arrives so large that only fragments of it fill the frame, collapses to slightly smaller than its final size, then gently breathes up to rest, as if the camera had found it.
techniques.recipe: Place the Mark with placeMark at its final spot; centre it where the lockup needs it, e.g. 80 px left of frame centre to leave room for the name. Pick the start scale s0 so the mark's outer edge starts about 750 px from its centre (s0 = 750 / the mark's half-width at rest, about 5x for a 300 px mark), so only fragments fill the frame. Scale it about its own centre in log space: s = lmix(s0, 0.93, prog(f, a, a+N, E.outSoft)) * lmix(1, 1/0.93, prog(f, a+N-24, a+N, E.smooth)), with N = 43 x ln(s0 / 0.93) frames (72 f from 5x). The log rate then starts near 0.105/f, so the outer edge never passes about 80 px/f; from 5x it crosses 1.0 near f35, bottoms out at 0.94 near f52 and breathes up to rest at 1.0 by f72 with no velocity step. Enter it on a cut: the outgoing shot shrinks into its centre on E.in over its last 24 f and cuts at a matching log speed (or start from zoomHandoff in camera.ts at the outgoing log speed). Render with the motion-blur pass. Keep the mark's counters and small parts outside the frame until the log rate falls below 0.07/f (~f10). Put the bottom of the undershoot on the strongest low hit after a ~15 f bass gap.
techniques.timing: Collapse: N = 43 x ln(s0 / 0.93) frames on E.outSoft (72 f from 5x; log rate about 0.105/f at the start, outer edge under about 80 px/f, under 0.07/f by f10). Breathe: the last 24 f on E.smooth (0.93 -> 1.0), bottoming at 0.94 near f52. Settled by f72. Hold the mark ~20 f before the name follows.
techniques.use_when: The mark's first full appearance at the end, or a logo sting. A hit after a short bass gap. Marks with a strong silhouette or inner shapes that read as abstract fragments when huge.
techniques.avoid_when: Thin line marks (at macro scale they become two hairlines crossing the frame). Right after another zoom-through seam. The mark was already shown at hero size earlier (that makes this a replayed reveal).

techniques.name: Dark slam, spin and brighten
techniques.summary: After a near-still beat, giant low-contrast arms of the mark sweep over the frame, and the mark rushes back to logo size while spinning into place and brightening to full contrast.
techniques.recipe: Hold the card before it (the URL or last line) almost still, drifting at most 0.3 px/f, and end that hold with a designed freeze of at most 15 f on silence. Then start the mark at full speed with no ease-in, centred on the frame. Scale s = lmix(12, 1, prog(f, a, a+66, E.outSoft)); rotation tw(f, a, a+60, -70, 0, E.outSoft) degrees; fill mixColor(C.ink2, C.white, p*p) with p = 1 - ln(s)/ln(12). The fastest frames are then dark grey on a C.ink stage and cannot strobe, and full contrast arrives only as the mark slows. Blur the previous text out underneath (blurOut over 10 f), and keep the motion-blur pass on while the log rate is above 0.05/f (about the first 18 f).
techniques.timing: 66 f. Log rate 0.17/f at f0, 0.10 at f10, 0.04 at f20. Spin 5.2 deg/f at the start, 2.8 deg/f by f10, at rest by f60. Fill 31% of the way to white at f10, 70% at f20, 97% at f40. Preceded by a near-still hold of 60-90 f that ends in a freeze of at most 15 f.
techniques.use_when: The finale of a high-energy film, where the single biggest motion spike follows the single biggest stillness. Radially symmetric or rotational marks (asterisks, petals, rings).
techniques.avoid_when: Marks with an obvious up direction that look wrong at -70 deg (lettermarks). Calm films. Films that already used a spin or a fast zoom-out seam.

techniques.name: Seed build with stroke draw-on
techniques.summary: The mark grows from a small seed while its strokes, stripes or arcs draw on in a quick stagger, so it assembles itself in about half a second and the label rises in beside it.
techniques.recipe: Build the mark from named parts (Mark pieces with per-piece transforms). Grow the body from a seed with scale lmix(0.2, 1, prog(f, a, a+54, E.out)) about its centre. Draw each line part on with stroke-dasharray = its length L and stroke-dashoffset = L * (1 - p). Reveal each filled stripe through a mask rect whose scaleX goes 0 -> 1 from one end. Part i starts at a + 6 + 6i and runs 10 f on E.out. When the last part lands, raise the label letter by letter from behind its baseline: each glyph sits in an overflow-hidden line box and moves translateY 100% -> 0 through arrive (or use MaskRise for whole words). Then push the whole group gently through the hold.
techniques.timing: Seed growth: 54 f on E.out (about 0.2x -> 1; first-frame edge speed ~4 px/f). Parts: 10 f each, 6 f apart (3 parts inside ~28 f). Label glyphs: 2 f apart, 12 f each on E.out. The whole mark reads within ~0.5 s. Then a 90-120 f hold that pushes from 1.0 to 1.10-1.15 on E.dolly (le-living-hold).
techniques.use_when: Geometric marks made of a body plus lines, stripes or orbits. A fresh logo reveal after a hard cut to a clean stage. Stings that must show the mark within 0.5 s.
techniques.avoid_when: Solid single-shape marks (there is nothing to draw). Marks with more than ~5 parts (it turns into a slow queue). The mark already exists on screen as the story device.

techniques.name: Liquid blob resolves into the mark
techniques.summary: A dot, or two soft lobes sliding in from the sides, swells into a liquid blob that stretches, splits and snaps into the crisp geometric mark.
techniques.recipe: Draw the mark's primitives as SVG circles and rects in one group, all starting stacked on the seed dot, and move each to its final place on E.smooth with a 2-4 f stagger. Two-lobe version: two large rounded shapes move translateX +/-600 -> +/-160 px on E.outSoft, fuse at centre and frame the closing line. Filter the group with feGaussianBlur stdDeviation 10, then feColorMatrix (type matrix, alpha row '0 0 0 18 -7'), which thresholds the blur into a liquid neck wherever parts are close. Over the last 8 f, ramp stdDeviation 10 -> 0. On the frame it reaches 0, swap the filtered group for the crisp Mark at the identical transform: a one-frame swap of identical shapes, never a crossfade. Use flat fills only; the threshold makes hard edges, and rim lights or inner highlights would be eaten or look like neon.
techniques.timing: 46 f. Parts travel f0-38 on E.smooth at a 2-4 f stagger, and the blob visibly splits ~26 f in. Blur ramp and crisp swap over the last 8 f. Two-lobe version: converge in 40 f on E.outSoft (first frame ~49 px/f, motion-blur pass on), then drift 0.3-0.5 px/f under the line.
techniques.use_when: Products about raw input becoming structure, or about merging and joining. The story device is a dot. Marks made of a few separate primitives.
techniques.avoid_when: Marks with thin strokes or text inside (the threshold eats them). Brands that need crisp precision throughout. Films already using a soft morph seam.

techniques.name: Staircase echo shape morph
techniques.summary: A large brand shape collapses into a slim pill around the URL, and mid-morph its moving edges show stepped echoes from staggered copies, like a mechanical transformation.
techniques.recipe: Animate one rounded rect from the big shape to a pill that hugs the URL over 48 f on E.smooth, using morphBox from Morph.tsx or width, height and radius directly. Render 7 copies behind it: copy k samples the same morph at frame f - 2k and draws as a 1.5 px stroke (no fill) with opacity 0.6 * (1 - k/9) in one tonal step of the stage colour. The copies show only where the shape moves, stack into a staircase along the moving edges, and coincide and vanish once it rests. The URL swaps in at the start of the morph (8 f fade on E.smooth) and stays still once the pill lands.
techniques.timing: Morph: 48 f on E.smooth, height 983 -> 227 px (edge peak ~22 px/f), width 1878 -> 997 px with a long tail. 7 copies at a 2 f delay each (14 f of echo after the leader stops). The URL stays readable for at least 102 f afterwards, under the card's 10-15% push (le-living-hold).
techniques.use_when: Turning a big brand shape or frame into the CTA container. Mechanical, engineered or developer-tool brands. One moment that should feel designed rather than tweened.
techniques.avoid_when: Short moves (under ~150 px the echoes collapse into a smear). Elements that already carry motion blur (double trails). More than once per film.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Draw the echoes as plain 1.5 px strokes in one tonal step of the stage (C.ink2 on C.ink, C.line on C.paper) with a linear opacity falloff. No rim light, bloom or coloured edges on the copies.

techniques.name: Story object becomes the mark
techniques.summary: The film's last object (a dot, circle, coin or pill) ends at exactly the mark's screen position and size, and the mark replaces it by a hard cut or an in-place morph, so the logo arrives as the answer to the story.
techniques.recipe: Compute the mark's final rect first (placeMark). Drive the story object so its last frame lands on that rect, or on 0.57 of it for the cut-and-grow ending, with matched centre, size, radius and colour. Examples: a coin turning rotateY 90 -> 10 deg on E.outSoft while it rises 20% of H; a word deleting from both ends (slice(k, n - k), k + 1 every 5 f) while its pill hugs the text down to a circle; a pill whose width collapses to the icon's rounded square (Morph on E.inOut). Then either hard-cut to the flat mark at exactly the object's last position and size (0.57 of the rect) and grow it lmix(0.57, 1, prog(f, cut, cut + 18, E.out)) about its centre, with half the growth in the first 2 f and no overshoot. Or finish in place: the dot's fill darkens to the mark's ink (mixColor over 12 f on E.smooth) and its glyph fades in over the last 4 f. Nothing may blink, double or change style across the seam, not even for one frame.
techniques.timing: Coin flip: 22 f on E.outSoft. Two-ended delete: 5 f per letter pair, pill width eased 4 f per step on E.ui. Pill-to-square morph: 30-40 f on E.inOut. Cut pop: 18 f on E.out (0.57 -> 1). In-place darkening: 12 f. Then hold ~20 f before the name follows.
techniques.use_when: Every film that has a story device: the default way to arrive at the mark, especially as the device's third and final use.
techniques.avoid_when: There is no recurring object (a mark forced out of an unrelated shape reads as a pun). The object's shape and the mark's disagree (a square into a circle needs a morph, never a cut).

techniques.name: Words part, URL types into the gap
techniques.summary: The closing line splits at its middle, both halves slide outward and dim, the URL types letter by letter into the gap, and the flanks fade so the URL holds alone.
techniques.recipe: Set the closing line as two spans that meet at the centre. Split them apart by +/-(urlWidth/2 + 40 px) over 44 f on E.smooth, with colour mixColor(C.ink, C.mute, p) so they dim but stay legible. From 40% of the split, type the URL centred in the gap with TypeOn: 1 character per 4 f, head fade 4 f, caret hidden once done. After the last key, fade the flanks to 0 over 16 f on E.smooth. Keep the URL still on the card while the card pushes 10-15% on E.dolly; the mark then joins above it, or the URL becomes the lockup's secondary line.
techniques.timing: Split: 44 f on E.smooth over 250-300 px (peak 20 px/f or less). URL starts at 40% of the split, 4 f per character. Flank fade: 16 f after the last key. URL readable and still for at least 102 f.
techniques.use_when: The closing line is a two-word phrase or pun built around the product, and the CTA is a URL. Minimal, type-only films.
techniques.avoid_when: Lines longer than ~4 words. Films with no typing anywhere else (it would add a new device at the very end). URLs too long for the gap to open within the safe width.

techniques.name: Card shrinks to a pill, words close in
techniques.summary: The last content card empties and shrinks into a small pill while the tagline words slide in from beyond the frame edges, blurred to sharp, to sit on either side of it; then the logo appears inside the pill.
techniques.recipe: Build a flex row [wordL][slot][wordR] and animate the slot's width from the card's width to the pill's width. Use Morph for the slot's box: radius to h/2, fill from the card surface to a solid tonal step of the stage. The words are then carried in from off-frame by the layout alone. Fade the card's content out over the first 6 f, before the slot moves fast, and shrink on E.whip. The words get blurIn(p, 8) and opacity prog(..., E.smooth), so they fly faded and resolve sharp on landing. When the pill lands, fade the Mark in inside it over 14 f on E.smooth. The row stays centred on the frame throughout.
techniques.timing: Content fade: 6 f. Shrink: 30 f on E.whip (card ~1240 -> ~310 px; each word travels ~470 px at a peak of ~58 px/f with the motion-blur pass on, faded until it lands). Logo fade: 14 f, starting 8 f after the pill lands. Then hold 90-120 f under a 10-15% push (le-living-hold).
techniques.use_when: Films that opened with a gap or pill inside a headline (the reverse closes the bookend). Products whose output is a card, post, message or result. A tagline that brackets the brand: [wordL] [mark] [wordR].
techniques.avoid_when: There is no card on screen to collapse. Words too long to fit beside the pill inside the safe width. Light-on-light stages where the pill loses its edge.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Make the pill opaque: a solid tonal step of the stage (C.ink2 on C.ink, C.mist on C.paper), optionally with a 1.5 px C.line stroke. No translucent fill and no backdrop blur over the background.

techniques.name: CTA line closes its gaps
techniques.summary: The end line starts with exaggerated spaces between its words, which close as the line settles centred; the last word, often the URL, travels farthest, so the eye ends there.
techniques.recipe: Lay the final line out centred. Give word i a start offset off_i = 70 + 80 * i px (capped at 290 px) in the direction of travel, so the last word travels farthest. Drive each word as x_i = finalX_i + off_i - inertia(f, a, off_i/14.6, 0.934).x: a pure exponential close with tau = 14.6 f and no overshoot (horizontal moves need no arrive). Enter on a hard cut from a larger line whose total width matches this line's stretched width. Optionally keep the URL soft for 8 f after it stops, then resolve it over 14 f with RackFocus, so focus is the last thing to settle.
techniques.timing: tau = 14.6 f: 55% closed in 10 f, 95% by 44 f. The last word starts at no more than 20 px/f and only slows from there. Gaps of ~150/115/80 px close to a normal word space (~0.25 em). URL focus: soft for 8 f, resolved over 14 f.
techniques.use_when: A one-line CTA (a sentence plus a URL) after a large type beat. Type-led films whose last beat is a phrase locking together.
techniques.avoid_when: Lines that wrap to two rows. Films that already closed a word gap earlier. Vertical frames where the stretched line would exceed the safe width.

techniques.name: The product clears the stage
techniques.summary: The last product element leaves (dropping out of frame, accelerating away, or bursting outward toward camera), and the brand, already waiting behind it, starts its reveal on the exact frame it is uncovered.
techniques.recipe: Keep the brand layer (stage plus lockup) mounted under the product for the whole shot, so the exit uncovers it instead of cutting to it. Exit the product one of three ways. (1) Time-reverse its own entrance with progress = 1 - entrance(1 - t); for a window this is typically a ~1000 px drop over 44 f on E.smooth. (2) Float a lone card up from its drift over 25 f on E.in while it grows 1 -> 1.33. (3) Burst a card cluster outward: each card translates 300-450 px along its vector from the cluster centre and scales lmix(1, 3) over 20 f on E.in, and the card layer is removed on the frame its fastest card passes ~75 px/f. Start the brand reveal on the frame the product's edge clears the lockup's box, computed from the exit curve. Either the mark grows lmix(0.48, 1, prog(..., E.out)) over 68 f, or a letterspaced wordmark (0.08 em) fades up over 40 f on E.smooth with no scale.
techniques.timing: Drop: 44 f on E.smooth (~1000 px, peak ~64 px/f, motion-blur pass on). Float-out: 25 f on E.in (5 -> 22 px/f, scale +33%). Burst: 20 f on E.in, cut at ~75 px/f. The brand reveal starts within 0-1 f of the clear frame. Mark growth: 68 f on E.out (edge speed ~17 px/f, no overshoot). Then hold 90-120 f under a 10-15% push (le-living-hold).
techniques.use_when: Walkthroughs and feature films whose last shot is the product itself. The opening was a window or card entering, so the reverse bookends it. A crescendo of many screens that should give way to calm.
techniques.avoid_when: The film's last beat is type, not product. A lockup that is already visible would be crossed by the exiting product. A burst with no build-up earlier to justify the energy.

techniques.name: End card replays the opening
techniques.summary: The ending reuses the opening's stage and its mechanic, now carrying the brand, so the film closes on a rhyme the viewer has already learned.
techniques.recipe: Build the opening's stage (a Background component with an intensity prop) and its signature mechanic (a gap opening in a line, a word-roll, a mark slide, a window rise) as components with props, and call them again at the end with the same type size, position and curves. Run the mechanic mirrored, or with the brand as its payload. The window's exit is its entrance time-reversed: 1 - entrance(1 - t). The flanking words roll up and away (Words exit at half the stagger, E.in) and 'made with' plus the name roll in while the centre object holds. The opening's mark slide plays again, this time with the name. Bring the stage back only for brand beats: intensity 0 on product beats, then a 25 f rise from the bottom edge on E.out at the lockup. Never replay a reveal identically; the third use must add the name or the CTA.
techniques.timing: Word-roll: 28 f with a 5 f stagger. Mirrored exits keep the entrance's distance and duration. Stage rise: 25 f on E.out. Final hold: 96-120 f under the push.
techniques.use_when: Films with a distinctive opening mechanic or stage. The signature move's third use. Loops, where the end hands back to frame 0.
techniques.avoid_when: The opening was generic (replaying it only repeats a template). The reprise would be a frame-for-frame replay that adds nothing. Films under 10 s, where the rhyme has no time to land.

techniques.name: Lockup keeps building through the hold
techniques.summary: Once resolved, the lockup never freezes: the card slowly pushes in (or exhales back), the tracking tightens a touch and the stage dims, so the last 1.5-2 s read as intentional rather than stalled.
techniques.recipe: Wrap the whole end card in one camera transform and push it about the lockup's optical centre with k = lmix(1, 1.15, prog(f, resolve, end, E.dolly)), a 10-20% push. Under that, tighten the name's letter-spacing from +0.03-0.06 em to its token track over 46 f on E.out, starting at its resolve. For a calm close, use the exhale instead: k = lmix(1, 0.9, prog(f, resolve, resolve + 120, E.out)) while only the stage dims to 35% over 36 f on E.smooth. The lockup stays at full strength to the last frame, because the last frame is the poster and never fades to black.
techniques.timing: Hold 90-120 f (1.5-2.0 s, never more than ~150 f). Push 10-20% over the hold on E.dolly. Tracking: 46 f on E.out. Exhale: 10% over 120 f on E.out, with a 36 f stage dim. Tail of at least 60 f after the last event, inside the hold.
techniques.use_when: Every lockup and URL hold, and any card that must sit for more than 48 f.
techniques.avoid_when: A designed freeze of at most 15 f on a silence (then stop everything, the push included). Loops whose hold must end at the frame-0 scale (ease the push back down instead).

techniques.name: Stop-motion brand strobe
techniques.summary: A burst of hard-cut brand states (the poster, the lockup tiled in ever denser grids, one flood, the boxed wordmark, the glyph) flickers past in under a second as a punchy sign-off.
techniques.recipe: After the lockup's hold, cut through an array of full-frame states with no interpolation: const seq = [[poster,7],[grid3,5],[grid4,5],[gridA,2],[gridB,2],[flood,5],[ink,5],[boxedName,5],[glyph,7]], accumulated into Sequences or chosen with fd(frame). The grids are a CSS grid of the lockup with n = 3, 4, 5, 5 columns and a half-tile offset on alternate states, so the cuts read as a stepped pull-back. Keep every state on the same dark stage, with the accent flood as the only bright state, so there are no more than 3 large light-dark flips per second. End on the glyph alone for at most 30 f, and export the poster from the lockup frame, not the last frame. A quiet version keeps only the last two states (boxed name 5 f, glyph 7 f) as a loop point.
techniques.timing: Holds 7, 5, 5, 2, 2, 5, 5, 5, 7 f (43 f, ~0.72 s). Glyph ~2% of H, centred, for at most 30 f. A tick cluster under it that matches the opening's sound.
techniques.use_when: Social stings and launch films with a poster-driven or stop-motion identity. A re-energising coda after a quiet end card. Autoplay loops that need a clean reset point.
techniques.avoid_when: Calm or premium brands. Any film where you cannot keep large light-dark flips under 3 per second (photosensitivity). Any case where it would cut the lockup's hold below 1.5 s.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Replace the cream flood with the film's single accent flood (or C.ink2), keep every other state on the dark stage, and allow only one bright state, so the strobe changes shape and density rather than luminance.

techniques.name: Accent icon cools to its neutral mark
techniques.summary: The app icon pops up from tiny in the film's hot accent, cools through darker tones to its neutral final colours, lifts a little to make room, and the name fades in beneath it.
techniques.recipe: Pop the icon from tiny with scale mix(0.19, 1, prog(f, a, a+38, E.out)), its tile filled C.accent. Cool it as one object, never as two crossfaded copies: tile fill mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, p) and glyph mixColor(C.ink, C.white, p), with p = prog(f, a+6, a+34, E.smooth). OKLab mixing passes through darker shades of the same hue instead of muddy grey. Then lift it to make room: translateY 0 -> -102 px and scale 1 -> 0.945 over 36 f on E.smooth. As the lift passes 60%, fade the label up under it: opacity 0 -> 1 and translateY 8 -> 0 through arrive, over 15 f.
techniques.timing: Pop: 38 f on E.out (0.19 -> 0.72 by f6). Colour: 28 f (f6-34) on E.smooth. Lift: 36 f on E.smooth. Label: 15 f. Then hold 90-120 f under a push.
techniques.use_when: Films whose accent stood for heat, urgency or the problem early on and should cool into the product. App-icon lockups.
techniques.avoid_when: The accent already means something else in the film (one accent, one meaning). Icons whose final colour is the accent itself.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Start the tile in the film's single accent as a flat fill, not a multi-hue gradient, and cool it through darker shades of that same hue to the neutral ink with mixColor. Any accent hue carries the idea, so it never needs a warm orange-to-red ramp.

techniques.name: Mark turns through a key light
techniques.summary: The mark (an extruded glyph, a coin or a tile) turns a few degrees in 3D, and its face passes through a light, so a single specular sweep crosses it as it settles face-on.
techniques.recipe: Give the mark depth with CSS 3D: perspective 1200 px on the parent, the front face plus 6-10 copies stacked 1 px apart in z in a darker tonal step for the extrusion (or a mesh in Three.js). Rotate it rotateY tw(f, a, a+40, -35, 0, E.outSoft) with a small rotateX 20 -> 0 so it settles face-on. Sweep the light in 2D: a white band 30% of the mark's width, with opacity 0 -> 0.9 -> 0 across its width, masked to the mark (mask-image of the mark SVG) with mix-blend-mode screen, translated across the face over 14 f. Time it so the band's centre crosses as the rotation passes ~70%.
techniques.timing: Turn: 40 f on E.outSoft (~4 deg/f peak for 35 deg). Glint: 14 f on E.smooth, starting ~f20. One glint per film.
techniques.use_when: Premium, material or physical brands (finance, hardware, collectibles). 3D marks. A mark that needs one moment of life early in its hold.
techniques.avoid_when: Flat, playful or line marks (a sheen on a stroke looks like a template effect). Films with no other 3D. A second glint anywhere in the film (it reads as a preset).

techniques.name: Device keeps time inside the lockup
techniques.summary: During the hold, the story device that became part of the mark (a dot, a bar, a stripe) gives one or two small ticks on the beat, so the bookend plays inside the finished lockup instead of after it.
techniques.recipe: Keep the device as its own Mark piece (e.g. MARK.D). During the hold, pulse only that piece: scale 1 + 0.12 * hitPulse(f - beat, 2, 6) about its own centre, or a nudge of 3 * hitPulse(f - beat, 2, 6) px along the device's signature direction. If the accent means 'what just landed', flash the piece to C.accent on the pulse and return it to its resting colour over 12 f with mixColor. Place 1-2 ticks on downbeats in the first second of the hold, in time with the stinger's tail, and none in the last 30 f, so the final frame is calm and identical to the poster.
techniques.timing: 1-2 ticks at least 30 f apart. hitPulse attack 2 f, tau 6 f (gone in ~38 f). Amplitude 10-14% scale or 2-4 px. None in the final 30 f.
techniques.use_when: Films whose story device became a piece of the mark. Ends that should close the device's loop without ending on the device alone.
techniques.avoid_when: Marks without a separable piece. Very still closes, where any pulse breaks the calm. Loops that need the device to travel back to its frame-0 position instead.

techniques.name: Monochrome world, one accent
techniques.summary: Everything is black, white and grey, and one saturated accent marks the single element in each shot that carries the meaning.
techniques.recipe: Declare neutrals plus one accent in brand/tokens.ts: C.ink for the stage, C.ink2 for surfaces, C.mute for labels, C.line for strokes, C.white for type, C.accent, and a press step of mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, 0.08). Grade every photo, map, clay render or backdrop screenshot with filter: grayscale(1) so mixed media reads as one world. Paint the accent on exactly one thing per shot (the payoff word, the pin, the pressed button, the focus ring) and keep one meaning for it all film. Focus devices use three steps of it: the full accent for strokes, mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, 0.65) for fills and a mid step for decaying outlines. Colour arrives on a cut or an impact frame (fd(frame) >= cue), never through a slow fade, and when you audit rendered stills the accent should average 0.05-6% of frame pixels (peak about 12.5%) with the stage at 85-90%.
techniques.timing: The palette stays the same for the whole film. The accent swaps on the cue frame (a step, 0 f). Focus outlines land 6-10 px wide with their container (26 f, E.out), thin to 1 px over 12 f on E.in, then decay to 30% opacity over 24 f on E.linear.
techniques.use_when: Films that mix photos, 3D, maps and UI, multi-cell layouts, or any shot where several things compete and the eye needs exactly one target.
techniques.avoid_when: The product's own colourful UI is the subject of every shot and greying it would misrepresent it, or the story needs two semantic colours on screen at once.

techniques.name: One-hue light ramp
techniques.summary: Every lit thing (rims, rings, stage lifts, the end-card field) comes from adjacent lightness steps of one hue on a single near-black stage.
techniques.recipe: Build five tokens of one hue with mixColor, running from the stage to a pale tint: C.ink, then mixColor(C.ink, C.accent, 0.2 / 0.45 / 0.75), then mixColor(C.accent, C.white, 0.5). Only ever draw a gradient between two adjacent steps, so the whole film's light comes from one decision. Rims, rings and orb lobes use the upper steps as crisp strokes or flat fills, never as soft halos or bloom, and the stage holds 63-99% of pixels on dark frames. For an end-card field behind a wordmark, use linear-gradient(to top, step0, step2 45%, step4) plus a repeating-linear-gradient(90deg) of flat, hard-edged 60-120 px bands at ±6% lightness (no blur, so they never read as fluted glass); the band layer drifts 0.3 px/f so the hold never freezes. Against banding, bake the field as a dithered PNG with scripts/dither-gradient.py and let the film's global 1.5-2% grain sit over it.
techniques.timing: The palette stays the same. The end-card field holds 90-120 f with the bands drifting 0.3 px/f on E.linear.
techniques.use_when: Dark launch films with many light-built shapes (orbs, rings, rims) that need a recognisable look. It also makes a single bright card hit harder.
techniques.avoid_when: Light-mode walkthroughs where the UI's own colours dominate, or films already using the monochrome-plus-accent system (pick one system).

techniques.name: Accent ground for claims only
techniques.summary: Narrative shots sit on the neutral stage, other claims flip to the opposite neutral, and the single full-bleed accent ground is saved for the hero claim or the closing card, so colour works as punctuation.
techniques.recipe: Use two ground tokens (C.paper or C.ink, and C.accent) and one ink. Tag each shot 'story' or 'claim' in timeline.ts. The accent floods the frame once per film: give the full-bleed accent ground to the one hero claim (about 72 f) or to the closing card, and set every other claim on the opposite neutral stage (C.ink after C.paper, or the reverse) with the accent only on its one key word, so accent pixels stay near 8% across the film. Switch grounds on hard cuts; elsewhere the accent appears only as a one-word highlight or a soft single-hue wash that previews the flood. Let the accent ground arrive as a radial flood. Layer order: the accent ground; a disc of radius 640 px whose fill steps mixColor(C.accent, C.paper, 0.75), then 0.4, then 0; a 60 px ring of mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, 0.1) at r 600 px, which appears with the last step and stays for the shot to frame the hero word; then the type.
techniques.timing: Grounds swap on cut frames. The radial flood takes 6 f, with tint steps on f0, f2 and f4 decided with fd(). The ring stays from f4 to the end of the shot. Claim shots run 60-120 f each.
techniques.use_when: Films with a few big statements that must feel louder than the walkthrough around them, and endings that need to feel conclusive.
techniques.avoid_when: The accent fails contrast as a ground for display type, or the film has no distinct claims (a pure UI tour).

techniques.name: Single inversion card
techniques.summary: In an otherwise dark film, one card cuts to a near-white field with dark type for one second, marking the key promise.
techniques.recipe: At about 40% of runtime, inside a gap in the music, hard-cut to an AbsoluteFill of cream C.paper whose edges carry a soft ring of colour, fading from white at 55% of the radius through two accent hues to the frame edge. Set the line in C.ink and rise it out of a line mask: overflow hidden, translateY from 100% to 0 through arrive(), on E.out. Let the ring breathe, with its scale moving between 1.00 and 1.02 on sin(2π·frame/120). Frame mean luma jumps from about 9 to about 232, so this must be the film's only light frame; cut out hard on the next beat.
techniques.timing: Hold for 60 f. The type rises over 18 f on E.out, starting on f4. The ring breathes with a period of 120 f, ±2%. Place it at about 40% of runtime.
techniques.use_when: A dark film's single most important promise needs to stop the viewer halfway through.
techniques.avoid_when: Light-mode films, films that already alternate dark and light, or when the music has no gap to place it in.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Keep a neutral C.paper field, never a cream one. Draw the ring as a single hard-edged accent stroke (a 6-10 px ellipse at 88% of the frame) that breathes in scale, with no soft colour falloff and no second hue.

techniques.name: Theme flip mid-move
techniques.summary: In the middle of a camera fly-over, the dark page and stage flash to their light versions, top first, and the motion never pauses.
techniques.recipe: Render dark and light versions of the same page as two identical layers on the same moving plane, inside one world container driven by src/lib/camera.ts so they share every transform. Reveal the light layer through mask-image: linear-gradient(to bottom, black X%, transparent X+30%), with X running from -30% to 100%, so the top bands lead by about 2 f. On the same span, swap the stage from the C.ink grid to the C.paper studio. Keep the camera at cruise speed through the flip: it shows theme support and doubles as the film's dark-to-light act change.
techniques.timing: 6 f in total, with the mask edge on E.linear (frame luma goes about 40, 140, 205, 235). The top leads by 2 f. Leave the camera's own easing untouched.
techniques.use_when: Products with dark and light modes, or as the single dark-to-light act transition of a film.
techniques.avoid_when: The camera is static (the flip turns into a plain crossfade), or the light version would not match the dark one pixel for pixel.

techniques.name: Palette shift as context cue
techniques.summary: The world's colour changes behind a steady foreground, for a whole act or for one beat, to say 'new context' or 'this is the moment' without words.
techniques.recipe: Keep two or three token sets keyed by act in brand/tokens.ts: for example, a loud act on C.paper with C.ink and C.accent, a technical process act in pure neutral greys, and a calm product act in pale tints of one hue with the accent withdrawn. Read colours through a palette(act) helper so a whole act switches at once, on a hard cut or hidden inside a zoom-through. For a single beat, park the hero (card, composer, device) and shift only the backdrop. Drive one blurred backdrop layer's filter brightness() and saturate() so its luma rises about 100 levels over 42 f on E.smooth, or step it on the cut into the hero beat and step back on the next wide. The hero never moves during the shift, so the eye stays parked.
techniques.timing: Act switches happen in 0 f on a cut. A neutral process act can be as short as 74 f. A backdrop shift takes 42 f on E.smooth. A hero-beat backdrop holds for up to about 300 f before stepping back.
techniques.use_when: Act changes without title cards, entering another app's world, or flagging the key moment (the user's prompt, the reveal).
techniques.avoid_when: The foreground is moving at the same time (the cue gets lost), or the film is shorter than two acts.

techniques.name: Ink resolve on arrival
techniques.summary: Text never simply fades in: it arrives pale (or dim on a dark stage) and darkens or brightens to full ink as it settles.
techniques.recipe: For each word or line, mix its colour from a pale tone to the ink with mixColor from src/lib/color.ts (interpolateColors stair-steps), while opacity goes from 0.3-0.4 to 1. On paper, go from mixColor(C.ink, C.paper, 0.65), or a pale accent tint mixColor(C.accent, C.paper, 0.8), to C.ink; on a dark stage, go from C.mute to C.white. Pair it with a short rise inside an overflow-hidden line mask (translateY 100% to 0 through arrive(), or at most 60 px), with words staggered and no blur on slow rises; src/fx/Words.tsx can carry the motion while you apply the colour per word. Connector words ('on', 'and', 'the') reach half strength in 2 f and finish over the next 6-12 f, so the nouns read first.
techniques.timing: Colour takes 12-16 f per word on E.out (a headline-scale darkening may run 40 f). The rise takes 20 f, peaking under 20 px/f. Stagger words 8 f apart (4-10). Connector words go 0 to 0.5 in 2 f, then to 1 over 6-12 f.
techniques.use_when: Every headline and caption reveal, especially over textured or busy backgrounds where an opacity fade alone looks washed out.
techniques.avoid_when: Numbers that must read instantly on a cut (land them at full ink), or type that already sits inside a colour-band fill.

techniques.name: Accent on the newest arrival
techniques.summary: Whatever just arrived (a typed character, a snapped word, a generated pill) wears the accent for a moment and then settles to neutral, so a short coloured wake leads the eye.
techniques.recipe: Store each item's birth frame. Type-on: give each glyph span colour = mixColor(C.accent, C.white or C.ink, clamp((frame - birth) / 12)); at 1-1.7 chars/f this leaves a wake of 10-20 characters behind the caret. Word builds work as either a wave or a step. Wave: each word is grey for 4 f, accent at about 8 f and ink by 16-20 f, on E.out. Step: the word that snapped last holds the accent (fd(frame) >= snap[i] && fd(frame) < snap[i+1]), and the final word keeps it until 1 frame before the cut. Objects (generated pills, pins, cards, an end-card icon): stack an accent-tinted duplicate clipped to the shape (mix-blend-mode: color) and fade it from 1 to 0 on E.out. Use one accent hue only: no multi-stop hue cycle, no bloom, no text-shadow.
techniques.timing: Glyph decay takes 12-16 f on E.linear. A word wave takes 16-20 f per word with an 8-12 f stagger. A step holds 16-20 f per word. An object's tint resolves over 20-40 f on E.out.
techniques.use_when: Prompts typing, statements building word by word, AI-generated items appearing, or any build where the newest piece should lead.
techniques.avoid_when: The accent already means something else in the shot (a focus ring or a pressed button), or long paragraphs where the wake becomes noise.

techniques.name: Accent hit envelope
techniques.summary: On a press or an impact, the element floods with the accent and peaks for one frame with its label inverted, then either bleeds back like decaying light or stays as the new state.
techniques.recipe: Put a solid C.accent overlay inside the button, with the same corner radius. Drive its opacity with hitPulse(frame - cue, 10, 8): a fast rise, a one-frame peak, and an exponential release about twice as long as the attack. Switch the label to C.ink when the overlay passes 0.6, and change no scale (the cursor may dip 1 to 0.9 to 1 over 12 f). For an impact that changes state, swap the object's fill to the accent on the contact frame (decided with fd), add a flat C.white overlay at 0.8·hitPulse(t, 1, 2), apply squash(t) anchored at the contact edge, and leave the accent on. No ring blur and no outer halo.
techniques.timing: Attack 10-12 f, a 1 f peak, then a release of 20-26 f (tau 8): an asymmetric 1:2 envelope. On an impact, the swap takes 1 f, the white flash about 4 f and the squash 8 f.
techniques.use_when: Primary-button clicks, send or confirm moments, and contact hits that turn an object into its new state.
techniques.avoid_when: Secondary controls and hovers (save it for the decisive action), or when the accent already floods the ground.

techniques.name: Specular sweep
techniques.summary: A soft bright band glides once across a settled number, word or logo face, so the element looks locked and made of a real material without moving.
techniques.recipe: Duplicate the settled text or mark and fill the duplicate with linear-gradient(100deg, transparent 0, C.white at 35% alpha 50%, transparent 100%). Make the band about 40% of the text height wide (about 30% of the width for a logo glyph, with peak opacity up to 0.9), clip it to the glyphs with background-clip: text or an SVG mask, and use mix-blend-mode: screen on dark stages. Drive the band's x from -20% to 120% of the element width on E.smooth, so its speed peaks mid-sweep, starting 6-10 f after the element lands. For a looping working state, use a light-grey label with a 120 px lighter band whose background-position is (frame % 60) / 60 on E.linear, and stop it on the frame the state resolves. Keep the sheen inside the glyphs, with no blur or halo outside them.
techniques.timing: A one-shot sweep takes 36 f on E.smooth (about 16 px/f mid-sweep, peaking near 26 px/f). A logo glint brightens over 9 f, holds about 11 f and is clear by 36 f. The loop has a 60 f period on E.linear and is held for up to about 74 f before the result.
techniques.use_when: A final number, price or logo that has landed and must hold attention through a still beat, or loading and generating labels.
techniques.avoid_when: The element is still moving, or you would need more than one sweep in the shot (it turns into decoration).

techniques.name: Rim streak on card edges
techniques.summary: A bright streak travels along a dark card's border while its edges carry a faint lit rim, separating it from a black stage without a drop shadow.
techniques.recipe: Fill the card with C.ink2 on a C.ink stage and give it a 1 px border of C.white at 8% alpha. Above it, place an SVG rect of the same size and radius with pathLength=1, a 1-2 px stroke of C.accent or C.white, strokeDasharray '0.12 0.88' and strokeDashoffset driven by the frame, so a 120 px segment runs along the top edge or around the whole perimeter. For the whole UI act, breathe the static rim's opacity between 0.6 and 0.8 on sin(2π·frame/180). For a brand that supplies glow, add soft box-shadow halos in a different colour on each of three sides.
techniques.timing: The streak crosses one edge in 20-30 f on E.linear. The rim breathes ±20% over 180 f and stays on for the whole UI act.
techniques.use_when: Flat dark UI cards floating on pure black that need depth and separation without tilting or shadows.
techniques.avoid_when: Light-mode UI (use a soft neutral shadow instead), or several cards on screen at once (the streaks compete).
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Drop the coloured halos entirely. Use one 1 px single-colour border highlight sweeping along the edge, plus a neutral low-opacity drop shadow (0 24px 48px of C.ink at 50%) for lift.

techniques.name: Travelling tone band fill
techniques.summary: A word, URL or logo mark fills through a band of colour (dark, then accent, then light) that sweeps across it and settles on the final ink.
techniques.recipe: Text: set background to linear-gradient(90deg, final ink 0 35%, light accent tint 50%, C.accent 65%, stage colour 80%) at background-size 300%, with background-clip: text and color: transparent, and animate background-position from 100% to 0%. For a domain plus path, delay the path span. For accent words in a tagline, step each letter from ink to C.accent with a 2 f stagger after the line lands. Mark: use the mark as an SVG mask over a tall gradient rect, reveal the fill bottom-up with clip-path from inset(100% 0 0 0) to inset(0), then translateY the rect by one gradient period so the tone scrolls and settles on solid accent, just before the colour floods the frame. The type itself stays still; only the fill travels.
techniques.timing: A word sweep takes 32 f on E.smooth (the front peaks at about 25 px/f). A URL takes 42 f, easing into the final ink on E.out, with the path lagging 8-12 f. A mark wipe takes 8 f on E.linear, then the tone scrolls for 36 f on E.smooth. Letters stagger 2 f.
techniques.use_when: Hero words, the URL card, or a logo mark that should introduce the accent before it fills the frame.
techniques.avoid_when: Small UI text, or type that is still moving (the band and the motion fight).

techniques.name: Living gradient stage
techniques.summary: Behind static cards the background never freezes: soft pools of colour at the corners breathe in brightness or drift slowly, like light through water.
techniques.recipe: Start from a C.ink base with two or three huge pools (radius 55-60% of the frame, for example one centred at 85% 15% and one at 10% 95%) in dark tints of one allowed hue (never violet, warm brown or a multi-hue mesh), each baked once as an RGBA PNG with scripts/dither-gradient.py rather than drawn as a CSS radial-gradient under a live blur(), which bands at 8 bits and costs render time. Breathe mode: each pool's opacity moves between 0.85 and 1.0 on sin(2π·frame/162), the second half a period out of phase, with no translation (about ±15% luma). Drift mode: 4-5 pools, each centre moving ±6% of the frame on sine loops of 360-660 f at different phases, with opacity ±8%. The pools light the stage, never an element: none sits centred behind type or a card. Let the film's global 1.5-2% grain sit over it, and give the stage an intensity prop (0-1) so brand beats (open, tagline, end card) raise it while UI beats sit on flat C.ink.
techniques.timing: The breathe period is 162 f. Drift loops run 360-660 f, at under 1 px/f. On brand beats the stage rises over 50 f on E.out (translateY +40% to 0) and drains to flat in 8 f.
techniques.use_when: Holds, end cards and statement cards that would otherwise sit still for more than 48 f.
techniques.avoid_when: Busy UI shots where any background motion competes, or films built on a hard flat-stage look. Behind a product window or readable type, where soft pools read as a generic gradient backdrop or as haze; light stages, where they read as smudges. A flat stage with one tonal step is the stronger default.

techniques.name: Light swell bridge into the hero
techniques.summary: Light swells around a small panel until the frame is bright, the film cuts on the brightest frame to the hero card sitting in the same light, and that light slowly exhales back to dark.
techniques.recipe: Shot A: a radial gradient centred on the panel with four stops (stage, dark tint, mid, light tint), whose radii grow at 12-25 px/f on E.linear so mean frame luma climbs about 2.25 levels per frame (from 15 to about 78); cut on a downbeat at the peak. Shot B opens on the identical gradient with the hero title already in place, then pulls the stops back inward so luma falls from about 112 to 43, handing off to the next dark shot. Put the cut on an act boundary so it stays crisp.
techniques.timing: The swell takes 28 f on E.linear. Cut at the peak, on a downbeat. The exhale takes 86 f on E.smooth (a fade-out never runs on an expo-out).
techniques.use_when: Releasing a dark section into the hero card or title: the biggest reveal in a dark film.
techniques.avoid_when: Light-mode films, or a second time in the same film.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Replace the soft multi-hue bloom with four hard-edged concentric discs in tonal steps of one hue (the stage, then 15%, 35% and 60% lightness toward the accent), their radii expanding with a 2 f stagger on normal blend. Keep the same swell, cut and exhale timing.

techniques.name: Rising colour wash carrier
techniques.summary: A soft single-hue field rises from the bottom edge behind the type, swells and sweeps up across the frame on the change, then recedes off the top, so the foreground swap reads as one move.
techniques.recipe: Place a full-frame layer under the type with background radial-gradient(ellipse 70% 60% at 50% Y, C.accent 0%, transparent 70%). The gradient is soft on its own, so use no blur filter, keep normal blend and keep the saturation low. Animate Y from 110% to 75% on E.out (coverage 0 to 47%). Then swell the ellipse from 70% to 110% and wipe it up (centroid from about 487 to 154 px at 1080p) on E.inOut, changing the foreground underneath on the fastest frame, and finally let it recede to Y -20% on E.outSoft. Short version into a hard cut: a bottom-anchored band of 40% height, linear-gradient(to top, mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, 0.5), transparent), translateY from 100% to 20% on E.in, with the cut landing mid-rise. Use it to preview the accent ground that is coming.
techniques.timing: The rise takes 39 f on E.out. The swell and wipe take 12 f on E.inOut (about 28 px/f). The recede takes 90 f on E.outSoft. The pre-cut band takes 16 f on E.in (about +14 luma levels).
techniques.use_when: Changing cards behind continuous colour, leading into an accent-ground claim or the end card, or smoothing a hard cut into a new scene.
techniques.avoid_when: Shots already on an accent ground, or dense UI that the wash would tint. A soft accent haze behind type reads as glow.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Keep the move and lose the soft falloff: a flat accent band with a crisp, straight top edge (a clip-path inset driven by the same Y curve) rises behind the type, sweeps up across the frame on the change and leaves off the top, at full opacity in a light tint of the accent. The swap still happens on its fastest frame; no radial gradient, no feathered edge.

techniques.name: Drain the stage, keep the hero
techniques.summary: Everything around the hero fades and the world drops to dark or bleaches to white, while the hero stays crisp in place, isolating it or closing a section.
techniques.recipe: Duplicate the hero onto a top layer at identical coordinates so nothing under it can shift. Isolate: fade the rest of the layer to 0 on E.linear to reveal a mid-grey plate, then mix the plate from C.mist toward C.ink2 on E.in (world luma from about 238 to 87) while the hero gains a 20 px radius and a soft shadow; in a light film, drain the surroundings to C.white instead and assemble the next page around the parked hero. Focus variant: render the side columns through RackFocus (t 0 to 1, blur 8; never an animated blur filter on the columns) and drop them to 0.6 opacity while the centre stays untouched and the parent scales from 1 to 1.06. Exhale: after a peak, or once the lockup has held 90-120 f, dim the stage first (stage opacity 1 to 0, or brightness 1 to 0.6 during a push-in) and fade the hero 8 f later, ending on a hard cut mid-film or on a short C.ink tail only at the very end.
techniques.timing: Neighbours fade over 12 f on E.linear, the world dims over 10 f on E.in, then hold about 30 f. A white drain takes 6-16 f on E.linear. Column focus takes 18 f on E.smooth. In the exhale, the stage fades over 36 f and the hero over 30 f starting 8 f later, with a tail of up to 22 f; a push-in dim takes 8 f on E.in.
techniques.use_when: Search results, a found item, a selected post or row, the moment before a detail view, and the ends of sections or of the film.
techniques.avoid_when: The hero itself must move during the isolation, or the neighbours carry context the viewer still needs.

techniques.name: Tilt-linked sheen
techniques.summary: As a card or device tilts in 3D, a faint highlight band slides across its face in step with the angle, so the surface reads as a real material catching a key light.
techniques.recipe: Inside the tilted element, add an overlay above the content and below its 1 px border: linear-gradient(105deg, transparent 40%, C.white at 18% alpha 50%, transparent 60%) at background-size 300%, with screen blend on dark UI or soft-light on light UI. Compute background-position-x from the same rotation value that drives the transform (50% plus 2.5% per degree of rotateY, with rotateX nudging it vertically), so the highlight moves only while the object turns and parks when it settles. Multiply its opacity by clamp((|rotateY| - 2) / 6) so a flat card stays clean. Assume one key light 45° camera-left for the whole film, so every card catches it from the same side.
techniques.timing: It follows the tilt move: for example, rotateY going from 12° to 0 over 40 f on E.out moves the band about 30% and parks it. Peak overlay opacity is 0.18 on dark UI and 0.10 on light UI.
techniques.use_when: Perspective UI tilt-ups, cards flipping or settling out of 3D, device turns, and logo tiles yawing.
techniques.avoid_when: Flat 2D layouts with no rotation (use the one-shot specular sweep instead).

techniques.name: Duotone until featured
techniques.summary: Screenshots and photos sit in a two-tone grade until their beat. Then full colour opens out from the point of interaction, and the previous item returns to duotone.
techniques.recipe: Give every non-featured media layer an SVG filter: feColorMatrix type saturate 0, then feComponentTransfer tables mapping shadows to C.ink and highlights to C.mist (or to a pale accent tint, mixColor(C.accent, C.paper, 0.85), for a branded duotone). On the featured item's beat, place the full-colour copy of the same image above it and reveal it through clip-path circle(r at x y), growing from the click or impact point to 150% on E.out, or swap it on the cut frame. When focus moves on, return the previous item to duotone by animating the matrix's saturate value from 1 to 0. Only one item is ever in full colour.
techniques.timing: The colour iris takes 18 f on E.out from the interaction point. The return to duotone takes 20 f on E.smooth. A swap on a cut takes 0 f.
techniques.use_when: Grids of integrations, galleries, template pickers, and multi-cell layouts where one item at a time is the subject.
techniques.avoid_when: Only one hero screenshot is on screen (nothing to contrast with), or the UI's colours are its selling point in every frame.

techniques.name: Key-light edge hairline
techniques.summary: Every card, device bezel and bevelled shape on a dark stage carries a hairline edge that is bright on the side facing one fixed key light and fades to nothing on the far side, so surfaces separate from black without shadows or halos.
techniques.recipe: Declare one light direction for the whole film in brand/tokens.ts (LIGHT = 135, meaning light from the top-left, the same key light cl-tilt-linked-sheen assumes). Give each surface an edge layer above its content: position absolute, inset 0, border-radius inherit, padding 1.5 px, background linear-gradient(calc(LIGHT - rotateZ) deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.40) 0%, rgba(255,255,255,0.10) 35%, transparent 65%), masked to a ring with mask: linear-gradient(#000 0 0) content-box, linear-gradient(#000 0 0) and mask-composite: exclude (-webkit-mask-composite: xor). Recompute the angle every frame as LIGHT minus the object's own rotateZ, so the lit edge stays on the light's side while the object turns. Add box-shadow inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.06) as a top inner highlight. In 3D, multiply the lit-edge alpha by clamp(1 + 0.04 x degrees tilted toward the light, 0.6, 1.4), so an edge brightens as it turns into the light. For bevelled decorative shapes drawn in SVG (stars, tiles, extruded marks), stroke each facet edge at 1 px with a linearGradient in gradientUnits='userSpaceOnUse' running along the light vector (white at 40% fading to 0), and keep facet fills within 2-4% luma of the stage. Use no blur and no outer halo. On light stages, replace the hairline with a 1.5 px C.white top edge and a C.line bottom edge.
techniques.timing: Static styling with no clock of its own: it rides every entrance and move of its surface. Lit-edge alpha is 0.40 at the light corner, 0.10 at 35% of the gradient line and 0 by 65%. The inner top highlight is 0.06. The angle is recomputed every frame as LIGHT - rotateZ. Tilt gain is 0.04 per degree, clamped to 0.6-1.4x. On a tilt resolve (for example rotateX 25 deg to 0 over 68 f on E.out), the edge brightness settles on the same curve.
techniques.use_when: Dark UI films with flat cards, panels, device bezels or bevelled brand shapes on near-black, where a drop shadow disappears and a glow is off-limits.
techniques.avoid_when: Light-mode shots, where a white hairline vanishes on paper. Also avoid it on cards that already carry cl-rim-light-sweep's travelling streak, and on layouts so dense that every lit edge turns the frame into wireframe noise.

techniques.name: Brightness rides the move
techniques.summary: A mark or icon takes its brightness from the same progress that drives its scale or depth, so an oversized pass stays a dark shape and the object reaches full brightness exactly as it lands.
techniques.recipe: Never give the fill a clock of its own: derive it from the transform. Log-scale slam: s = lmix(s0, 1, prog(f, a, a + 66, E.glide)) with s0 = 6-8. Then p = 1 - Math.log(s) / Math.log(s0), and fill = mixColor(mixColor(C.ink, C.white, 0.14), C.white, p * p * p) on a dark stage (on paper, mix from mixColor(C.paper, C.ink, 0.12) to C.ink). While the mark is three or more times its final size and covering much of the frame, it stays a dark grey under about luma 60, so the frame's mean luma never flashes. Lift toward camera: an icon tile peeling out of its row inverts as it travels, with the tile going mixColor(C.ink2, C.white, q) and the glyph mixColor(C.white, C.ink, q), where q = clamp(travel progress / 0.75), so the inversion finishes before the last quarter of the move. Depth field: in a multi-depth parallax field, mix each layer's fill from C.ink toward its own colour by a weight read from its current z (0.45 far, 0.75 mid, 1.0 near), and keep reading it during a push so objects brighten as they approach. Turn on true motion blur while |delta log s| > 0.1 per frame, and check with scripts/measure-speed.py that edges stay under 80 px/f.
techniques.timing: Slam: 66 f on E.glide from s0 = 6-8. The fill follows p^3, so it passes mid-grey only in the second half of the move and reaches full brightness on the landing frame. Lift-out: 24 f of travel on E.inOut, with the inversion complete at 75% (about 18 f); a mid-grey tile goes from about luma 160 to 248. Depth weights are 0.45 / 0.75 / 1.0 by z, re-read every frame of the push. Motion blur stays on while |delta log s| > 0.1 per frame, and edges stay under 80 px/f.
techniques.use_when: A logo mark or icon slams in oversized and shrinks to size, an icon lifts out of the UI toward camera, or a field of objects at several depths is pushed through on a dark stage.
techniques.avoid_when: Text (use cl-ink-resolve, which runs on time), and moves under about 150 px or 1.5x, where the change would not show. On a light stage a giant near-black pass would itself be the flash, so mix toward the paper there.

techniques.name: Now, was, next tone ladder
techniques.summary: Items in a sequence sit on three neutral tones: the one being read is at full ink, the ones already read step down to a mid grey and stay as context, and the ones still to come wait in a dim grey.
techniques.recipe: Declare three tones in brand/tokens.ts. NOW is C.white on an ink stage (C.ink on paper). WAS is C.mute. NEXT is mixColor(C.ink, C.white, 0.24) on ink (mixColor(C.paper, C.ink, 0.2) on paper). Give every item in the sequence (caption words, list rows, step labels, roller slots, status words) a cue frame, and compute its state with fd(): NEXT before its cue, NOW from its cue, and WAS from the next item's cue. Promote NEXT to NOW over 6 f on E.ui. Start the previous item's NOW-to-WAS demotion on the same frame, over 10 f on E.smooth, so the eye is handed over and only one item is at full ink after each handoff. Rollers and ratchets step their tones on the slot frame with no tween. Show pending items at NEXT only when 'there is more' is the message (lists, slot ratchets, step lists, with at most three visible); otherwise they do not exist yet. Exits go through WAS: an item drops to WAS before it leaves, never straight from NOW. Keep weight and size the same so tone alone carries the order. The accent stays out of the ladder because it marks meaning (cl-mono-one-accent).
techniques.timing: Promotion takes 6 f on E.ui. Demotion takes 10 f on E.smooth, starting with the next item's arrival. Each item holds NOW for at least 24 f. Rollers and ratchets step on the slot frame (0 f). An exit starts at least 8 f after the item reaches WAS. On ink, the tones sit at about 100% (NOW), 40% (WAS) and 24% (NEXT) of the way from the stage to white.
techniques.use_when: Captions that build in steps, lists and checklists that grow, slot rollers, status sequences, and flanking words that make way for a new focal word.
techniques.avoid_when: A single statement that lands all at once, or real product UI whose own text colours must stay true. In lens lists, tone should follow distance from the focus line, not reading order.

techniques.name: Graphic softens into the stage
techniques.summary: A crisp graphic that has just finished its move, such as a wall of bars or a stripe field, loses its edges, widens and keeps drifting until it has become the soft backdrop for the next title, with no cut.
techniques.recipe: Keep the graphic's own elements mounted after their build and render them through src/fx/RackFocus (render = the bar group, blur 48, mid on). Drive t from 0 to 1 over 72 f on E.smooth. RackFocus crossfades a sharp copy and a copy at constant blur, so the softening does not step the way an animated filter: blur() does. On the same progress, widen each element (scaleX 1 to 1.5 about its centre) so the gaps close, and mix the whole field 25% toward the stage colour so its contrast drops under the type to come. Fill every element with a vertical gradient between two adjacent steps of the film's one-hue ramp (cl-one-hue-light-ramp). Slide each element's background-position-y at its own speed, 0.3 + 0.5 x rand(i) percent per frame, so the bands shift tone at different rates and the field never freezes once it is soft. Bring the next foreground in from frame 36 of the soften, when the stripes no longer read as objects. If banding shows, add 1-2% feTurbulence noise over the field, or bake a matching still with scripts/dither-gradient.py. In full colour, the field shifts through several hues as it softens.
techniques.timing: The soften takes 72 f on E.smooth (RackFocus t from 0 to 1, blur 48 px at 1080p). The widen from 1 to 1.5 and the 25% contrast drop run on the same curve. Each element's gradient drifts at 0.3-0.8% per frame on E.linear and keeps drifting for 60-120 f under the next element. The next foreground enters from frame 36.
techniques.use_when: After a graphic build (a bar wall, a stripe or tile field, a filled pattern), when the next beat is a title or the end-card mark and needs a backdrop born from what was just on screen.
techniques.avoid_when: The graphic carries data the viewer still needs to read, or it is a UI act where the stage should stay flat. When no graphic build comes before the title, use cl-living-stage directly.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Fill the bars with tonal steps of one non-banned hue (from the stage to a light tint), not a periwinkle-pink-orange spectrum, so the softened field becomes a single-hue living stage. Keep the RackFocus soften, the widen and the per-bar drift.

techniques.name: Rolling band flood
techniques.summary: A light frame fills with the brand colour as soft horizontal bands of it roll upward and grow opaque. The text tints and dissolves into it, and the film arrives on its end-card field without a cut.
techniques.recipe: Over the last product frame, add a full-frame overlay holding a strip three frames tall: a linear-gradient(to bottom) that repeats six soft tonal bands of one hue (mixColor(C.accent, C.paper, 0.7), then 0.45, then 0.2, then C.accent, then back up). Make each band about half the frame height, with its stops blending over about 10% of the band. Drive the strip's translateY from 0 to -1 frame height on E.linear, so the bands roll up at constant speed. Drive its opacity with p * p, where p = prog(f, a, a + 60, E.linear), so the colour arrives late and decisively (quarter strength at the halfway point). Mix the foreground text to mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, 0.4) over the first 12 f, then fade it from 1 to 0 over f12-f40 on E.smooth, so the colour absorbs it rather than covering it. End on the end-card field, with the same bands slowing to a 0.3 px/f drift, and let the lockup appear on it afterwards. Bake the strip once with scripts/dither-gradient.py (space oklab) so the soft bands do not contour. In full colour, the flood runs through several hues.
techniques.timing: 60 f in total. The bands roll one frame height on E.linear (about 18 px/f at 1080p), and the opacity follows p^2 over the same 60 f. The text tints over 12 f and fades over f12-f40 on E.smooth. Frame mean luma goes from about 250 to 215: a light-to-mid flood, not a polarity flip. The bands then ease to a 0.3 px/f drift for the end card's 90-120 f.
techniques.use_when: Closing a light product act into the end card, or returning to the brand world after the last UI beat (a success state, a published page) without a hard cut.
techniques.avoid_when: Dark films, where the flood reads as fog over black. Also avoid it a second time in the same film, and before an end card whose ground is not the flood's hue.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Build the bands only from tonal steps of one non-banned hue (light tint, mid tint, the accent), not a lavender-pink-peach-orange spectrum. Keep the roll, the p^2 opacity ramp and the text absorption.

techniques.name: Shadows tinted by the stage
techniques.summary: On a tinted light stage, lifted cards and solid pills cast soft shadows in a dark step of the stage's own hue instead of grey, so depth reads as part of the world's colour rather than dirt on it.
techniques.recipe: Derive one shadow colour from the stage, never from the accent: SH = mixColor(stageHue, C.ink, 0.6), where stageHue is the act's tint (for example, the pale-tint act of cl-context-palette-shift). Give each lifted card two shadows: a contact shadow, 0 2px 6px of C.ink at 0.10, and an ambient shadow, 0 24px 56px -16px of SH at 0.22 (convert mixColor's rgb() output to rgba). Under a solid black pill or icon tile, use a single tinted ellipse instead. Make it 80% of the element's width and 30% of its height, offset downward by 40% of its height, filled with radial-gradient(SH at 0.35, transparent 70%) and blur(32px), on multiply, below the element. Tie the shadow to lift: with lift = scale - 1 (or translateZ / 200), multiply offset and blur by 1 + 3 x lift and alpha by 1 / (1 + 3 x lift), so a rising card's shadow spreads and fades. Because SH reads from the act's tokens, a palette switch retints every shadow on the same frame. In its richer form, the look puts blurred blobs of two pastel hues beside a black pill and coloured halos on three sides of cards floating on black.
techniques.timing: Static while parked. On a lift (scale 1 to 1.04 over 20-26 f on E.out), the ambient blur goes from about 56 to 63 px and the alpha from 0.22 to 0.20 on the same curve. On seating, it returns on the seat move's own easing. A palette switch retints the shadows in 0 f, on the cut.
techniques.use_when: Light-mode acts on pale tinted stages, pastel product worlds, and black pills or tiles floating on a tinted field where a grey shadow looks muddy.
techniques.avoid_when: Dark stages, where a coloured shadow becomes a glow. Keep shadows neutral in neutral C.paper films, and skip the tint wherever it would echo the accent and spend its meaning.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Use only one dark step of the stage's own hue, on light stages only, with shadows that fall downward and never spread past about half the element's size. On dark stages, drop the tint entirely and separate cards with cl-key-light-edge-hairline instead of a coloured halo.

techniques.name: Type solidity arc
techniques.summary: The type gains body across the film. Early statements are translucent white that lets the coloured stage show through, and the closing line and lockup are solid, so the payoff reads as more certain than the promise.
techniques.recipe: Add a typeAlpha value to each act in timeline.ts, for example [0.65, 0.85, 1.0] for opening, middle and end, and read it through one helper so every caption in an act shares it. Apply it as the opacity of the C.white line container, not as per-glyph rgba, which darkens where glyphs overlap, so the stage colour shows through the letters. Keep weight, size and tracking identical across acts so that only confidence changes. Step the value only on cuts or act changes, never inside a line or a shot. cl-ink-resolve still handles each arrival; the arc only sets where that resolve ends. Keep translucent acts to display type (at least 64 px at 1080p) over stage areas darker than about luma 110, and check contrast on rendered stills (Stills.tsx). The end-card line and lockup are always solid C.white.
