Give each appearance cut one centred tick (pan 0, weight 0.35, 1-3 f after the cut), and let a run of removals multiply the weight by 1.26 per tick so the run gets louder as the edit speeds up. The only sustained sound is one low pad under the reveal act: a section with style breakdown, layers {drums: 0, arp: 0, bells: 0, bass: 0} and level about 0.5 spanning that act, a swell event that peaks on the first reveal, and a one-bar tail section after it so the pad rings out instead of stopping. On each resolution frame (a number lands, a polarity cut), schedule nothing after the last tick so the sound stops within a frame, and put one bell there at weight 0.15 with pitch 'D8' as a faint high shimmer. Close by repeating the opening cluster at the same spacing under the stinger, then let the lockup's single land ring into silence over a slow push. The picture never sits still longer than 48 f, any designed freeze also gets a silences entry, and master.lufs is -16.
techniques.timing: At least 50% of the runtime silent, in gaps of 30-96 f between sound clusters. Opening cluster: 5 ticks over 14 f from frame 0. Reveal pad: on from the act's first frame, swell peak on the first reveal, about 42 f of plateau, about 84 f of ring-out. Sound stops within 1 f of each resolution; the shimmer bell (weight 0.15) fades over about 54 f. Removal ticks rise about 2 dB each. Lockup hold 90-120 f in silence after its single land, under a push of at least 10% across the hold.
techniques.use_when: Short stings and feature spots under about 15 s, calm or premium tones, number and unlock reveals, and films with fewer than about one decisive event per second.
techniques.avoid_when: Launch films and walkthroughs over about 20 s, dense sequences with more than about 3 visible events per second (use a steady bed instead), briefs that supply a music track, or feeds where the brief asks for high energy.

techniques.name: Long-tailed beat lengths
techniques.summary: Beat lengths follow a long tail instead of an even grid: most beats sit near one median length, a few connective beats snap past at a third of it, and one or two hero beats run about three times as long, so the film never settles into a slideshow rhythm.
techniques.recipe: Before animating anything, write the cut list in src/timeline.ts as a BEATS array of cut-to-cut lengths in 8ths, and derive the ACT and CUE start frames from its running sum with b() so every boundary sits on the grid. Pick a median M of 60-72 f (2-2.4 beats at 120 BPM, inside the house shot median of 60-90 f) and fill the list from four bins. Core beats run 0.75-1.33x M (about 60%: features, claims, answers). Connective beats run 0.25-0.5x M and never under 24 f (about 20%: a punch-in insert, a whip, a one-word card, an isolate hold). Long beats run 1.5-2x M (10-15%: a walkthrough setup, a two-step interaction). One or two hero beats run 2.5-3x M, capped at 180 f, the house shot maximum (the hero result or the key feature), placed in the back half before the sign-off. Put one or two connective beats directly before each hero beat so the hero lands as a release, and never let three neighbouring beats sit within 10% of each other in length. Beats under 42 f carry no readable text (the copy rule is 36 f + 6 f per word). A hero beat is filled with continuous action, either a camera journey or a UI event at least every 40 f, never a long hold. Beside grid-check, add a node check asserting that max/M is 2.5-3.0, min/M is 0.16-0.5, no beat exceeds 180 f and the coefficient of variation is 0.4-0.8. An evenly spaced cut list scores about 0.1 and reads as a slideshow.
techniques.timing: M = 60-72 f. Connective beats 24-36 f (never under 24 f); core 0.75-1.33x M; long 1.5-2x M; hero 2.5-3x M, at most 180 f and at most 2 per film; coefficient of variation 0.4-0.8. Example 28.75 s cut at 120 BPM: 75, 60, 30, 75, 120, 45, 60, 75, 30, 75, 60, 45, 105, 60, 30, 180, 75, 45, 30, 180, 90 and 60 f, then a 120 f lockup (M 60, max/M 3.0, CV 0.56).
techniques.use_when: Launch films and walkthroughs of 15 s or more with eight or more beats, any cut list that came out evenly spaced, and deciding where the hero feature gets its time.
techniques.avoid_when: Polyrhythm loops and fixed-length ask cycles, where equal length is the point; stings under about 8 s, which have too few beats for a distribution; accelerando runs, which set their own length ratios.

techniques.name: One screen direction per act
techniques.summary: Each act owns one direction of travel, so every entrance, exit, drift and camera ramp in it runs the same way, and the direction turns only at an act seam, where the turn itself marks the new chapter.
techniques.recipe: Add a DIR map beside ACT in src/timeline.ts with one unit vector per act ({x: 1, y: 0} for left to right, {x: -1, y: 0} for right to left, or {x: 0, y: -1} for an upward feed), plus a helper along(act, d) that returns {x: d * DIR.x, y: d * DIR.y}. Route every directional number through that helper. Entrances start upstream at along(act, -O), with O = 8-15% of frame width, and brake on E.out. Holds drift downstream at 0.3-1 px/f. Exits and accelerate-into-cut ramps leave downstream on E.in, and whoosh pan takes the sign of DIR.x. Inside an act nothing travels against the vector except a settle tail or a final move to centre. Across each cut inside the act, the hero leaves by the downstream edge and comes back in from the upstream edge, still travelling the same way. Turn the vector only at an act seam, on its downbeat (a seam may also keep it). Make each turn coincide with a second channel change (a polarity flip, a score section change, or the switch from imagery to type) so it reads as a new chapter rather than a continuity slip. The last act's vector delivers the lockup: the mark arrives along it and settles centred. Check it in a node test beside grid-check: sample each act's text positions at f and f + 1 from the same functions the acts use, and assert that every text element moving faster than 2 px/f has a velocity whose dot product with DIR is positive, except settle tails of at most 6 f.
techniques.timing: 2-4 vectors per film, one per act, each turn on b(n) at an act seam. Entrance offsets 8-15% of frame width (150-290 px at 1080p), braking on E.out over 30-50 f; hold drift 0.3-1 px/f downstream; exit ramps 18-24 f on E.in, reaching 17-38 px/f; counter-motion above 2 px/f lasts at most 6 f and only in settle tails.
techniques.use_when: Films built from hard cuts with velocity handoffs, two-act spots (imagery, then type), runs of statements (an upward feed), and vertical films with a rising vector.
techniques.avoid_when: Oners and single camera journeys, where the layout of the surface sets the direction; films whose motion is mostly radial zooms; multi-cell grids; a film with no act change, which should keep one vector throughout.

techniques.name: Machine on the grid, hands off it
techniques.summary: Work the product does (rows inserting, items stacking, text streaming) ticks on a strict metronome, while what a person does (moving the cursor, flipping toggles, clicking) arrives on uneven, deliberating gaps, so the viewer can feel who is acting.
techniques.recipe: Tag every scheduled event in src/timeline.ts with who performs it: SYS for work the product does (rows inserting, items stacking, text streaming, status steps) and USER for what a person does (cursor travel, clicks, toggles, drags). SYS start frames come from b() on a fixed step: 15 f (an 8th at 120 BPM) for inserts, or 16ths via b(bar, beat, sub) for bursts. Every SYS instance uses the same curve and duration (for example a 12 f E.ui reveal) at a constant or ratcheting rate. Streamed text uses TypeOn with cps at 25-40 characters per second, or one fixed time box, and never jitters. USER start frames come from a hand-written list of uneven gaps, with at least 2x between the shortest and longest gap and no two neighbouring gaps within 15% of each other ([0, 4, 19, 37] f for four toggles, or gaps of 10, 26 and 14 f). Cursor travel runs through cursorArc (bow 0.15-0.25) on E.glide and lasts max(14, D / 20) f for a trip of D px, which keeps its peak under 60 px/f. A dwell of 6-18 f, chosen per instance with rand(seed), separates arrival from the press, and pressAt drives the click. Only the decisive press of each scene lands on a beat (±1 f); the rest of the user layer stays off the grid. Sound follows the same split: each SYS insert gets one soft tick so the metronome is heard (dropped once inserts pass about 3 per second over a bed), and USER actions stay silent except the decisive click.
techniques.timing: SYS: one event every 15 f (an 8th at 120 BPM), or every 7-8 f (16ths) in bursts; identical 12 f E.ui reveals; streams at 25-40 characters per second. USER: gaps such as 4, 15 and 18 f, or 10, 26 and 14 f; cursor travel max(14, D/20) f on E.glide, peak under 60 px/f, with motion blur above 12 px/f; dwell 6-18 f; press 12 f via pressAt; the decisive press on the beat ±1 f.
techniques.use_when: Product demos where a person gives an instruction and the product or an agent responds, walkthroughs that mix input with generated output, and any sequence where automation should feel tireless next to a human.
techniques.avoid_when: Pure type films or brand stings with no user in the story; polyrhythm grids, which run their own clocks; musical montages where every event must land on the beat.

techniques.name: Focus ring: pop on click, trim to point
techniques.summary: A thin outline around a control either pops outward and fades the moment it is clicked, or draws itself clockwise around a target and erases from the tail, pointing at the action without a cursor.
techniques.recipe: Draw an SVG rounded rect around the control's bounds, with rx equal to the control radius plus the outset, a crisp 2-3 px stroke and no blur copy. Pop mode: on the press frame, grow the outset from 4 to 14 px with prog(..., E.out) over 8 f and fade the stroke from 0.9 to 0 linearly over 20 f. For a handoff, keep the ring at 14 px instead so it becomes the border of the next element (an alert card, or the frame of the next shot). Trim mode: 6 px outset, dasharray '10 8', masked by a second rect with pathLength 1 that shows only the run from tail to head (strokeDasharray `${h - t} 1`, strokeDashoffset -t). Here head = prog(f, s, s + 24, E.smooth) and tail = prog(f, s + 24, s + 48, E.smooth). Repeat on the next target about 108 f later while the cursor rests nearby. Use C.accent for the stroke only when the accent's one meaning is 'act here'; otherwise use C.ink on light stages and C.white on dark ones.
techniques.timing: Pop: outset 4 to 14 px in 8 f E.out; opacity 0.9 to 0 over 20 f, linear from the press. Trim: draw 24 f and erase 24 f, both E.smooth (a 48 f loop); dashes 10/8 px, 3 px stroke; next target about 108 f later.
techniques.use_when: A click needs a visible result the next shot can build on, or a calm frame must point at the next action without moving a cursor.
techniques.avoid_when: The cursor already sits on the target (the ring is redundant), or the ring would need a glow or blurred halo to read.

techniques.name: In-place character rewrite
techniques.summary: A small monospace status field is overwritten left to right by its new state, or a sensitive value turns to dots and deletes from the right, all inside the same fixed slot with no layout change.
techniques.recipe: Set the field in FONT.mono with whiteSpace pre so every character keeps its column. Overwrite: k = fd(prog(f, s, s + 12, E.linear) * max(oldLen, newLen)) and text = next.slice(0, k) + prev.slice(k). Start it 8 f into the press release, so the status changes as the button's light fades. Optionally lift a companion icon 10 px over 4 f E.out and bring it back over 8 f. Redact: on the click frame, swap the value to '•'.repeat(n) in one frame, then set n = len - fd((f - s) / 2) so one dot deletes every 2 f. Meanwhile, an anchor-camera pan over 40 f E.inOut keeps the toggle icon centred; put the click on a downbeat.
techniques.timing: Overwrite at about 1 character per frame (13 characters in 12 f), linear, starting 8 f after the press peak. Redact: 1 f swap, then 1 dot deleted every 2 f; camera pan 40 f E.inOut.
techniques.use_when: The product's own status (sending, receiving, connected) or a privacy claim should change in place and read as the machine's voice.
techniques.avoid_when: The text is decorative rather than real UI status (it becomes filler text), or the field uses a proportional face, so the columns jump.

techniques.name: Anticipation dip before an unlock
techniques.summary: Light builds on a locked card, the card briefly darkens as the lock's shackle swings open, then it pops to clean full-tone content, so the release feels bigger than it is.
techniques.recipe: Drive the card wrapper's filter brightness through a tw chain: 1.0 to 1.5 over 14 f E.in (the build), then 1.5 to 0.8 over 12 f E.out (the dip). On the pop frame, swap the locked art for the clean art in one frame (decided with fd), hidden inside the brightness pulse, never crossfading the two. Set brightness to 1 + 0.35 * hitPulse(t, 3, 6) and scale to 1 + 0.024 * hitPulse(t, 4, 4): a pulse, not a spring. During the dip, rotate the shackle -30 degrees about its hinge (transformOrigin at the hinge point) with E.out and lift it 4 px. Repeat it faster on a second card (a 7 f pop instead of 12 f) so the second read is snappier, and put a 'pop' or 'snap' event on each pop frame.
techniques.timing: Build 14 f E.in to 1.5x. Dip 12 f E.out to 0.8x, with the shackle at -30 degrees. Pop 12 f (7 f on the repeat) with a hitPulse(t, 3, 6) brightness pulse and a 2.4% scale pulse. About 38 f in all.
techniques.use_when: Something locked, gated or hidden becomes available (an unlock, a reveal, access granted) and the moment should land as a payoff.
techniques.avoid_when: The brightness would clip whites into a bloom, or the film already has two big payoff beats.

techniques.name: One-element tell before the event
techniques.summary: Just before a state change or a cut, exactly one small thing moves, such as a plus glyph turning 45 degrees into an x or an object slowly turning toward its target, while everything else holds.
techniques.recipe: Plus mode: rotate the plus glyph 0 to 45 degrees with prog(f, cut - 16, cut - 6, E.smooth) so it finishes 6 f before the cut. Repeat it before every result cut so the viewer learns the tell. Yaw mode: rotateY the object 0 to 35 degrees over 40 f E.linear inside perspective 1200px. The camera tail creeps at most 0.1% scale per frame and nothing else changes; fire the event (a 2-4 f impact or a hard state change) on the frame the yaw ends. The tell is the motion of the shot, so keep it to one element and add no cursor.
techniques.timing: Plus: 10 f E.smooth, finishing 6 f before the cut. Yaw: 40 f linear to 35 degrees, with the event on the next frame; camera creep at most 0.1% per frame.
techniques.use_when: A repeated result cut, or a sudden 2-4 f event, needs anticipation so it reads as caused rather than random.
techniques.avoid_when: Several things already move in the frame (the tell gets lost), or the yaw would leave the rest of the frame static for more than 48 f.

techniques.name: Chip bloom around content
techniques.summary: A container grows out of its content: a dropped icon tile widens into a labelled chip that floods with the accent and wipes back to an outline, or a solid pill swells behind a name so the group becomes a button.
techniques.recipe: Tile to chip: on the drop, scale the tile 0.8 to 1 over 8 f E.out. Then tween the pill width from the tile width (equal to its height) to the label width plus padding over 12 f E.out. On the same progress, the icon slides to its left slot and the label reveals with a clip-path inset from the right. A flat C.accent fill clipped to the pill is erased by a mask-image linear-gradient with an 80 px feather, sliding left to right over 20 f E.outSoft and leaving a 1.5 px border. Bloom behind: an absolutely positioned pill behind the text (radius height/2, C.ink fill) tweens from the text bounds (measureTracked) to the bounds plus 48 px on each side over 10 f E.out. Meanwhile the text mixes from C.ink to C.white over 6 f, starting on the bloom's second frame. Hold the finished chip at least 18 f before it does anything else.
techniques.timing: Tile pop 8 f E.out; widen 12 f E.out; fill wipe-off 20 f E.outSoft with an 80 px feather; bloom behind 10 f E.out with a 6 f text inversion; hold at least 18 f.
techniques.use_when: An integration, tag or name should become a tangible, clickable object (attached, added, now a button), shown as cause and effect.
techniques.avoid_when: The fill would need several hues to read, or the chip has nothing to do next (a bloom with no follow-up reads as decoration).

techniques.name: Shape handoff: pill becomes the icon
techniques.summary: A labelled capsule empties its text, then collapses at a fixed height into a square tile or circle that becomes the next thing (the app icon, a loader or a dock slot), so the object never disappears, it changes role.
techniques.recipe: One div owns the shape and tweens width, height and borderRadius, with its content centred. Empty the label first. Either backspace from the end (one character every 1-2 f, with fd) or delete from both ends at once (text.slice(k, n - k), k + 1 every 5 f), with the pill width hugging the measured text plus padding over 8 f E.out per step. Then collapse the width down to the height about the centre over max(40, e/7) f on E.inOut, where e is each edge's travel in px (half the width lost), so each edge peaks under about 55 px/f (E.inOut peaks at 7.7x its mean speed). Take the radius from 999 to 22% of the side for a tile, or to 50% for a circle. Then do one of three things: loop a 3x3 pixel-dot loader inside it (one dot step every 6 f); raise an arrow glyph into the circle through overflow hidden (translateY 100% to 0 over 14 f E.out); or tween the tile to a dock-slot rect over 20 f E.out while the dock mounts behind it and sibling icons scale in on SPR.micro at a 6 f stagger. Close with a 1 + 0.05 * hitPulse(t, 3, 5) scale pulse just before the cut.
techniques.timing: Backspace 1 character every 1-2 f (pairs every 5 f, width hug 8 f E.out). Collapse max(40, edge travel / 7) f on E.inOut at a fixed height (each edge under about 55 px/f). Dock variant 20 f E.out plus SPR.micro siblings at 6 f. The loader holds about 72 f.
techniques.use_when: A thinking state, prompt or button should hand off to the product identity, or to its new place in the interface, in one continuous take.
techniques.avoid_when: The target shape has nothing to do with the source (the continuity feels arbitrary), or the shot needs a hard cut for rhythm.

techniques.name: Guide cursor: arrive, hover, press
techniques.summary: A cursor travels a bowed path to the element about to act, the target shows its hover state a few frames after the cursor arrives, and a short press triggers the response on the same frame.
techniques.recipe: Use src/fx/Cursor.tsx in screen space: position = cursorArc(from, to, prog(f, m0, m1, E.smooth), 0.2), with the target from toScreen(shot, point), and press = pressAt(f, CLICK). The target's response (a press envelope or a state flip) starts on CLICK. Calm mode: travel at 5-15 px/f along the path and arrive 6-12 f before the press. The target's hover fill (C.mist, or a 6% ink tint) fades in over 4 f, starting 4 f after arrival, and any highlight that follows the cursor trails it by 4 f. Snappy mode, for vertical or phone-size frames: scale the cursor to about 11% of frame height (Cursor scale about 2.8 at 1080p). Move about 300 px in 24 f with E.out (about 72 px/f on the first frame, velocity x0.78 per frame), then dwell about 60 f while the UI reacts. Once the product acts on its own, fade the cursor out over 10 f after its last click.
techniques.timing: Calm: arcs at 5-15 px/f on E.smooth, bow 0.15-0.25, arriving 6-12 f early; hover starts 4 f after arrival and takes 4 f. Press: 4 f down, 8 f recoil (pressAt). Snappy: 300 px in 24 f E.out, dwell about 60 f. At most one click per 30 f, at uneven gaps; exit fade 10 f.
techniques.use_when: A person is driving the product, and dense UI needs a point of view that shows the viewer where to look next.
techniques.avoid_when: The product acts on its own, clicks would come faster than one per 30 f, or the shot already has a pointer such as a focus ring.

techniques.name: Velocity-stretch dot
techniques.summary: A small round dot (a cursor or a list marker) stretches into a capsule along its motion in proportion to its speed, anchored at its trailing end, and shrinks back to a dot when it stops.
techniques.recipe: Compute the head H(f) from an eased path, clamped to its start position before the move. Compute the tail as a pure-function exponential follow: T(f) is the sum over i = 0..29 of 0.8^i * H(f - i), divided by the sum of 0.8^i, which gives a lag of about 4 f. Draw an SVG line from T to H with strokeLinecap round, strokeWidth equal to the dot diameter, a flat fill and no shadow. Size it at 3.3-5.3% of frame height for a cursor (C.white on dark), or 18-21 px for a list marker (C.accent). Marker mode: drop it in from the top edge over 31 f E.out, so it arrives as a long streak that shortens into the dot. Hop it 54 px to the next item over 22 f E.smooth on a 54 f cadence, with the active label mixing from C.mute to C.ink over 8 f around the hop midpoint. Exit by stretching it into a dash about four times the dot's length (about 84 px for a 21 px marker) over 17 f on E.smooth, then shoot it off with E.in. The stretch is the streak, so draw nothing behind it.
techniques.timing: Tail weights 0.8^i over 30 f (a lag of about 4 f): length about rest + 4-5.5 f x speed, back to a dot in 16-20 f. Marker: drop 31 f E.out; hop 54 px in 22 f E.smooth every 54 f; label colour 8 f; exit: stretch to an ~84 px dash over 17 f (E.smooth), then off on E.in.
techniques.use_when: A tiny element must lead the eye across a slab or down a list, and needs speed, direction and character.
techniques.avoid_when: UI truth requires a standard system arrow, or several dots would stretch at once (the trick only reads once).

techniques.name: Shared highlight walks the menu
techniques.summary: One rounded highlight slides from row to row of a sidebar or menu, trailing the cursor, and the chosen row settles into a pale accent tint.
techniques.recipe: Render a single absolutely positioned highlight behind the rows: radius 8 px or row height / 2, C.white on a dark sidebar, C.mist on a light one. Tween its translateY and height to each target row's rect, taken from the layout data, over 12 f E.out, starting 4 f after the cursor reaches that row. Walk about 24 f per row; the first hover can appear in one frame. On the click, mix the chosen row's background to C.accent at 10% opacity over 8 f E.ui and its label to C.ink, then fade the moving highlight over 8 f. The row text never moves.
techniques.timing: 12 f E.out per hop; about 24 f per row; trails the cursor by 4 f; click tint 8 f E.ui; highlight fade 8 f.
techniques.use_when: Navigation through a menu, sidebar or list should read as a small human decision, with spatial continuity.
techniques.avoid_when: The rows are too small to read at the shot's framing (push in first), or a soft radial bloom would be added to the highlight.

techniques.name: Stretchy tab indicator
techniques.summary: The selected pill of a segmented control shoots to the new option with its leading edge arriving first, stretches to about 1.9x its width mid-travel, then hugs the new label as the label takes the active colour.
techniques.recipe: Animate the indicator's leading and trailing edges as two tweens on the same E.glide: the leading edge reaches the target edge in 12 f and the trailing edge in 20 f. Width = right - left therefore swells to about 1.9x near frame 6 and relaxes into the target width. Keep the height fixed, the radius at height / 2 and the fill flat. Mix the new label from C.mute to the active colour over the last 8 f, and the old label back over the first 8 f. Step the new label's weight from 500 to 600 on the landing frame with fd. Calm variant: fade the fill to a 1.5 px outline ring over the first 6 f. Swell the ring to 1.35x by 30% of the travel and shrink it onto the target by 100%, over 48 f E.smooth, then snap the solid fill back over 4 f on landing. Put a tick on the landing frame.
techniques.timing: Leading edge 12 f, trailing edge 20 f, both E.glide, for hops up to about 250 px. For longer hops keep the 0.6 ratio and lengthen both so the leading edge stays under about 65 px/f (a 420 px hop takes 18 f / 30 f). Label colour 8 f. Calm variant: 48 f E.smooth, 6 f fill fade, 4 f snap.
techniques.use_when: A tab, filter or toggle switch causes the next state (the chart changes, the list swaps) and deserves weight.
techniques.avoid_when: The control has more than about five options in a tight row (the stretch overlaps its neighbours), or the indicator would only read with refraction or a frosted backdrop behind it.

techniques.name: Radial dash burst around a word
techniques.summary: Short dashes burst outward around a hero word on the beat, drift almost imperceptibly while it is read, then fly outward faster as the frame pushes into the cut.
techniques.recipe: Place 22 rounded rects (4x20 px) around the word at angles from rand(`dash${i}`), oriented radially, in C.ink at 60-80% opacity. Their radius is r = 187 + 87 * prog(f, b, b + 16, E.out) + 0.5 * max(0, f - b - 16), plus 176 * prog(f, cut - 20, cut, E.in) in the last 20 f while the camera pushes in. The motion-blur pass smears the burst and the exit. Start it on the beat the word lands.
techniques.timing: Burst +87 px in 16 f E.out; drift 0.5 px/f for about 50 f; exit +176 px over the last 20 f E.in into the cut.
techniques.use_when: A single hero word on a beat needs a physical punch.
techniques.avoid_when: The text is body copy, the shot is UI, or the burst has already been used once in the film.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Replace the random dashes with 12 evenly spaced radial ticks (every 30 degrees, 20 px long, 3 px stroke, C.ink, one SVG) forming an ordered ring around the word. Drive them with the same radius curve: 187 to 274 px in 16 f E.out, a 0.5 px/f drift, then out to about 450 px over the last 20 f E.in. It reads as a graphic emphasis mark rather than debris. A single 2 px ring stroke on the same curve also works.

techniques.name: Launch hop that never lands
techniques.summary: A centred app icon hops up as if launching, hangs at the top for a beat and starts to fall, and the camera leaves before it lands, so the hop motivates the scene change.
techniques.recipe: Chain the icon's translateY with tw: 0 to -77 px over 10 f E.outSoft, hold 4 f, then -77 to +20 px over 18 f E.contact (gravity, ending with velocity), with no squash. Scale a soft contact shadow from 1 to 0.85 and fade it as the icon rises. Start the scene change (a camera tilt-away, a whip or a cut) on frame 14, the first frame of the fall, so the landing never resolves on screen.
techniques.timing: Rise 77 px in 10 f E.outSoft; hold 4 f at the top; fall 18 f E.contact; the camera leaves from frame 14; 32 f in all.
techniques.use_when: Opening the app or launching a feature should motivate the move to the next scene with a familiar OS gesture.
techniques.avoid_when: The icon must come to rest in the same shot (then it needs a real landing), or several icons would hop in turn.

techniques.name: Two-beat confirm cascade
techniques.summary: A row of buttons or toggles confirms one by one: the label or knob changes first, the fill follows a beat later, and the rows go at uneven, human gaps.
techniques.recipe: Give the rows irregular start frames, never a metronome: for example [0, 4, 19, 37] for four toggles, or [0, 10] for two buttons. Button: swap the label at t0, with a 4 f crossfade or a 6 f roll (the old label rises 8 px and leaves, the new one enters from 8 px below through arrive()). Then mix the background from C.ink2 to C.accent over 8 f E.out, starting at t0 + 12. Toggle: slide the knob 0 to 20 px over 8 f E.out with no overshoot, and mix the track from C.line to C.accent over 10 f E.smooth from the same frame. Put a light 'tick' (weight 0.25-0.35, panned by x) on each state change.
techniques.timing: Label 4-6 f; fill 8 f E.out at +12 f. Knob 8 f E.out; track 10 f E.smooth. Row gaps such as 4, 15 and 18 f.
techniques.use_when: Several integrations, permissions or capabilities switch on, and each confirmation must stay legible at video speed.
techniques.avoid_when: There is only one control (use the press envelope), or every row would start at the same interval.

techniques.name: Spinner resolves to a check
techniques.summary: A working indicator (a rotating dashed ring in a step list, or a small spinning disc pushed into the middle of a sentence) turns into a check with a short tag the moment the step is done.
techniques.recipe: Working: an SVG circle (r 10-12 px, 2.5 px stroke, dasharray '4 4' or a 270-degree arc) rotated (f - s) * 7.5 degrees, one turn per 48 f. Inline variant: open a slot between two words by tweening its width 0 to 1.4em over 6 f E.out (the words slide apart as flex siblings). In it, spin a 1.2em x 0.6em accent disc with a 3 px C.ink rim on rotateX, one turn per 24 f linear, in perspective 300px. Done: on the done frame (fd), replace the spinner with a check ring that draws strokeDashoffset 1 to 0 (pathLength 1) while scaling 0.6 to 1 over 8 f E.out. The tick path draws over 8 f from 3 f later, a small 'Done' tag rises 6 px and fades in over 8 f, and the step label mixes from C.mute to C.ink. Start the next step's spinner on that same frame, and put a pitched 'pop' on each check's 50% frame, climbing with each step.
techniques.timing: Ring: one turn per 48 f, linear (disc: one per 24 f). Slot opens over 6 f E.out. Check ring 8 f E.out from 0.6; tick draws over 8 f from +3 f; tag 8 f. One step every 24-36 f.
techniques.use_when: The product works through steps on its own (an agent, a sync, an import), and each completion should land as a small lock.
techniques.avoid_when: There is a single long wait with nothing resolving (show progress instead), or all the checks would resolve on one frame.

techniques.name: Send as a ghosted handoff
techniques.summary: On send, the composer's text drifts up and fades away while the same content appears above as a posted message, briefly overlapping the old text, instead of flying between containers.
techniques.recipe: From the send press, fade the composer text over 12 f using q = prog(f, send, send + 12, E.smooth): opacity 1 - q, translateY -12 * depart(q) px, and blur blurOut(q, 4), so it only softens once it is moving. Starting 4 f after the press, bring the posted bubble in at its final place over 18 f, with opacity on E.smooth and translateY 12 to 0 px through arrive(prog(..., E.out)). Empty the composer on frame +12 and bring its placeholder back over 8 f. Pair it with the press envelope on the send button.
techniques.timing: Composer out over 12 f E.smooth (-12 px, blur up to 4 px). Bubble in over 18 f from +4 f (12 to 0 px, E.out with arrive). 8 f of overlap; placeholder back over 8 f.
techniques.use_when: A message, prompt or post is submitted and the result appears elsewhere in the same frame; this is calmer and cheaper than a flight.
techniques.avoid_when: The journey itself is the point (show the flight), or the move would serve as a transition between shots, where a crossfade is never the default.

techniques.name: Drag, lift and seat
techniques.summary: A chip or file picked up by the cursor lifts off the surface, follows the hand with a slight lag and tilt, then drops into its slot with a small contact squash as the slot accepts it.
techniques.recipe: On the grab (pressAt), scale the item 1 to 1.04 and deepen its shadow from 0 2px 4px to 0 16px 32px at 18% black over 8 f E.out. While dragging, place it at the cursor path evaluated at f - 3 (a 3 f lag). Tilt it by rotateZ = clamp(vx * 0.25, -6, 6) degrees, where vx is the cursor's horizontal speed. When it enters the slot, thicken the slot outline from 1 to 2 px and tint it over 6 f E.ui. On release, run the last 40-80 px into the slot on E.contact over 8 f and settle the scale and shadow back. Apply squash(t) anchored at the contact edge, and put a 'snap' or light 'land' on the contact frame.
techniques.timing: Lift 8 f E.out to 1.04 with a 16/32 px shadow. Follow lag 3 f; tilt at most 6 degrees. Slot tint 6 f E.ui. Drop 8 f E.contact, plus squash over about 8 f.
techniques.use_when: A drag-and-drop (attach a file, add an integration, reorder a card) causes the next state.
techniques.avoid_when: The drag path is long (over about 600 px, cut it), or the item contains text that must be read while it tilts.

techniques.name: Badge count bump
techniques.summary: A notification badge or counter chip ticks up: the digit rolls to the next value while the badge gives a small pulse, once per increment.
techniques.recipe: Draw the badge as a pill (C.accent fill, C.white tabular-nums digit) with the digit in an overflow-hidden slot. On each increment frame c, roll the old digit up and out and the new one in from below, one line height of travel over 8 f, with arrive(prog(f, c, c + 8, E.out)). Pulse the badge scale to 1 + 0.12 * hitPulse(f - c, 2, 5), and retween its width over 8 f E.out when the digit count changes (9 to 10). The badge first appears from its icon's corner (transformOrigin there) on SPR.micro. Space increments unevenly, at least 12 f apart, with a 'tick' of weight 0.3 on each.
techniques.timing: Digit roll 8 f E.out; pulse hitPulse(t, 2, 5) x 0.12; width 8 f E.out; first appearance on SPR.micro; increments at least 12 f apart, uneven.
techniques.use_when: Incoming activity (messages, leads, approvals) should register as small, countable events on the UI.
techniques.avoid_when: The count is the hero number of the shot (use a full counter), or increments would come faster than about one per 12 f.

techniques.name: Click to focus: I-beam, ring, caret
techniques.summary: An arrow cursor turns into an I-beam as it enters an empty field and clicks. The field's border sharpens, a caret appears and blinks twice at an uneven, human pace, and on the first key the placeholder vanishes and the pointer fades away.
techniques.recipe: Draw the I-beam as a variant of src/fx/Cursor.tsx: a 2.5 px C.ink stem 28 px tall with 9 px crossbars over a 2 px C.white outline, using the arrow's drop shadow. Its stem centre, not a tip, sits on the hotspot, and it scales about that point. The arrow travels on cursorArc and swaps to the I-beam in one frame, on the fd(f) where its tip enters the field's rect, arriving 8-12 f before CLICK. On CLICK (pressAt) the field takes focus: its border goes from 1.5 px C.line to 2 px C.ink through mixColor on prog(f, CLICK - 1, CLICK + 4, E.ui), so the change shows on the press frame, with no halo. On the same frame a 0.08 em x 1 em caret appears at the start of the text, while the C.mute placeholder stays where it is. Blink the caret on a hard, uneven table decided with fd: on 18, off 16, on 24, off 12 f, then the first key at CLICK + 70 (or just on 18, off 16 when the beat is tight). The pause should read as a person gathering a thought, never as a metronome. On the first key the placeholder vanishes in one frame, TypeOn takes over with a solid caret, and the I-beam fades out over 8 f on E.smooth, because a system pointer hides while typing. Run one log-space push toward the field under the arrival and the blinks (lc between two shots in src/lib/camera.ts, up to about 1.8x over 40-44 f on E.cam), so the wait is never a still frame. Put one 'click' at weight 0.3 on CLICK and no sound on the blinks.
techniques.timing: Arrive in 24-36 f on E.smooth, 8-12 f before the click; glyph swap 1 f; press 4 f down, 8 f recoil; focus border 5 f E.ui from CLICK - 1; caret blink in hard steps of 18/16/24/12 f (70 f) or 18/16 f (34 f); placeholder gone in 1 f on the first key; I-beam fade 8 f E.smooth; push up to 1.8x over 40-44 f E.cam.
techniques.use_when: A shot opens on an empty prompt, search or chat field and the first action is typing into it, so the click into the field becomes the cause of everything after.
techniques.avoid_when: The field is already focused or pre-filled, the product acts on its own with no cursor, or the film has already played the full two-blink wait once (later prompts start at the first key).

techniques.name: Cursor glyph follows context
techniques.summary: The pointer changes shape with what it is over, as a real system pointer does: an I-beam over text, an open hand over something draggable, a closed fist while dragging, and the arrow everywhere else. Each change is a one-frame swap.
techniques.recipe: Add a kind prop to src/fx/Cursor.tsx ('arrow' | 'ibeam' | 'hand' | 'grab'). Draw every glyph with the same C.ink fill, 2.4 px C.white outline and drop shadow, and give each its own hotspot, so a swap never shifts the point the cursor acts on: the arrow keeps its tip at (x, y); the I-beam (a 2.5 px stem 28 px tall with 9 px crossbars) is centred on (x, y); the open and closed hands have the hotspot at the centre of the hand. Choose the kind on fd(f) from the layout rects, never by tween. Use 'ibeam' while the hotspot is inside a text field or selectable text, 'hand' over a draggable item, and 'grab' from the frame pressAt goes down on a grab until the release. Then show 'hand' for 6-10 f until the hotspot leaves the item, and 'arrow' everywhere else. Each swap takes one frame, with no crossfade or scale blend. The press scale (1 - 0.12 x press) and the motion-blur pass apply to every glyph alike, and the fist appears on the press frame, so closing the hand is the press. While dragging, evaluate the item's path at f - 2 so it rides behind the fist and reads as pulled. Use the I-beam only on slow approaches (15 px/f or less) and at no less than about 2.2% of frame height (Cursor scale about 1.6 at 1080p), because its thin stem flickers in fast motion.
techniques.timing: Swap in 1 f on the frame the hotspot crosses a rect edge; fist on the pressAt down stroke (4 f down, 8 f recoil); open hand for 6-10 f after the release; item trails the fist by 1-3 f; I-beam approaches at 15 px/f or less.
techniques.use_when: A cursor drives a walkthrough that both types and drags, and the pointer must behave like the real system's rather than an arrow stamped on everything.
techniques.avoid_when: The cursor only clicks buttons (the arrow is correct there), or a snappy vertical edit would flash the glyph changes past before they read.

techniques.name: Drag-select snaps glyph by glyph
techniques.summary: An I-beam presses at the start of a phrase and drags across it, a tinted highlight grows behind the text one whole character at a time, and on release a small action bar grows out of the selection, ready for the product to act on it.
techniques.recipe: Measure the line once under FontGate: px[k] = measureTracked(text.slice(0, k), size, weight, track) for every k, so the highlight snaps to real glyph edges. Park the I-beam on boundary a and press with pressAt at DOWN. Then drag it to boundary b along x = lineLeft + mix(px[a], px[b], prog(f, DOWN + 2, DOWN + 2 + D, E.smooth)), with D = max(24, 2 x (b - a)) f, so the cursor stays at or under 12 px/f. The selection end is the boundary nearest the cursor, decided on fd(f): k is the index in a..b that minimises |px[k] - x|. The highlight therefore jumps one glyph at a time and never tweens, and that stepping is what makes it read as a real selection. Draw it between the field and the glyphs (layer order: field, highlight, text, cursor), from px[a] to px[k] at full line height with a 3 px radius, in mixColor(C.paper, C.accent, 0.22), keeping the text C.ink. On a dark stage use solid C.accent with C.white text, but only if the accent means 'chosen'. Release the press 6 f after the last step. 4 f later, grow an action bar 12 px above the line from the selection's top centre: transformOrigin at its bottom centre, scale lmix(0.05, 1, prog(f, UP + 4, UP + 14, E.out)), opacity over its first 4 f. For the follow-up, either remove the range in one frame (highlight and glyphs together, with the rest of the line closing up through the measured layout) and type the replacement in from px[a] with TypeOn, or restyle the selected glyphs in place. To select a whole word, use a double click: two presses 8 f apart select it in one step on the second press.
techniques.timing: Drag about 2 f per glyph (24-40 f) on E.smooth, cursor at 12 px/f or less; highlight steps per glyph on whole frames; release 6 f after the last step; action bar 10 f E.out from +4 f; hold at least 36 f before the edit; replacement typed over about 26 f; double-click presses 8 f apart.
techniques.use_when: The product acts on a piece of text the user picks (rewrite, translate, comment, format, ask about a passage), and the pick should read as a human choice rather than a preset.
techniques.avoid_when: The text is under about 40 px tall at the shot's framing (push in first), the range spans more than two lines, or the cursor never touches text anywhere else in the film.

techniques.name: Card fan that buries, then scatters
techniques.summary: A dozen identical cards swoop in from two corners along a curved arc and stack in depth until they bury the frame. They drift for a beat, then scatter outward and leave one small card in the centre that carries the number.
techniques.recipe: Place N = 12 card divs along a cubic bezier from two opposite corners toward the centre (sample it with getPointAtLength from @remotion/paths). Card i gets rotateZ = the path tangent, rotateY = 35 - 4i deg, rotateX = 18 deg and translateZ = -60i px inside one perspective(2000px) stage; the shot clips with overflow hidden, which flattens preserve-3d, so sort the cards by z yourself before rendering. Each card flies from just beyond the corner (travel at most about 700 px) to its slot on E.outSoft with start offsets stagger(i, 12, 22), then the whole fan drifts 15-40 px and breathes +2% on E.smooth. The hero card sits small and lowest in z at frame centre from the start. The scatter moves every fan card 340 px outward along its own radial vector while translateZ rises +700 px (about x1.5) on E.in, so they leave by scale and travel and uncover the hero card, whose figure then locks (Roll or Words). Card faces use a single-hue tonal ramp (dark to light of one colour, as a dithered PNG) so the repetition reads as one material.
techniques.timing: Per card 50 f on E.outSoft, starts 2 f apart (22 f span): the fan covers 50% of its final area by f6, 90% by f26 and all of it by f50 (peak about 62 px/f). Drift 84 f at 0.2-0.5 px/f plus breath +2%. Scatter 26 f on E.in, peak about 75 px/f (master motion blur). The hero figure locks 4-6 f after the last card clears.
techniques.use_when: A big count or scale claim (cards issued, transactions, users) needs to feel physical before it collapses to one legible number.
techniques.avoid_when: The film already has a card or tile swarm, or the stat must be read at once; in a calm film the 50 f bury is too loud.

techniques.name: Pinned label over a swapping world
techniques.summary: A pin pops on a 3D-rendered place and a short data tag on a leader line tracks that point as the camera orbits. On a cut, the world underneath switches between 3D and flat while the tag holds its screen position.
techniques.recipe: Keep two layers: the world (a pre-rendered 3D plate played with OffthreadVideo, or a CSS 3D stage whose container uses transformOrigin 0 0) and a screen-space overlay. Every frame, project the pin's world point with the same matrix the world uses: new DOMMatrix(cameraTransformString).transformPoint(new DOMPoint(x, y, z)), then divide x and y by w (or do the rotateX, rotateY and perspective divide by hand as references/camera.md describes). Place the overlay with one translate() and add skewY of about 0.15x the camera yaw so the tag leans with the ground. The pin scales 0 to 1 on E.out over 8 f with a ring of hitPulse(t, 2, 6), the leader line draws by stroke-dashoffset over 8 f from +4 f, the mono tag (a value or status, not a decorative kicker) types on with TypeOn, and the place name slides 25 px on E.out over 12 f from +12 f. For the swap, cut only the world layer on the velocity peak of a pull-back and continue the zoom with zoomHandoff (in the flat map the same point sits about 1.8x larger and keeps shrinking, decelerating) while the overlay keeps animating untouched; the flat-to-3D version cuts a shrinking flat mark to its 3D twin at the same screen position, starting 8x large and pulling back on E.out.
techniques.timing: Pin 8 f E.out; leader 8 f from +4 f; name 25 px over 12 f E.out from +12 f; orbit yaw 0.1-0.2 deg/f E.linear. 3D segment about 90 f, flat segment about 70 f; cut on the zoom's velocity peak, zoomHandoff settle 30 f. Flat-to-3D: 8x to 1x over 18 f E.out (fastest per-frame ratio about 0.65 at frame 2), settled by f22.
techniques.use_when: Location or geography matters ('this happens in a real place'), or a flat diagram should be revealed as a real object, and back.
techniques.avoid_when: There is no real 3D plate or scene to anchor to; a tag floating over a flat screenshot gains nothing from projection.

techniques.name: Tilted object on a spotlit ground
techniques.summary: A real card or device lies in perspective on a dark surface under one soft pool of light. Most of the frame falls to black, and a slow drift slides the light across the object's face.
techniques.recipe: Stage on ink. Put a ground plane (a bezel slab, a tile or rib pattern, or a rect one step lighter than the stage) under the object at the same rotation, and transform both with perspective(2200px) rotateZ(4deg) rotateX(8deg) rotateY(-12deg), so the roll stays outside the tilt. The light is a dithered PNG of a single-hue radial falloff (white at 12% alpha down to 0 at 60% radius, centred at 60%/55% of the frame) over ground and object, plus a 35-40% edge vignette; the object casts a soft contact shadow (blur 36 px, alpha 0.35) offset away from the pool's centre. The pool stays fixed in screen space while the object drifts translateX -0.5 px/f and yaws +0.03 deg/f (or orbits at 0.1 deg/f for a device), so the highlight travels across its surface; start the drift from rest at a seam with the camera.md drift formula. Fill the card solid, never frosted, and let its content change state on E.ui while the plane drifts.
techniques.timing: Shot 30-84 f. Drift 0.5 px/f E.linear (eased in from rest over about 60 f at a seam), plus yaw 0.03 deg/f or an orbit of 0.1 deg/f. Pool radius about 35-40% of the frame. Content state changes over 10-14 f on E.ui.
techniques.use_when: A single notification, card or device should feel like an object in a room, not on a slide, especially in a dark, low-key film.
techniques.avoid_when: The same act already tilts things on this axis, or the film is bright and flat; never on a bare screenshot without ground and shadow.

techniques.name: Depth orbit ring that collapses into the mark
techniques.summary: Small icons orbit the central mark on a tilted ellipse: they grow and pass in front as they come near and shrink behind it as they go far. Then the ring speeds up and contracts into the mark.
techniques.recipe: For each of 6-8 icons: theta = theta0 + i*360/n + omega*f, x = cx + 0.35W*cos(theta), y = cy + 0.2H*sin(theta). Depth d = sin(theta) (near at the bottom of the ellipse) drives scale mix(0.7, 1.3, (d+1)/2), brightness mix(0.6, 1, (d+1)/2) and paint order. Rebuild the list sorted by d every frame with the mark inserted at d = 0, so far icons draw behind it and near ones in front; near icons go soft through RackFocus with t = clamp((d - 0.4)/0.6) and blur 6 px, never an animated filter. To contract, multiply rx, ry and icon scale by lmix(1, 0.3, E.in(p)) over 34 f while omega doubles. Fade each icon over the last 8 f as it passes behind the mark, and scale the mark by 1 + 0.03*hitPulse(t, 2, 6) on the frame the ring closes.
techniques.timing: Orbit omega = 0.67 deg/f (40 deg/s) E.linear for about 50 f; contraction 34 f on E.in (ring x0.3, omega x2); icon fade over the last 8 f; mark punch hitPulse(t, 2, 6) x 0.03.
techniques.use_when: Showing an ecosystem of integrations or inputs around one core in about 1.5 s, without words.
techniques.avoid_when: The icons must be read or named, or the film already used an orbit; more than 8 icons turns into noise.

techniques.name: Folded channel that unfolds flat
techniques.summary: A wide card starts bent into a U-shaped channel with its side walls folded toward camera. It flattens open while the cards stacked inside fan out into a neat row, then the whole thing tips away.
techniques.recipe: Build three panels in a preserve-3d node under perspective(2000px): a front panel, plus left and right walls hinged on its edges (transform-origin at the shared edge) at rotateY(+/-60deg) toward camera. Unfold on E.out over 24 f: the walls go rotateY +/-60 to 0 and the front scale 1.15 to 1, so the channel's outer width goes from about 1890 to 1650 px. Shade each wall with a single-hue black overlay of opacity 0.35*sin(angle) and edge it with a solid 2 px rim one tone lighter than the panel. Inside, 4-5 cards stacked at -70% of a card width and rotated +/-6 deg slide to their row slots and square up on E.out over 20 f with a 2 f stagger, painted in z order. Exit: the whole card rotates rotateX 0 to 35 deg about its bottom edge and drops translateY +80 px on E.in over 16 f, receding to about 74% of its width.
techniques.timing: Unfold 24 f E.out; inner cards 20 f E.out, 2 f apart; live hold 30-48 f with breath +2%; tilt-away 16 f E.in (width 1650 to 1225 px).
techniques.use_when: Revealing a list, a set of plans or a stack of items as a tangible moment, not a flat fade-up.
techniques.avoid_when: The same act already uses a vertical-hinge yaw, or the contents are dense text that must be read during the unfold.

techniques.name: 3D flip that swaps state
techniques.summary: An icon or card turns over in 3D and comes back around changed (outline to solid, grey to full colour), then shrinks and travels to its next place.
techniques.recipe: Give the wrapper a perspective about 3.5x the object's width (about 1000 px for a 280 px icon; UI-scale planes stay at 1800-2600 px). Stack two faces with backface-visibility: hidden, the back one pre-rotated rotateY(180deg), or keep one face and swap its source when |angle| > 90 deg, mirrored with scaleX(-1) and decided with fd(frame). Turn rotateY 0 to 180 on E.inOut over 10 f with brightness 0.7 + 0.3*|cos(theta)| so the edge-on frames darken, and put a strong transient on the edge-on frame, where the face swaps. Chain on E.rest, overlapping 4 f: scale 1 to 0.38 and translateX 290 px on E.whip over 16 f into the slot. For a deck of logo cards, flip each in 6 f, 6 f apart (the whole group inside 30 f), then move each into its grid slot (scale about 0.25, rotateZ to 0) on E.glide over 12 f, with its label arriving with blurIn 6 px over 8 f.
techniques.timing: Hero flip 10 f E.inOut, swap on the edge-on frame (about f5); shrink x0.38 plus 290 px over 16 f E.whip (peak about 62 px/f). Deck: 6 f flips, 6 f apart, slot move 12 f E.glide, labels 8 f.
techniques.use_when: A state change (activated, connected, colourised) needs a physical cause, especially as the film's only 3D turn.
techniques.avoid_when: Several flips have already happened, or the cards carry heavy text (it goes mirrored and soft mid-turn).

techniques.name: Peek, hover, launch and recede
techniques.summary: A device or product panel barely rises from the bottom edge, pauses, then shoots up to centre. It is tipped back as it rises, faces camera as it arrives, and slowly settles away from camera.
techniques.recipe: Start the object below the frame inside a perspective(2200px) parent with transform-origin bottom centre. Peek: translateY -170 px on E.out over 14 f; hover 4 f. Launch to centre on E.whip over 34 f with travel capped at about 640 px: the peak is 3.7x the mean speed, so lengthen the tween for longer travel to keep the peak under 70 px/f. Tip it to rotateX 10 deg while rising and resolve to 0 on E.rest over the last 20 f of the launch. Then recede: scale lmix(1, 0.93, E.smooth(p)) over 60 f while its ground shadow (motion-tokens section 7 formula, z falling from 120 to 0) tightens.
techniques.timing: Peek 170 px over 14 f E.out (peak about 64 px/f); hover 4 f; launch of up to 640 px over 34 f E.whip; tilt 10 to 0 deg over the last 20 f on E.rest; recede x0.93 over 60 f E.smooth.
techniques.use_when: Introducing hardware or a hero product surface, where anticipation makes the main move feel powerful.
techniques.avoid_when: The film has already used anticipation twice, or the object is small UI (it reads as a bounce).

techniques.name: Edge-on sliver snaps face-on
techniques.summary: A thin edge-on sliver snaps open into a full face-on coin or badge. Most of the turn happens in the first frame, then it eases into place as its face catches the light.
techniques.recipe: Build the disc as a face plus a 24 px edge made of 12 stacked disc slices at translateZ steps of 2 px in a darker tone, under preserve-3d, with a perspective about 4x the diameter. Hold it edge-on (rotateY 90 deg) for 4 f, then turn rotateY 90 to 0 on E.out over 10 f (E.out lands about 37% of the turn in the first frame, and the master blur smears it). For a calmer reveal, turn over 22 f to a 10 deg three-quarter rest while it rises 20% of the frame height on E.outSoft. Tie the face brightness to the angle, brightness = 0.75 + 0.25*cos(theta - 20 deg), so it brightens as it turns into the key light (a tonal sheen, no bloom). For a logo reveal at the close, hard-cut on the frame after it settles to the flat logotype, with its mark at exactly the emblem's screen position and size.
techniques.timing: Edge hold 4 f. Snap 10 f E.out: frames 1-9 reach about 37, 48, 56, 61, 68, 77, 88, 94 and 100% of the turn. Calm form: 22 f E.outSoft to 10 deg with a 0.2H rise. Match cut on the first settled frame.
techniques.use_when: Revealing a token, coin, badge or mark decisively, or turning a physical object into the logo at the close.
techniques.avoid_when: Flat UI icons without thickness (the edge-on frame becomes an invisible line), or the film already has several flips.

techniques.name: Product on a thick extruded slab
techniques.summary: The live interface sits on the front of a thick matte slab with rounded corners. When the camera orbits or yaws, the slab's solid edge appears, which turns a screen into an object and makes every angle readable.
techniques.recipe: Build the slab behind the live UI face: thickness d = 0.045 x slab height, made of 16-24 stacked rounded-rect slices (same border-radius as the face) at translateZ(-i*d/N) in a flat near-black side tone. The slice just behind the face gets a 1.5 px lighter top edge; render the slices in DOM order back to front under preserve-3d, with no reflections. Move the anchor camera (a Shot with yaw and pitch, perspective 2200), not the slab. Hero push: 1 to 2.56x in log space with yaw 0 to 30 deg and pitch 5 deg on E.smooth over 60 f, landing the target panel in the right third so a void opens for the caption. Cursor-led whip: yaw +/-30 deg, roll at most 11 deg and zoom x0.77 on E.whip over 74 f, with the cursor leading by 4-6 f. After each move the camera stops and the caption, cursor and UI micro-interactions carry the hold (add breath() if nothing moves within 48 f). Lay the UI out at shot scale with CSS zoom and camera scale3d(k/Z, k/Z, 1/Z), switching Z only on a velocity-peak frame.
techniques.timing: Slab depth 4-5% of its height; the edge reads from 20 deg of yaw and clearly at 30-35 deg. Hero push 60 f E.smooth (peak about 47 px/f mid-move); whip orbit 74 f E.whip, roll at most 11 deg; the caption builds while the camera decelerates.
techniques.use_when: A single-take product walkthrough or a feature film where the camera travels across one interface.
techniques.avoid_when: The film is flat 2D throughout, or the camera never yaws (the edge never shows and the build is wasted).

techniques.name: Impact morph with stretch and floor ripple
techniques.summary: Something accelerates into a 3D tile. On contact the tile swaps shape and colour in one frame, stretches tall and settles without rebound while the floor beneath it ripples.
techniques.recipe: A solid accent dot (or the previous shot's element) accelerates into the tile on E.contact over 12 f, with travel of at most 270 px so the peak stays near 70 px/f; the master's motion blur draws its streak. On the contact frame (decided with fd), swap the tile's shape and fill in one frame (border-radius 22% to 50%, ink2 to accent). Then stretch it along the impact axis, anchored at the contact edge: scaleY = 1 + 0.31*hitPulse(t, 1, 4) and scaleX = 1 - 0.10*hitPulse(t, 1, 4), so it pops taller and settles in about 12 f with no rebound. Redraw the perspective grid floor as SVG paths every frame, displacing each vertex by 6*sin(0.052*r - 0.8*t)*exp(-t/6) px, where r is the vertex's distance from the contact point, only where r < 15*t (the wavefront). Punctuate with a camera punch of 1 + 0.02*hitPulse(t, 2, 6) and the impact sound on the swap frame, with no flash.
techniques.timing: Approach 12 f E.contact (at most 270 px); swap in 1 f; height stretch +31% decaying over about 12 f (hitPulse(t, 1, 4)); ripple 6 px, tau 6 f, front at 15 px/f, gone by about f20; punch hitPulse(t, 2, 6) x 0.02.
techniques.use_when: Cause and effect is the message: raw input hits the product and becomes something new.
techniques.avoid_when: The film has already spent its two true landings or is calm; never as a generic transition.

techniques.name: Icon lifts out of its row into a 3D hero
techniques.summary: A small icon tile peels out of a settings row and inverts from dark to light. It flies to frame centre growing almost 2x, tilted in 3D and slowly turning as it floats into the next chapter.
techniques.recipe: On frame c, duplicate the chosen tile into a top layer at its exact row rect with the same placement transform, so the swap is pixel-identical, and hide the original. Rack the rest of the UI soft with RackFocus (blur 12 px) as it dims to 40%. Fly the tile to centre on E.whip over 24-30 f (travel at most 560 px so the peak stays under 70 px/f). On the way it tilts to rotateX 15, rotateY 20 and rotateZ -4 deg (perspective about 3.5x its width, radius 22%) and inverts its colours over 18 f on E.smooth (tile C.ink2 to C.white, glyph C.white to C.ink). As the travel lands, grow it from 0.53 to 1.0 (x1.9) on E.out over 27 f, then float for 45 f with linear drifts of rotateY +4 deg and rotateZ -1.5 deg, grounded by a lift shadow at z of about 150 (motion-tokens section 7). It then becomes the anchor of the next chapter or exits shrinking x0.43 over 12 f on E.in.
techniques.timing: Travel 24-30 f E.whip; colour inversion 18 f E.smooth; grow x1.9 over 27 f E.out (fastest growth about 3 f in); float 45 f E.linear (rotateY +4 deg, rotateZ -1.5 deg); exit x0.43 over 12 f E.in.
techniques.use_when: A tiny detail (an integration, a setting, a source) should become the hero of the next section, bridging two chapters.
techniques.avoid_when: The icon has no follow-up role, or another element already did a lift-to-centre in this film.

techniques.name: Cube turn to a blank face
techniques.summary: Words converge and slide under an icon, then the icon turns 90 degrees like a cube to show a plain accent face that becomes the field for what comes next.
techniques.recipe: Build the tile as a CSS box of width w: the front face (the icon) at translateZ(w/2) and the right face (plain accent, or the next state) at rotateY(90deg) translateZ(w/2), both with backface-visibility hidden, inside a preserve-3d node offset translateZ(-w/2) so it turns about its centre, with perspective about 4w. First the flanking words accelerate inward and slide under the tile on E.in over 22 f (lower z, motion blur from the master). Then turn rotateY 0 to -90 deg on E.smooth over 12 f, shading the departing face from brightness 1 to 0.55 and the arriving face from 0.85 to 1 by the cosine of each face's angle. Hold the new face for 6 f as a designed freeze on a silence; then it expands, punches or opens into the next element.
techniques.timing: Converge 22 f E.in; cube turn 12 f E.smooth; blank-face freeze 6 f; then the next move.
techniques.use_when: Clearing a sentence into a single colour field or a seed for the logo with a clean geometric gesture.
techniques.avoid_when: The tile carries fine detail (it shears during the turn), or the same element was already flipped.

techniques.name: Press tilt that hides a swap
techniques.summary: A card tips in 3D toward the point that was clicked or tapped and relaxes back flat. The content changes on the tilt's peak frame, so the change has a physical cause.
techniques.recipe: Wrap the card with a perspective about 3.5x its width (1800-2600 px for full-width panels) and set transform-origin at the edge opposite the press, so the pressed side dips. On the press frame c (the Cursor click), drive rotateX and rotateY toward the press point (direction = the press offset from the card centre, normalised) with an amplitude of 10*hitPulse(f - c, 8, 9) deg: in over 8 f, decaying with tau 9. Swap the state (button fill and label, a photo source, a value) with fd on the peak frame c + 8, so the tilt hides the change. A quick snap variant rocks rotateY 12*hitPulse(t, 1, 2.5) deg plus skewY 2*hitPulse(t, 1, 2.5) deg, swaps the content on the peak and can repeat every 54 f as a rhythm. There is no counter-swing, since overshoot belongs only to true landings.
techniques.timing: Press at 10 deg: 8 f in, tau 9 f (under 1 deg by about f30). Snap rock at 12 deg: attack 1 f, tau 2.5 f, settled in about 8 f. Swap on the peak frame; repeat cadence 54 f; often preceded by a 24 f E.cam push-in.
techniques.use_when: Clicks, copies, likes and swaps in a UI walkthrough that need tactility without a flash.
techniques.avoid_when: Every click in the film already tilts (use it for 1-3 key presses), or the target is a tiny chip where the tilt cannot be seen.

techniques.name: Exploded layer stack
techniques.summary: A live UI component turns to a three-quarter view and separates into its layers along depth to show how it is built, then snaps back together and turns flat.
techniques.recipe: Split one component into 3-5 full-size layers that share its rect (surface, content block, controls, one live chip) and render them in z order. Turn the group to a three-quarter view on the anchor camera (yaw -28 deg, pitch 14 deg, perspective 2200, roll outside the tilt) on E.cam over 36 f. Then separate the layers to translateZ = i*90 px on E.out over 24 f with stagger(i, n, 12), each casting a neutral shadow on the layer below (alpha 0.18, blur 20 px, offset growing with the gap). Hold for up to 48 f on a yaw drift of 0.05 deg/f while one layer animates its own state. Then collapse z to 0 on E.contact over 16 f, punch 1 + 0.015*hitPulse(t, 2, 6) on the contact frame, and return yaw and pitch to 0 on E.rest over 30 f, starting 10 f before the collapse ends; lay the UI out at shot scale with CSS zoom so its text stays sharp at the angle.
techniques.timing: Turn 36 f E.cam; separate 24 f E.out with a 12 f stagger span, 80-120 px per layer; hold up to 48 f with a 0.05 deg/f yaw; collapse 16 f E.contact plus punch hitPulse(t, 2, 6) x 0.015; flatten 30 f E.rest, overlapping by 10 f.
techniques.use_when: Explaining what a product is made of (data, logic, interface), or that one surface stacks several capabilities.
techniques.avoid_when: The component is visually thin (the layers look identical), or the act's axis is already yaw.
